# The ground rules

One line per rule, and the link to the rule that owns it. Generated from `docs/rules/` by `bun nv rules --render`.


## Programs

- **Novis is built for web applications of every kind, with command-line tooling second** — Novis is for web applications — not a segment, not a vertical, not a trust posture. ([`programs/audience`](rules/programs.md#programs-audience))
- **Novis claims three things, and "faster than PHP" is not one of them** — Novis claims exactly three things about itself, and each is a property no incumbent can add later:… ([`programs/three-claims`](rules/programs.md#programs-three-claims))
- **The PHP-shaped syntax is an on-ramp, and no document may promise compatibility** — The PHP-shaped syntax is an on-ramp. ([`programs/no-compatibility-promise`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-compatibility-promise))
- **When two slices compete, the one that gets a working application sooner wins** — When two slices compete for a session, the one that gets a working web application sooner wins. ([`programs/slice-ranking`](rules/programs.md#programs-slice-ranking))
- **Memory buys security, latency and simplicity — bounded, attributable and stated** — When a design trades memory footprint against security, latency or simplicity, Novis pays the memory. ([`programs/memory-priority`](rules/programs.md#programs-memory-priority))
- **`Core\Program::implementing<T>()` lists every concrete class that is a `T`, for an interface or a class, and it expands while compiling** — It expands, while compiling, to an array literal of `new` expressions — one per non-abstract class `C` in the program for which `$c is T` holds, **sorted by fully-qualified name**, so the order never depends on filesyst… ([`programs/implementing`](rules/programs.md#programs-implementing))
- **`Core\Program::implementingWith<I, T>($member)` joins the enumeration with one attribute per class, and it expands while compiling** — `programs/implementing`'s enumeration joined with `attributes/structural-retrieval`'s retrieval in one expansion: one row per class the enumeration would instantiate, in its order, each carrying the instance and what `C… ([`programs/implementing-with`](rules/programs.md#programs-implementing-with))
- **`Core\Program::constructors<T, C>()` lists the enumeration's classes with one callable each, typed by `C`, and it expands while compiling** — It expands, while compiling, to an array literal of one row per class `programs/implementing`'s `implementing<T>()` would list, **in the same order**, so the two can be zipped. ([`programs/constructors`](rules/programs.md#programs-constructors))
- **A compile target changes the host context, never the language** — Every compile target shares one front end, one resolver, one type checker and one IR. ([`programs/compile-target`](rules/programs.md#programs-compile-target))
- **A name reaches its file while compiling; there is no runtime loader of any kind** — Nothing in Novis loads code in response to a name being referenced at run time. ([`programs/no-runtime-autoload`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-runtime-autoload))
- **`autoload` maps a prefix to roots, resolved relative to the file that declares it** — `autoload` is a top-level declaration in two forms, both taking **literal strings only**:… ([`programs/autoload`](rules/programs.md#programs-autoload))
- **A file reached by autoload declares exactly one thing, under the name the map finds it by** — A file loaded through an autoload root contains exactly one top-level declaration — class, interface, enum or `type` alias — whose qualified name is the one the map found the file by: the prefix, the directories under t… ([`programs/one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file`](rules/programs.md#programs-one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file))
- **A `require` path is compared against the on-disk entry exactly, on every OS** — A `require` whose path is a string literal resolves, and the resolved real path is then compared component-wise against the path as written. ([`programs/path-case`](rules/programs.md#programs-path-case))
- **A relative path given as a string literal at a path parameter names a file beside the source file that wrote it, and a relative path built at run time throws** — A relative string literal passed to a path parameter is joined to the folder of the source file that contains it, while compiling, the way `require` resolves its path. ([`programs/relative-paths-resolve-from-their-file`](rules/programs.md#programs-relative-paths-resolve-from-their-file))
- **`Core\Program::id()` is 64 hex characters naming this program's code and environment** — `BLAKE3(unit content hashes in program order ‖ env_hash)`, rendered as all 32 bytes in lowercase hex — 64 characters, never truncated by the runtime, because a caller that wants eight of them can take eight and one that… ([`programs/program-id`](rules/programs.md#programs-program-id))
- **A bundled executable is one trust domain: a program, never a service** — `nvs build --compile` ships a runnable *program*, not a deployable *service*. ([`programs/bundle-trust-domain`](rules/programs.md#programs-bundle-trust-domain))
- **Novis ships no framework: `Core` holds what needs privilege, and an opinionated layer is a package anyone may write** — Novis ships no web framework and no `nvs new` scaffold. ([`programs/no-first-party-framework`](rules/programs.md#programs-no-first-party-framework))
- **The privileged primitives a web framework needs are `Core`, each placed by a tier test** — The primitives a web framework builds on are compiled into the binary, and every entry is placed by a standard-library tier test rather than by convenience:… ([`programs/framework-core-half`](rules/programs.md#programs-framework-core-half))

## Types

- **Every binding declares its type, and no binding's type ever changes** — Every binding site carries a type, and only a local and a `foreach` binding may take theirs with `var` rather than writing it. ([`types/declaration`](rules/types.md#types-declaration))
- **`var` takes a local's or a `foreach` binding's type from the expression that fills it, and fixes it there for good** — `var` stands in for a written type in two places — a local declaration and a `foreach` binding — and the binding takes its type from the expression it is filled from, then keeps it for good. ([`types/var-inference`](rules/types.md#types-var-inference))
- **The type grammar is a closed set of atoms under unions and intersections** — Unions are canonicalised — flattened, de-duplicated, order-insensitive — so `int|string` and `string|int|int` are one type. ([`types/grammar`](rules/types.md#types-grammar))
- **An integer literal is decimal, `0x`, `0o` or `0b`, and a leading zero is not a radix** — An integer literal is written decimal, `0x`, `0o` or `0b` — either case of the prefix letter, with `_` separators allowed between digits. ([`types/integer-literals`](rules/types.md#types-integer-literals))
- **A numeric literal is untyped until it is placed, and `as T` is a placing position** — A numeric literal is **untyped until it is placed**, and takes its type from the position it appears in. ([`types/numeric-literal-placement`](rules/types.md#types-numeric-literal-placement))
- **`uint` is a distinct unsigned 64-bit integer, and it costs no bytes a value did not already hold** — `uint` is an unsigned 64-bit integer, `0 … 2^64−1`. ([`types/uint`](rules/types.md#types-uint))
- **An arithmetic operator answers in its operands' own type, and overflow throws rather than wrapping or promoting** — The arithmetic rows are a **closed** list. ([`types/arithmetic`](rules/types.md#types-arithmetic))
- **An `int` or `uint` widening into a `float` position is the only implicit conversion in the language** — Implicit conversion happens in exactly one place: an `int` or `uint` **widening into a `float` position** — an argument, a return, an assignment, a field of an anonymous object, an element of an array literal, or the fa… ([`types/implicit-widening`](rules/types.md#types-implicit-widening))
- **`decimal` is an exact scalar of 96 mantissa bits and a scale of 0 to 28** — `decimal` is a scalar: a sign, a 96-bit unsigned mantissa, and a scale of 0 to 28 giving the digits after the point. ([`types/decimal`](rules/types.md#types-decimal))
- **Only the types the table orders may be ordered, and two objects need `Comparable`** — `< <= > >= <=>` are defined on a **closed** list of operand pairs, and refused everywhere else:… ([`types/ordering`](rules/types.md#types-ordering))
- **A `string` is valid UTF-8 for its whole lifetime, and its unmarked unit is the grapheme cluster** — A `string` cannot hold invalid UTF-8 at any point in its lifetime. ([`types/string-is-utf8`](rules/types.md#types-string-is-utf8))
- **`bytes` is a primitive peer to `string` for data that carries no encoding** — `bytes` is a primitive scalar, peer to `string`, for data with no encoding at all — a file's contents, a socket read, a hash digest, a request body before anyone has claimed it is text. ([`types/bytes`](rules/types.md#types-bytes))
- **`1h30m` is a `Core\Time\Duration` constant, in one grammar shared by source, `parse` and `nvs.toml`** — errors naming this rule, so there is exactly one spelling of any given constant. ([`types/duration`](rules/types.md#types-duration))
- **A `string` or `int` value in type position is a single-value type, and a union of them is a set of allowed values** — A `string` or `int` value written in type position is a **single-value type** — the type whose only value is exactly that one — parsed only in type position, the way `array<T>` is. ([`types/single-value-types`](rules/types.md#types-single-value-types))
- **A scalar class constant used as a type folds to the single-value type of its own value** — `ClassName::CONST_NAME`, written where a type is expected, resolves at compile time to the constant's own value — exactly as long as that value is a `string` or `int` compile-time constant. ([`types/constant-in-type-position`](rules/types.md#types-constant-in-type-position))
- **An enum case used as a type is a narrowed subtype of its enum, never its backing integer** — `EnumName::CaseName`, written where a type is expected, does **not** resolve to its backing integer. ([`types/enum-case-type`](rules/types.md#types-enum-case-type))
- **An array is PHP's ordered hash with `string` keys and a declared element type** — The container is an insertion-ordered hash with copy-on-write value semantics. ([`types/arrays`](rules/types.md#types-arrays))
- **Three combining members treat every key alike, and `array + array` does not compile** — Three members combine arrays, and each walks its arguments left to right treating **every key the same way**:… ([`types/array-combination`](rules/types.md#types-array-combination))
- **`{preserveKeys: false}` discards every key, whatever shape the key has** — Wherever the `{preserveKeys: …}` option appears — `slice`, `chunk`, `reverse`, the sorts —… ([`types/preserve-keys`](rules/types.md#types-preserve-keys))
- **A subscript through a `mixed` is the tag's question; every other base answers it where it is written** — A base that declares an element type is checked where it is written. ([`types/mixed-subscript`](rules/types.md#types-mixed-subscript))
- **There are no user-declared generic functions or classes** — A program declares no type parameter of its own: a type variable belongs only to a declaration the compiler owns — a `Core` member, and a user class implementing a compiler-owned generic interface at a concrete type (`i… ([`types/no-user-generics`](rules/types.md#types-no-user-generics))
- **`property<T>` is a type whose values are `T`'s public property names, and `as` is its only source** — `property<T>` is a type atom, written in every position a type is written, whose **values** are the names of `T`'s public declared instance properties — its own and its ancestors' — and nothing else. ([`types/property-key`](rules/types.md#types-property-key))
- **`property<T>` widens as `T` narrows, because the argument bounds the receiver** — A subclass *adds* properties, so `property<Animal>`'s names are all valid on a `Dog` while `property<Dog>`'s are not all valid on an `Animal`. ([`types/property-key-variance`](rules/types.md#types-property-key-variance))
- **`$obj->$key` accepts a `property<T>` and nothing else; a read is the union and a write is checked** — `$obj->$key` and `$obj->{$expr}` are admitted, and **only** when the operand's type is a `property<T>` whose argument the receiver satisfies (`types/property-key-variance`). ([`types/property-key-access`](rules/types.md#types-property-key-access))
- **`propertyPath<T>` is a type whose values are dotted chains of public property names starting at `T`, checked one segment at a time** — `propertyPath<T>` is a type atom beside `property<T>`, written in every position a type is written, whose **values** are dotted chains of public declared property names starting at `T`: `customer`, `customer.address.cit… ([`types/property-path`](rules/types.md#types-property-path))
- **`string<K>` is a string whose `{…}` holes are each a `K`, checked where it is written, and its text keeps its taint** — `string<K>` is a string with holes: text in which every `{…}` is one value of `K`, checked where the string is written. ([`types/string-holes`](rules/types.md#types-string-holes))
- **A union permits only what every member permits, and `mixed` is the one position checked nowhere** — A union permits only the operations valid for *every* member. ([`types/unions-and-mixed`](rules/types.md#types-unions-and-mixed))
- **A union of classes reads and calls a member every class declares with the same type** — A property read and a method call through a union of classes compile when every class of the union declares or inherits that member, the member is visible at the access site in every class, and every class gives it the… ([`types/a-member-every-class-of-a-union-declares`](rules/types.md#types-a-member-every-class-of-a-union-declares))
- **One mistake in a program reports one error, and a value written as `mixed` keeps every error it has** — One mistake in a program reports one error: a name that does not resolve gives its root diagnostic once, and no later use of it reports again. ([`types/one-mistake-reports-once`](rules/types.md#types-one-mistake-reports-once))
- **`$x is T` tests whether a value holds a `T`, answers `bool`, and never refuses because the answer is knowable** — `$x is T` asks whether a value currently holds a `T` and answers `bool`, for any type a value can inhabit. ([`types/type-test`](rules/types.md#types-type-test))
- **Narrowing is flow-sensitive and branch-local, and there are exactly four spellings of it** — Narrowing is flow-sensitive and **branch-local**, and there are four spellings of it: `is`, a `== null` test, a comparison against a value of a single-value type, and `match (true)`. ([`types/narrowing`](rules/types.md#types-narrowing))
- **`expr as T` is the only conversion, and it produces a `T` or throws** — There are exactly two ways to obtain a value of a different type: `expr as T`, and a second binding declared at the type you want. ([`types/conversion`](rules/types.md#types-conversion))
- **PHP's `(T)expr` cast does not parse, and the diagnostic names the `as` that replaces it** — `(int)expr`, `(uint)expr`, `(float)expr`, `(string)expr`, `(bool)expr`, `(array)expr` and `(object)expr` are all rejected at parse time. ([`types/no-legacy-cast`](rules/types.md#types-no-legacy-cast))
- **A `type` alias is a transparent, compile-time-only synonym for a type expression** — `type Name = TypeExpr;` declares a compile-time-only synonym for a type expression, written either at file and namespace scope alongside `use` and `namespace` or as a member of a class, interface or enum body (`types/cl… ([`types/type-alias`](rules/types.md#types-type-alias))
- **A `type` alias may not name a single bare class** — A `TypeExpr` that is nothing but one bare `ClassName`, `EnumName`, `self`, `static` or `parent` atom — with no union, intersection, array wrapper or `?` sugar around it — is refused (`E0307`). ([`types/alias-is-never-a-bare-class`](rules/types.md#types-alias-is-never-a-bare-class))
- **A `type` alias is also a member of a class, interface or enum, reached as `Owner::Name` and as a bare `Name` inside its owner** — A `type` alias is also a member of a class, interface or enum body, taking no visibility modifier, reached as `Owner::Name` from anywhere and as a bare `Name` inside its owner's own body, and never inherited. ([`types/class-scoped-alias`](rules/types.md#types-class-scoped-alias))
- **`callable` is satisfied by an anonymous function or a method reference and by nothing else, and no object is callable** — `callable` is satisfied by exactly two kinds of value: an anonymous function (`fn (...) => ...`) and a method reference — `Core\Str::length`, `$user->getName(...)`, `self::helper` (early-bound), `static::helper` (late-b… ([`types/callable-values`](rules/types.md#types-callable-values))
- **`fn` is the only way to write an anonymous function, with an expression body or a block body** — `fn` is the only way to write an anonymous function, in two body shapes:… ([`types/anonymous-function`](rules/types.md#types-anonymous-function))
- **A `callable` type may name its parameters, and must then name its return type** — A `callable` type may name its parameters and its return type:… ([`types/callable-signature`](rules/types.md#types-callable-signature))
- **A callable satisfies a callable type when its arity is at most the type's, matched from the left** — A callable of arity *n* satisfies `callable(T₁..Tₘ): R` when **`n ≤ m`**, and only the first *n* parameter types are compared. ([`types/callable-arity`](rules/types.md#types-callable-arity))
- **A callable's parameters are contravariant and its return type covariant** — A callable type's **parameters are contravariant** and its **return type covariant**:… ([`types/callable-variance`](rules/types.md#types-callable-variance))
- **An unannotated `fn` parameter takes its type from the position the anonymous function is written in** — Where an anonymous function appears in a position whose expected type is a callable type, each parameter the anonymous function does not annotate takes its type from the corresponding position of that type. ([`types/anonymous-function-parameter-inference`](rules/types.md#types-anonymous-function-parameter-inference))
- **`callable` is the only type name for a function value, and a callable is invoked directly** — `callable` is the only type name for a value made by an anonymous function or a method reference. ([`types/callable-is-the-only-function-type`](rules/types.md#types-callable-is-the-only-function-type))
- **An anonymous function captures by value exactly the outer names its body reads, and there is no `use` clause** — An anonymous function captures exactly the outer variables its body reads, snapshotted **by value** at the point the anonymous function is evaluated. ([`types/implicit-capture`](rules/types.md#types-implicit-capture))
- **An anonymous function may carry a self-name, visible only inside its own body** — An anonymous function that needs to call itself may carry an optional name between `fn` and its parameter list:… ([`types/anonymous-function-self-name`](rules/types.md#types-anonymous-function-self-name))
- **`object` is the opaque top of every class type** — `object` is the opaque supertype of every class type — a named declared class, and the anonymous class an anonymous object synthesizes (`types/anonymous-object`). ([`types/object-top`](rules/types.md#types-object-top))
- **`{name: value}` builds an anonymous, methodless object and nothing more** — Each anonymous object's precise type is a private, compiler-synthesized class with exactly the fields written, each field's type inferred from its initializer. ([`types/anonymous-object`](rules/types.md#types-anonymous-object))
- **`{name: T}` in type position is a structural shape checked by width subtyping, and `{name?: T}` marks a key that may be absent** — A shape type is **not** a class and **not** an interface. ([`types/shape-type`](rules/types.md#types-shape-type))
- **A member reached through an erased receiver is answered at run time, and a failure is a throw** — Three receivers are erased: plain `object`, a shape type asked for a name it does not list, and `mixed` — the widest, because it defers not only *which* class is behind the handle but *whether there is one*. ([`types/erased-member-access`](rules/types.md#types-erased-member-access))
- **`class<T>` is a type whose value is a class descriptor, and `as` is its only source** — `class<T>` is a type atom, written in every position a type is written, whose **value** is the run-time class descriptor — the same word a `new static(...)` already allocates from, carrying the class's name, parent chai… ([`types/class-reference`](rules/types.md#types-class-reference))
- **`class<T>` widens wherever `T` widens, and never narrows without an `as`** — `class<Dog>` widens to `class<Animal>` wherever `Dog` widens to `Animal` — a parameter, a return, an assignment to a wider binding — and **never back**. ([`types/class-reference-variance`](rules/types.md#types-class-reference-variance))
- **Three sites accept a `class<T>`, and every other operand is still refused there** — Three spellings accept a `class<T>` operand, and nothing else:… ([`types/class-reference-sites`](rules/types.md#types-class-reference-sites))
- **`::class` answers the class the value is, and folding is an optimization of that** — `::class` answers the class the value **is**. ([`types/class-constant`](rules/types.md#types-class-constant))
- **Absent storage never reads as a zero value: an unassigned variable and `[]` in a read position are refused, and an absent key throws** — Absent storage never reads as a zero value: a hole is answered before the program runs or thrown at. ([`types/absent-storage-is-never-a-zero-value`](rules/types.md#types-absent-storage-is-never-a-zero-value))
- **An element write through a temporary is refused, because the separated copy has nowhere to be written back** — An element write through a temporary is refused, because copy-on-write separates the array before the element is written and the separated copy has to land back in whatever held the array. ([`types/an-element-write-needs-storage-to-write-back-into`](rules/types.md#types-an-element-write-needs-storage-to-write-back-into))
- **`->` on a receiver that can hold no object is refused where it is written** — `->` on a receiver whose declared type can hold no object is refused where it is written: `$i->name` where `$i` is declared `int` is `E0495`. ([`types/a-declared-type-answers-before-the-program-runs`](rules/types.md#types-a-declared-type-answers-before-the-program-runs))
- **`instanceof` is refused where it is written, and `is` is the one type test** — Novis has one type test, `$x is T`, and `instanceof` is refused where it is written (`E0253`): the diagnostic names the rewrite — *write `$x is Request`; a class reference on the right is `$x is $cls`*. ([`types/one-type-test`](rules/types.md#types-one-type-test))

## Expressions

- **Six syntax positions test truthiness; every other `bool` position stays checked** — Exactly six syntax positions test a value's truthiness instead of requiring it to already be `bool`: `if`/`elseif`'s condition, `while`/`do…while`'s condition, `for`'s middle clause, the ternary and elvis condition, and… ([`expressions/truthy-positions`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-truthy-positions))
- **The truthy table is PHP's, and `bytes` is falsy only when it is empty** — A condition is decided by one truthy table over Novis's type set:… ([`expressions/truthy-table`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-truthy-table))
- **`and`, `or` and `xor` do not parse, and `&&`/`||` are the whole set** — `and`, `or` and `xor` are rejected at parse time, in every position, as `E0226`. ([`expressions/no-keyword-logical-operators`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-no-keyword-logical-operators))

- **Two operator mixes whose grouping a reader misreads warn with `W1022`, offering the parentheses that keep the meaning and the grouping most likely meant** — `nvs check` warns with `W1022` at two operator mixes whose grouping a reader misreads, and at no others: a `??` whose right operand is an arithmetic or `.` expression written without parentheses (`$n ?? ([`expressions/misread-grouping-warns`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-misread-grouping-warns))
- **`==` and `!=` are the whole of equality, and `===`, `!==` and `<>` do not parse** — There is **one** equality operator, `==`, and its negation `!=`. ([`expressions/one-equality-operator`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-one-equality-operator))
- **Equality has one row per type, and every row is the strict reading** — Nothing converts. ([`expressions/equality-semantics`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-equality-semantics))
- **A `mixed` or union operand resolves at run time, and a mismatched pair answers `false`** — `$a == $b` where either side is `mixed` or a union compiles, dispatches on the runtime tags, and applies `expressions/equality-semantics`'s table to the row they land in.
