- **Two objects are equal only when they are the same object, and no class may change that** — `$a == $b` on two class instances asks whether they are the same object. ([`expressions/object-identity-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-object-identity-equality))
- **Comparing two types that no single value inhabits is a compile error** — A comparison whose two static types are **disjoint** — no single value inhabits both — is a compile error (`E0466`), because the compiler already knows the answer and the author did not mean to write it. ([`expressions/disjoint-comparison-refused`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-disjoint-comparison-refused))
- **A `switch` label and a `match` arm compare by the equality rule and by nothing else** — A `switch` label and a `match` arm are compared against the subject by `expressions/equality-semantics`, and by nothing else. ([`expressions/switch-match-equality`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-switch-match-equality))
- **A `match` has at least one arm** — A `match` with no arms is `E0476` where it is written. ([`expressions/a-match-has-at-least-one-arm`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-a-match-has-at-least-one-arm))
- **A constant argument to an intrinsic `Core` call is validated while checking and prepared into the artifact** — A short, closed roster of `Core` methods takes an argument that is really a small program — a regex pattern, a URI, a date format, a duration, a format string, a SQL placeholder list. ([`expressions/intrinsic-constant-arguments`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-intrinsic-constant-arguments))
- **The intrinsic roster is a closed set in the compiler's own source, and nothing declares itself into it** — The compiler recognises intrinsics by fully-qualified name from a **closed set in its own source** (`crates/nvs-types/src/intrinsics.rs`). ([`expressions/intrinsic-list-is-closed`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-intrinsic-list-is-closed))
- **`list(...)` does not parse; `[...]` is the only destructuring target** — `list(...)` as a destructuring target does not parse. ([`expressions/bracket-destructuring`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-bracket-destructuring))
- **`??+=`, `??-=` and `??.=` are `$a = ($a ?? d) op $v` with the target evaluated once and `d` the zero of the target's type** — `$a ??+= $v`, `$a ??-= $v` and `$a ??.= $v` mean `$a = ($a ?? ([`expressions/defaulting-assignment`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-defaulting-assignment))
- **`expr as ?T` yields the converted value or `null`, and never throws** — `expr as ?T` produces the value that `expr as T` would produce where that succeeds, and `null` where it would throw. ([`expressions/nullable-conversion`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-conversion))
- **`as ?T` is refused where the conversion cannot fail, where none exists, and at every class target** — `as ?T` is available for exactly the conversions the checked form already defines, and is a compile error everywhere else:… ([`expressions/nullable-conversion-availability`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-nullable-conversion-availability))
- **`as ?T` decides `tainted` and `secret` by exactly the rule `as T` uses, and launders nothing of its own** — Nullability and the security qualifiers are orthogonal axes. ([`expressions/conversion-keeps-qualifiers`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-conversion-keeps-qualifiers))
- **A failable single-`string` parse is spelled `tryParse`, and no separate validity predicate stands beside it** — A class whose `parse` takes **exactly one `string`** and can fail also carries `tryParse(string $s): ?T` — `Core\Uri::tryParse` and `Core\Uuid::tryParse` are it today. ([`expressions/try-parse`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-try-parse))
- **The prepared path and the runtime path are one implementation, so preparation is only earlier and never different** — The prepared path and the runtime path **share one implementation**. ([`expressions/preparation-preserves-behaviour`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-preparation-preserves-behaviour))
- **`|>` substitutes one hole at parse time, and has no run-time representation** — `|>` is a binary operator whose right side is an expression containing the hole `$_`. ([`expressions/pipeline-substitution`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-pipeline-substitution))
- **`|>` binds tighter than every binary operator and looser than unary** — `|>` binds **tighter than every binary operator and looser than unary**. ([`expressions/pipeline-precedence`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-pipeline-precedence))
- **The hole is `$_`, it appears exactly once on a right side, and nowhere else at all** — The hole is `$_`. ([`expressions/pipeline-hole-once`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-pipeline-hole-once))
- **There is no null-skipping pipeline step** — There is no `?|>`. ([`expressions/no-null-skipping-pipeline`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-no-null-skipping-pipeline))
- **An expression-level `catch` is a chain of typed arms guarding one expression** — A `catch` arm is a postfix on an expression. ([`expressions/catch-expression`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-expression))
- **`catch` sits between assignment and the ternary, so one arm guards a whole `??` chain** — `catch` sits **between assignment and the ternary**. ([`expressions/catch-expression-precedence`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-expression-precedence))
- **An arm body is an expression, which admits `throw` and refuses `return` by name** — The arm body is parsed as an expression, and that is the entire rule for what it may hold. ([`expressions/catch-arm-is-an-expression`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-arm-is-an-expression))
- **The result type is the union of the guard and every arm, and an arm is checked from the pre-guard state** — The expression's type is the union of the guarded expression's type and every arm's, computed by the same union the `match` arms use. ([`expressions/catch-result-type`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-result-type))
- **An unbound `catch (Throwable)` arm that supplies a value is warned about** — `W1006` warns on an expression-level arm that names `Throwable`, **binds no variable**, and whose body is not a `throw`. ([`expressions/bare-throwable-arm-warns`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-bare-throwable-arm-warns))
- **The expression form lowers to the block form's landing pad, with the value in a temporary** — There is no run-time representation of the expression form. ([`expressions/catch-lowers-to-block-form`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-catch-lowers-to-block-form))
- **A method reference is the bare `Class::method` on a class and `$obj->method(...)` on an object, one form per receiver, and a dropped reference is a compile error** — A method reference takes a reference to a declared method, and each receiver form has exactly one way to write it. ([`expressions/method-reference`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-method-reference))
- **Partial function application is not adopted; an anonymous function already spells it** — `f(?, $x)` and every application-with-holes shape do not parse. ([`expressions/no-partial-application`](rules/expressions.md#expressions-no-partial-application))

## Statements

- **`<?nvs` is the only code-mode open tag; `<?php` is refused** — `<?nvs` is the only code-mode open tag. ([`statements/nvs-is-the-only-open-tag`](rules/statements.md#statements-nvs-is-the-only-open-tag))
- **`namespace X;` is the only namespace statement, once per file and before any declaration** — `namespace X;` is the only namespace statement, written once per file and before any declaration. ([`statements/one-namespace-statement-per-file`](rules/statements.md#statements-one-namespace-statement-per-file))
- **A name containing a separator is read from the root, and one without it through the imports** — Given a name as written, and the namespace and import set active where it was written:… ([`statements/a-qualified-name-is-absolute`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-qualified-name-is-absolute))
- **A short name resolves through the imports and then the enclosing namespace, and stops** — A short name resolves through the imports and then the enclosing namespace, and stops. ([`statements/no-fallback-to-the-root-namespace`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-fallback-to-the-root-namespace))
- **A leading separator does not parse, in any of the three positions PHP writes one** — The leading separator is refused in all three positions a name could carry one, rather than stripped:… ([`statements/a-leading-separator-does-not-parse`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-leading-separator-does-not-parse))
- **One function decides what a name means, and there is no second place that does** — Name resolution is `nvs_hir::resolve_ref` and nowhere else. ([`statements/one-function-resolves-every-name`](rules/statements.md#statements-one-function-resolves-every-name))
- **A declaration is reachable under exactly the name it was declared with** — A class, interface, enum, method or constant is reachable under exactly the name it was declared with — its own short name, or a fully-qualified path to it — and under no other. ([`statements/nothing-gets-a-second-name`](rules/statements.md#statements-nothing-gets-a-second-name))
- **A use line that no name reads is a warning, and its safe fix deletes the line** — A `use` line that no name in its namespace scope reads is the warning `W1026`. ([`statements/an-unused-use-is-a-warning`](rules/statements.md#statements-an-unused-use-is-a-warning))
- **An enum's name is an ordinary type, usable at every binding site a class name is** — The `enum` keyword appears only at the *declaration*. ([`statements/an-enum-name-is-a-type-everywhere`](rules/statements.md#statements-an-enum-name-is-a-type-everywhere))
- **`require` is the only file-inclusion construct, and it runs every time it is reached** — `require 'path.nvs';` is the only same-frame inclusion construct. ([`statements/require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct`](rules/statements.md#statements-require-is-the-only-inclusion-construct))
- **Declarations cross a `require` and variables do not** — Every name a required file *declares* — a class, an interface, an enum, a `type` alias — is visible to the requiring file exactly as if it had been pasted in. ([`statements/a-required-file-shares-declarations-not-locals`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-required-file-shares-declarations-not-locals))
- **A `require` used for its value hands back `mixed`, and converts like any other boundary** — `require` is an expression, and `$config = require 'config.nvs';` is its value form. ([`statements/a-require-expression-is-mixed`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-require-expression-is-mixed))
- **`static` marks a class member and names a class-relative type, and nothing else** — `static` is a class-member modifier and a class-relative type. ([`statements/static-is-a-member-modifier`](rules/statements.md#statements-static-is-a-member-modifier))
- **A function holds no state of its own, and `global` does not exist** — Two spellings are refused, and each diagnostic names its replacement:… ([`statements/no-function-static-and-no-global`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-function-static-and-no-global))
- **A program holds state in five declared places, and the list is closed** — Exhaustive by construction. ([`statements/storage-that-outlives-a-call`](rules/statements.md#statements-storage-that-outlives-a-call))
- **An isolate's class statics are its own, and a child cannot reach its parent's** — An isolate's context is built with a **statics base of its own**, and that single word is the whole of "a child cannot read or write a parent static". ([`statements/an-isolate-has-its-own-statics`](rules/statements.md#statements-an-isolate-has-its-own-statics))
- **No variable is ever populated by the host; every superglobal is a `Core` class member** — No variable is ever populated by the host. ([`statements/no-host-populated-variables`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-host-populated-variables))
- **`$GLOBALS` and `$_REQUEST` have no replacement of any kind** — `$GLOBALS` and `$_REQUEST` are dropped with no replacement of any kind: no `Core` class, no method, no later addition under a different name. ([`statements/globals-and-request-are-dropped-outright`](rules/statements.md#statements-globals-and-request-are-dropped-outright))
- **An anonymous function captures `$this` only when its body names it, so `static fn` has nothing left to assert** — An anonymous function captures `$this` only when its body uses it, decided by the compiler. ([`statements/an-anonymous-function-captures-this-only-where-it-uses-it`](rules/statements.md#statements-an-anonymous-function-captures-this-only-where-it-uses-it))
- **A by-reference binding is written `inout`, in the modifier slot before the type** — `inout` is a reserved word, written **before the type**, in every position a by-reference binding is legal:… ([`statements/inout-is-the-by-reference-spelling`](rules/statements.md#statements-inout-is-the-by-reference-spelling))
- **An argument that binds an `inout` parameter says so at the call** — An argument bound to an `inout` parameter carries `inout` at the call, and an argument bound to a by-value parameter must not:… ([`statements/inout-is-written-at-the-call`](rules/statements.md#statements-inout-is-written-at-the-call))
- **An `inout` argument is a local or an instance property, and never an element** — `Adder::bump(inout $n)` binds a local, and `Adder::bump(inout $obj->n)` binds an instance property whose class is known while compiling. ([`statements/an-inout-argument-is-a-local`](rules/statements.md#statements-an-inout-argument-is-a-local))
- **There is no write-only `out` mode** — `inout` invites the question of a write-only `out` mode: assigned before return, unreadable on entry. ([`statements/there-is-no-out-mode`](rules/statements.md#statements-there-is-no-out-mode))
- **`&` in a by-reference position is refused at parse time** — `&` where a by-reference marker would go is still recognised, so the diagnostic can name the exact fix, and produces an error node — the AST keeps no variant for it. ([`statements/ampersand-is-not-a-by-reference-marker`](rules/statements.md#statements-ampersand-is-not-a-by-reference-marker))
- **`exit` is the only process-termination keyword; `die` is refused** — `exit` is the only process-termination keyword. ([`statements/exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword`](rules/statements.md#statements-exit-is-the-only-termination-keyword))
- **`exit` ends the program where it stands: no `catch` sees it, no `finally` runs, and a clean exit is not a failure** — `exit` and `exit(n)` end the program from any frame. ([`statements/exit-stops-the-program-where-it-stands`](rules/statements.md#statements-exit-stops-the-program-where-it-stands))
- **A non-`void` body hands back a value at every exit; nothing returns `null` for a declaration it did not make** — A body checked against a declared non-`void` return type never reaches its own end: that path writes no value at all, and there is no implicit conversion by which `null` becomes the declared type, so accepting it would… ([`statements/a-body-never-falls-off-its-end`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-body-never-falls-off-its-end))
- **`continue` always continues a loop, and a written level counts the way PHP counts** — A `switch` owns `break` and nothing else, so `continue` always continues the innermost enclosing loop. ([`statements/continue-always-continues-a-loop`](rules/statements.md#statements-continue-always-continues-a-loop))
- **A `try` has a `catch` or a `finally`, and a `catch` clause names exactly one class** — A `try` has at least one `catch` clause or a `finally`, and a `catch` clause names exactly one class. ([`statements/a-try-has-a-clause-and-a-catch-names-one-class`](rules/statements.md#statements-a-try-has-a-clause-and-a-catch-names-one-class))
- **A `return` never leaves a `finally` block, and neither does a `break` or `continue` whose target lies outside it** — `return` inside `finally` does not compile. ([`statements/no-return-leaves-a-finally`](rules/statements.md#statements-no-return-leaves-a-finally))
- **`let` and `is` cannot name anything; `var` declares, `as` converts, and `is` is the type test** — Neither `let` nor `is` may name a class, interface, trait, enum, constant, function or parameter. ([`statements/let-and-is-are-reserved`](rules/statements.md#statements-let-and-is-are-reserved))

## Classes

- **No `function` and no `const` may be declared outside a class body** — A `function` declaration and a `const` declaration are legal inside a class body and nowhere else. ([`classes/no-free-functions-or-constants`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-free-functions-or-constants))
- **A `class`, `interface` or `enum` is declared at file scope, or not at all, and an `enum` may also be declared in a class or interface body** — A `class`, `interface` or `enum` is declared at file scope, or not at all, with one exception: an `enum` may also be declared in a class or interface body (`enums/class-scoped-enum`). ([`classes/a-type-is-declared-at-file-scope`](rules/classes.md#classes-a-type-is-declared-at-file-scope))
- **Every name is compared exactly, so `Foo` and `foo` are two names and never one** — Every name — class, interface, enum, enum case, namespace segment, method, property, parameter, local, class constant — is compared exactly, everywhere resolution happens. ([`classes/names-resolve-case-sensitively`](rules/classes.md#classes-names-resolve-case-sensitively))
- **Keywords, contextual keywords and the `<?nvs` tag are lower case and nothing else** — Keywords are matched exactly: `if` is a keyword, `IF` and `If` are not. ([`classes/reserved-spellings-are-lower-case`](rules/classes.md#classes-reserved-spellings-are-lower-case))
- **No property, parameter or local name may begin with `_`** — No property, parameter or local variable name may begin with `_`. ([`classes/no-leading-underscore-identifiers`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-leading-underscore-identifiers))
- **A constructor is an ordinary method named `constructor` that runs only through `new` and `parent::constructor(...)`, and `__construct` does not compile** — The constructor is a method named `constructor` — an ordinary lowercase-first name that needs no casing exception of its own. ([`classes/constructor-is-a-method-named-constructor`](rules/classes.md#classes-constructor-is-a-method-named-constructor))
- **A visibility keyword on a parameter promotes it to a property only in the `constructor`** — A `public`, `protected` or `private` keyword on a parameter promotes it to a property, and it does that only in the `constructor`. ([`classes/promotion-is-constructor-only`](rules/classes.md#classes-promotion-is-constructor-only))
- **A `new` through a class reference checks `T`'s constructor, and an implementor whose constructor diverges is refused there** — `new $cls(...)` over a `class<T>` types its arguments against **`T`'s** constructor, exactly as `new static(...)` types them against the current class's. ([`classes/constructor-compatibility`](rules/classes.md#classes-constructor-compatibility))
- **Every property a class declares is definitely assigned on every path out of every constructor** — Every property a class declares is assigned on every path out of every constructor the class exposes, checked by the same flow analysis that already proves definite assignment for locals. ([`classes/definite-property-initialization`](rules/classes.md#classes-definite-property-initialization))
- **There is no `undefined`: a property that may legitimately hold no value is `?T`** — There is no `undefined` type and no `undefined` value. ([`classes/no-undefined-value`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-undefined-value))
- **Reading a property that has never been written throws a catchable error and never yields a value** — Reading a property that has never been written throws a catchable `LogicError` — "`Post`'s property `$author` is read before it is initialized." — propagated by checked return (`errors/propagation`) rather than routed t… ([`classes/an-unwritten-property-read-throws`](rules/classes.md#classes-an-unwritten-property-read-throws))
- **A `lateinit` property is assigned after the constructor rather than inside it** — A property declared `lateinit` is exempt from the constructor-must-assign obligation, for the pattern that obligation cannot express: a container, an ORM, or any setter injection that populates a property after `new` re… ([`classes/lateinit`](rules/classes.md#classes-lateinit))
- **`lateinit` takes every type, and is refused on a promoted parameter and beside `readonly`** — `lateinit` is admitted on a property of every type: a class or an interface, a scalar, a string, an array and a nullable `?T`. ([`classes/lateinit-restrictions`](rules/classes.md#classes-lateinit-restrictions))
- **`isinit($obj->prop)` tests whether a `lateinit` property has a value, and reads nothing** — `isinit($obj->prop)` is a construct, parsed like `isset`, whose value is a `bool`: `true` once the `lateinit` property has been written, `false` before. ([`classes/isinit-reads-nothing`](rules/classes.md#classes-isinit-reads-nothing))
- **A `readonly` property is written once, by its own class's constructor through `$this`, and every other write is refused or throws** — A `readonly` property is written once, by its own class's `constructor` through `$this`, and nothing writes it after construction ends. ([`classes/readonly-is-written-once`](rules/classes.md#classes-readonly-is-written-once))
- **`$this` is not assignable** — An assignment to `$this`, plain (`$this = …`) or compound (`$this .= …`, `$this ??= …`), is `E0875` at the target. ([`classes/this-is-not-assignable`](rules/classes.md#classes-this-is-not-assignable))
- **A `lateinit` read the enclosing method can prove is too early is a compile error, and nothing wider is attempted** — The definite-assignment pass runs inside every method, not only constructors, with a `lateinit` property entering in the "not yet proven written" state, and a read reachable from the method's entry with no intervening w… ([`classes/lateinit-read-before-write`](rules/classes.md#classes-lateinit-read-before-write))
- **A class implementing `LateInit` initializes a `lateinit` property on its first read, and the writes that initialize it are plain** — A read or an element write that finds a `lateinit` property uninitialized, on an object whose class implements `LateInit`, calls `initProperty(string $name): void` with the property's name and then reads the slot again. ([`classes/late-init-initializes-on-the-first-read`](rules/classes.md#classes-late-init-initializes-on-the-first-read))
- **A property that the class does not declare cannot be read or written, and no user code runs for the attempt** — A class's declared properties are its whole property surface. ([`classes/no-dynamic-properties`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-dynamic-properties))
- **`unset` on a declared property is a compile error, and `isset` on one is an ordinary null test** — `unset($obj->prop)`, and `unset(Class::$prop)` with it, is a compile-time diagnostic for every declared property, static or instance, whatever its nullability. ([`classes/unset-is-refused-on-a-property`](rules/classes.md#classes-unset-is-refused-on-a-property))
- **A property's own `get`/`set` hook is PHP 8.4's, unchanged, and every read or write of that property is a call to it** — A property may declare one `get` and one `set` hook, scoped to that one property. ([`classes/property-hooks`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-hooks))
- **A class observes every read and write of its own properties by implementing `PropertyObserver`, never by declaring `__get`/`__set`** — A class observes its own properties by implementing the global interface `PropertyObserver`, whose members are `onPropertyGet(string $name, mixed $value): void` and `onPropertySet(string $name, mixed $value): void`. ([`classes/property-observer`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-observer))
- **A property write runs the guard, then its hook or its storage, then the observer, and neither the guard nor the observer can change the value** — Every read or write of a property runs one fixed pipeline, and each interface a class implements adds its own step to it:… ([`classes/property-observer-pipeline`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-observer-pipeline))
- **A class that implements no `PropertyObserver` pays nothing for one** — Whether a class implements `PropertyObserver` is known at compile time from its declaration, so a property with no hook on a class that does not implement it compiles to a direct field load or store: no branch, no virtu… ([`classes/property-observer-costs-nothing-when-unused`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-observer-costs-nothing-when-unused))
- **A class implementing `PropertyGuard` is called before every write of its properties, and a throw stops the write** — A class implementing the global interface `PropertyGuard` has `beforePropertySet(string $name, mixed $value, array<string> $keys): void` called before every write of one of its properties, and `beforePropertyUnset(strin… ([`classes/property-guard-runs-before-the-write`](rules/classes.md#classes-property-guard-runs-before-the-write))
- **A method declared again over an ancestor's keeps a signature a call through the ancestor can use** — A method a class or an interface declares again over one an ancestor declares is an override, and it keeps a signature a call through the ancestor can use. ([`classes/an-override-keeps-its-parents-signature`](rules/classes.md#classes-an-override-keeps-its-parents-signature))
- **A property declared again over a superclass's keeps the superclass's exact type** — An instance property a class declares again over one a superclass declares keeps the superclass's exact type. ([`classes/a-redeclared-property-keeps-its-parents-type`](rules/classes.md#classes-a-redeclared-property-keeps-its-parents-type))
- **A covariant parameter or property takes a narrower type, and each value that enters it is tested** — A method parameter and an instance property may be declared again at a narrower type when the declaration writes `covariant` after its modifiers and before its type: `public function feed(covariant Dog $a)`, `inout cova… ([`classes/a-covariant-type-is-checked-where-a-value-enters`](rules/classes.md#classes-a-covariant-type-is-checked-where-a-value-enters))
- **A member reachable from two default or delegated sources with no override is a compile error** — A method name reachable from more than one source — a default from one implemented interface, a default from another, or a `by`-delegated interface — is a compile error (`E0859`) when the class does not itself declare t… ([`classes/member-conflict-is-an-error`](rules/classes.md#classes-member-conflict-is-an-error))
- **There is no `trait`: shared behaviour is an interface method with a body, shared state is `by` delegation** — `trait`, a class-body `use Trait, ...;` and `insteadof` are not in the grammar. ([`classes/no-traits`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-traits))
- **A `public` interface method with a body is a default method, and `$this` inside it is the interface** — An `interface` method may carry a body. ([`classes/interface-default-methods`](rules/classes.md#classes-interface-default-methods))
- **A `private` interface method is visible only to that interface's own bodies** — An `interface` method declared `private` and carrying a body is an internal helper for that interface's own method bodies. ([`classes/interface-private-methods`](rules/classes.md#classes-interface-private-methods))
- **An interface declares no property: one written there is `E0254`, and the value comes from a method or a constant** — An interface declares no property. ([`classes/interfaces-declare-no-state`](rules/classes.md#classes-interfaces-declare-no-state))
- **`implements I by $field` forwards every member `I` requires to that property** — Each entry in a class's `implements` list may carry a `by $field;` suffix. ([`classes/delegation-by-property`](rules/classes.md#classes-delegation-by-property))
- **Two objects order only when their class implements `Comparable`, and there is no property-walk fallback** — Two objects may be compared with `<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` or `<=>` only when their class implements the global interface `Comparable`, whose single member is `compareTo(self $other): int` returning negative, zero or positive. ([`classes/comparable`](rules/classes.md#classes-comparable))
- **`compareTo` fixes the other operand to `self`, so two different classes are never ordered against each other** — `compareTo(self $other)` fixes the other operand to the implementing class. ([`classes/comparable-is-same-class-only`](rules/classes.md#classes-comparable-is-same-class-only))
- **`<`, `>`, `<=`, `>=` and `<=>` on two objects lower to one `compareTo` call** — All five relational spellings lower to one call: `$a < $b` is `$a->compareTo($b) < 0`, `$a >= $b` is `$a->compareTo($b) >= 0`, and `$a <=> $b` is the call itself. ([`classes/ordering-lowers-to-compare-to`](rules/classes.md#classes-ordering-lowers-to-compare-to))
- **An object becomes a string only through `Stringable::toString`, and everywhere else is a diagnostic** — An object reaches a string only through the global interface `Stringable`, whose single member is `toString(): string`. ([`classes/stringable`](rules/classes.md#classes-stringable))
- **No method name changes a class's behaviour by being present; every PHP magic method is replaced by a declared interface or gone** — No method name changes what a class does by being present. ([`classes/no-magic-methods`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-magic-methods))
- **There is no `__call` or `__callStatic`: a call to a method the class does not declare is a diagnostic** — Calling a method a class does not declare is a compile-time diagnostic, like any other unresolvable name. ([`classes/no-call-magic`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-call-magic))
- **There are no destructors: cleanup is an explicit method call the holder makes** — Novis has no destructors. ([`classes/no-destructors`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-destructors))
- **A debug dump shows a class's real declared properties and their real values, and no class can change that** — A debug dump shows a class's real declared properties and their real current values. ([`classes/no-debug-hook`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-debug-hook))
- **A copy is either `clone`'s one level or the graph copy, and no class customizes either** — Novis has two copy depths and no third. ([`classes/two-copy-depths`](rules/classes.md#classes-two-copy-depths))
- **`clone` copies an object's declared storage one level deep and shares every object it reaches** — `clone $x` produces a new instance of `$x`'s class and copies its declared storage one level deep. ([`classes/clone-is-shallow`](rules/classes.md#classes-clone-is-shallow))
- **The graph copy is one recursive, cycle-safe walk with two carriers, and it refuses what has no meaning on the other side** — The graph copy is a recursive, cycle-safe traversal of a value's reachable structure producing a result that shares no mutable heap state with its source. ([`classes/graph-copy`](rules/classes.md#classes-graph-copy))
- **`Core\Serialize::decode` accepts only bytes this build's `encode` produced, and refuses everything else outright** — `Core\Serialize::encode($x): bytes` runs the graph copy and encodes the result; `decode` runs it in reverse. ([`classes/serialize-is-a-closed-format`](rules/classes.md#classes-serialize-is-a-closed-format))
- **Every encoder that walks a value graph ends a cycle by identity and names the path, never by exhausting a depth cap** — Every encoder that walks a value graph carries the identity of the objects on the path from the root to the value it is writing, and the first value it meets twice ends the walk there — refused, naming the property chai… ([`classes/an-encoder-ends-a-cycle-by-identity`](rules/classes.md#classes-an-encoder-ends-a-cycle-by-identity))
- **A class is reachable under its declared name and nowhere else** — A class is reachable exactly where it is declared — under its own short name, in scope through an import, or by its fully-qualified path — and nowhere else. ([`classes/no-class-alias`](rules/classes.md#classes-no-class-alias))
- **A constructor's `return` carries no value; a bare `return;` may still leave early** — `return $value;` inside a `constructor` does not compile: the object under construction is the result, and nothing else can be. ([`classes/a-constructor-return-carries-no-value`](rules/classes.md#classes-a-constructor-return-carries-no-value))
- **A `readonly` property declares no default; a value known at the declaration is a `const`** — `readonly` with an initializer is refused where it is written. ([`classes/a-readonly-property-declares-no-default`](rules/classes.md#classes-a-readonly-property-declares-no-default))

## Enums

- **A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero** — An enum body is a comma list of `Name` or `Name = <integer literal>`, and the optional `: int` or `: uint` before it names the backing type (`enums/one-backing-type`):… ([`enums/declaration`](rules/enums.md#enums-declaration))
- **PHP's `case` keyword does not parse, and each one is diagnosed where it is written** — There is no `case` keyword in an enum body. ([`enums/no-case-keyword`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-case-keyword))
- **An `enum` is also a member of a class or interface body, reached as `Owner::Name` and `Owner::Name::Case`, and as a bare `Name` inside its owner** — An `enum` is also a member of a class or interface body, taking no visibility modifier, reached as `Owner::Name` and `Owner::Name::Case` from anywhere and as a bare `Name` and `Name::Case` inside its owner's own body, a… ([`enums/class-scoped-enum`](rules/enums.md#enums-class-scoped-enum))
- **An enum one class uses is declared in that class, and an enum several classes share is declared in their namespace** — An enum exactly one class takes, returns or holds is declared in that class; an enum several classes use, or none, is declared in their namespace. ([`enums/an-enum-lives-in-the-class-that-uses-it`](rules/enums.md#enums-an-enum-lives-in-the-class-that-uses-it))
- **An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type** — `enum Status { Active, Banned }` declares a new named integer type with a fixed set of cases, and the enum's name is then a type like any other — a property, a parameter, a return, a local, a class constant, an `array<T… ([`enums/closed-integer-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-closed-integer-type))
- **Every enum is backed by exactly one integer type, and nothing else backs one** — `enum E: int` and `enum E: uint` name the backing type; with no `: T` written it is `int`. ([`enums/one-backing-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-one-backing-type))
- **An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is** — An enum value is its backing integer and nothing more — zero additional bytes over what `int` or `uint` already costs, no allocation, no refcount, no descriptor. ([`enums/representation`](rules/enums.md#enums-representation))
- **An enum case is always truthy, whatever integer backs it** — An enum case in a condition is **always truthy**, whatever integer backs it. ([`enums/truthiness`](rules/enums.md#enums-truthiness))
- **A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases** — `EnumName::CaseName` **is** an integer constant, inlined at every use site the way a literal `5` is: nothing is allocated, nothing is refcounted, there is no descriptor, and there is no per-isolate storage slot for an e… ([`enums/no-class-machinery`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-class-machinery))
- **Reflection describes an enum's shape and grants it nothing a class has** — `Core\Reflect\EnumInfo::of(Status::class)` reports an enum's shape as ordinary structural metadata — the type's name and its closed case list — the same way `ClassInfo` reports a class's shape. ([`enums/reflection`](rules/enums.md#enums-reflection))

## Iteration

- **A `for` init clause is one typed declaration or a list of expressions, never both** — A `for` header's init clause holds **one typed local declaration, or a list of expressions, and never a mix**:… ([`iteration/for-init-clause`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-for-init-clause))
- **A header-declared counter is function-scoped, and a second header declaring it again is refused** — A counter declared in a `for` header is **function-scoped**, exactly as every other binding is. ([`iteration/for-counter-scope`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-for-counter-scope))
- **A refused `for` header is one diagnostic, never a cascade** — Two grammatical refusals, each raised once and each naming the spelling that works:… ([`iteration/for-init-refusals`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-for-init-refusals))
- **`foreach` drives exactly three subjects, and a fourth is refused where it is written** — `foreach` accepts three subjects and refuses a fourth where it is written:… ([`iteration/foreach-subjects`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-foreach-subjects))
- **Two interfaces carry every iteration, and a cursor is `advance()` then `current()`** — Iteration has exactly two interfaces, both reserved names the compiler owns:… ([`iteration/two-interfaces`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-two-interfaces))
- **A class implements a compiler-owned generic interface at a concrete type, and declares no type variable of its own** — Type variables belong to declarations the compiler owns. ([`iteration/concrete-generic-implements`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-concrete-generic-implements))
- **A class cannot make `$obj[$k]` or a count into a method call** — `ArrayAccess` and `Countable` do not exist, and no other interface makes a syntactic form dispatch to a method. ([`iteration/no-magic-collection-interfaces`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-no-magic-collection-interfaces))
- **`current()` outside the protocol throws rather than answering** — `current()` throws a `LogicError` when it is called before the first `advance()`, and when it is called after an `advance()` returned `false`. ([`iteration/cursor-out-of-range`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-cursor-out-of-range))
- **A body that yields is a generator, and calling one returns a state object without running a line of it** — A function whose body contains `yield` is a **generator**. ([`iteration/generators`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-generators))
- **A generator is a lazy sequence and nothing more** — A generator is a lazy sequence in one direction. ([`iteration/one-way-only`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-one-way-only))
- **`yield` appears only in the generator's own body** — `yield` is confined to the generator's own body. ([`iteration/yield-lexical-confinement`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-yield-lexical-confinement))
- **A generator does not cross a boundary and does not clone** — A generator object is not serializable, does not cross a `spawn`, `spawn worker` or `spawn script` boundary, and does not `clone`. ([`iteration/generator-stays-in-one-isolate`](rules/iteration.md#iteration-generator-stays-in-one-isolate))

## Attributes

- **An attribute is an anonymous object on a declaration, and nothing is ever declared or instantiated for it** — `#[Name(field: value, ...)]`, or the bare `#[{field: value, ...}]`, attaches an anonymous object to a declaration. ([`attributes/inert-metadata`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-inert-metadata))
- **An attribute attaches to a declaration or a parameter, and a named one's name is a shape-typed `type` alias** — An attribute attaches to a declaration: a class, an interface or an enum, a method, a property or one of its hooks, a class constant, an enum case, and a method's parameter. ([`attributes/attach-sites-and-forms`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-attach-sites-and-forms))
- **Every field value in an attribute payload is a compile-time constant** — Every field value inside a `#[...]` payload is a compile-time constant: a literal, a class constant, an enum case, or `Foo::class`. ([`attributes/payload-is-a-compile-time-constant`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-payload-is-a-compile-time-constant))
- **An attribute may be attached to one declaration any number of times, and attach time never counts them** — The same attribute — named or bare, with the same field values or different ones — may be attached to one declaration any number of times. ([`attributes/repeatable`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-repeatable))
- **An explicit `<T>` at a call site is written for compiler-owned members only** — `Core\Attributes::get<T>` needs `T` supplied at the call site: no argument has a type it could be inferred from. ([`attributes/call-site-type-argument`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-call-site-type-argument))
- **A retrieval matches a payload by the shape it satisfies, never by the name it was attached under** — `T` is a shape type — an inline `{...}`, or a `type` alias naming one. ([`attributes/structural-retrieval`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-structural-retrieval))
- **A retrieval is answered while checking and replaced by its answer, so ambiguity is a compile error** — A declaration's attached-attribute list is fixed by its source, so `Core\Attributes::get<T>` and `::all<T>` are answered by `nvs check` and the call is **replaced** with the answer:… ([`attributes/retrieval-folds-while-checking`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-retrieval-folds-while-checking))
- **`#[Api]` may add to the generated document and may not contradict the code** — `#[Api]` supplies what a handler's types cannot say — tags, error responses, a security scheme, an example — to the OpenAPI document `nvs build --openapi` writes. ([`attributes/api-adds-and-cannot-contradict`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-api-adds-and-cannot-contradict))
- **A method carrying `#[Route]` carries `#[Access]`, and an omission does not compile** — A method carrying `#[Route]` must also carry `#[Access]`. ([`attributes/access-is-a-required-sibling`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-access-is-a-required-sibling))
- **`#[Access]` names one resolvable decision in `allow`, and one of them covers a method** — `allow` is required, and its declared type is `mixed` because the compiler promises not to know what the value means. ([`attributes/access-payload`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-access-payload))
- **`#[Core\Deprecated]` names its replacement as a Novis expression checked where it is declared, and every use is warning `W1003` carrying that replacement as its fix** — `#[Core\Deprecated(since:, note:, replace:)]` marks a declaration as retired, and its `replace` is one Novis expression whose placeholders are the declaration's own parameters and `$this`. ([`attributes/a-deprecation-names-its-replacement-as-code`](rules/attributes.md#attributes-a-deprecation-names-its-replacement-as-code))

## Errors

- **A limit report is not a Throwable, and the type checker knows it** — The `Throwable` classes are global and are the ordinary `catch` target. ([`errors/throwable-hierarchy`](rules/errors.md#errors-throwable-hierarchy))
- **An error propagates as a checked return, never by unwinding** — Every compiled function and every runtime helper carries one signature, and errors travel in its return value:… ([`errors/propagation`](rules/errors.md#errors-propagation))
- **A throw costs no more than a return, and only its raise allocates** — The marginal cost of `errors/propagation`'s status check is **0.85 ns per frame**, measured as the slope between a 2-frame and an 18-frame chain so the harness's own call-out overhead cancels. ([`errors/throw-is-not-slower`](rules/errors.md#errors-throw-is-not-slower))
- **A runtime helper never unwinds, and a panic dies inside one request** — Because nothing may unwind through a JIT frame, a runtime helper is declared `extern "C"` — never `extern "C-unwind"` — and wraps its body in `catch_unwind`, turning a panic into `FATAL` with the message recorded in `Ct… ([`errors/helper-abi`](rules/errors.md#errors-helper-abi))
- **Recursion is bounded twice: a catchable error, then a fatal** — Novis compiles natively, so every user call is a real machine frame. ([`errors/stack-depth`](rules/errors.md#errors-stack-depth))
- **Tier 1 — a resource limit reaches the request that spent it** — `Core\Fatal::onLimit(callable(LimitReport): void $handler): void` fires only for a resource-limit `FATAL` — memory, CPU time, `max_output`, wall time, `max_script_depth` and call-stack depth. ([`errors/on-limit`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-limit))
- **An allocation past the memory ceiling is refused before it is made, and the refusal is a complete no-op** — An allocation that would carry a request past `[limits] memory` is refused **before** the block is taken, and the refusal is a complete no-op. ([`errors/an-allocation-past-the-ceiling-is-refused-in-front-of-itself`](rules/errors.md#errors-an-allocation-past-the-ceiling-is-refused-in-front-of-itself))
- **A failure escalates through four tiers, and no tier is retried** — Nothing Novis runs is silently dropped, but not everything is *caught* — those are different guarantees. ([`errors/escalation-ladder`](rules/errors.md#errors-escalation-ladder))
- **Tier 2 — an uncaught throw reaches the request root as itself** — `Core\Fatal::onUncaughtThrow(callable(Throwable): void $handler): void` fires when an ordinary `THROWN` propagates through every frame uncaught and reaches the isolate or request root. ([`errors/on-uncaught-throw`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-uncaught-throw))
- **Tier 3 — the configured handler is an ordinary isolate on the engine's own budget** — `[log] handler = 'path/to/handler.nvs'` names a script invoked as an ordinary `spawn script` isolate — fresh arena, fresh globals, its own config overlay, sharing nothing but compiled code — receiving one explicit repor… ([`errors/handler-script`](rules/errors.md#errors-handler-script))
- **Tier 4 — the floor is native, bounded, and gives up rather than escalating** — Hardcoded in Rust, with no script execution — there is nothing left here that could throw, panic or need a further tier, because this is the floor. ([`errors/engine-floor`](rules/errors.md#errors-engine-floor))
- **An internal panic never runs the failing request's own code** — A resource-limit `FATAL` means the *script* asked for too much. ([`errors/panics-bypass-user-code`](rules/errors.md#errors-panics-bypass-user-code))
- **A compile failure is catchable mid-execution and reaches the ladder at entry** — the chance to register anything. ([`errors/compile-failure`](rules/errors.md#errors-compile-failure))
- **Every developer-facing output is one closed record** — Every developer-facing output in Novis is a **record**: an envelope plus a tree of **nodes**. ([`errors/diagnostic-record`](rules/errors.md#errors-diagnostic-record))
- **Five producers build the one record** — Five producers build `errors/diagnostic-record`, and none of them implements a format:… ([`errors/record-producers`](rules/errors.md#errors-record-producers))
- **A record names the file, line and member it was produced at, and a `Throwable`'s location is that same datum** — A record's envelope carries where it was produced — the file as the program named it, its one-based line, and the enclosing `Class::member` where there is one — filled by the producer from a constant the compiler alread… ([`errors/a-record-names-where-it-was-produced`](rules/errors.md#errors-a-record-names-where-it-was-produced))
- **Redaction, control bytes, bidi and elision are decided in the record** — Four transformations are properties of the **record**, applied when it is built, before any rendering sees it. ([`errors/record-transformations`](rules/errors.md#errors-record-transformations))
- **The sink in force picks the rendering, and no call site may name one** — A record is rendered as **plaintext**, **HTML** or **JSON**, and the sink already in force picks which. ([`errors/renderings`](rules/errors.md#errors-renderings))
- **A class cannot change how it is dumped** — There is **no customization hook**: no `DebugRepresentable`, no `__debugInfo`, no per-class renderer. ([`errors/no-render-hook`](rules/errors.md#errors-no-render-hook))
- **A dump goes to the log, and reaches a response body only in development** — CLI dumps go to stderr, not stdout, so piping and redirection keep working while debugging. ([`errors/debug-dump`](rules/errors.md#errors-debug-dump))
- **One write path, and the engine floor is its other caller** — Application code and `errors/handler-script` call this; it is a thin binding over the **same native record-and-write helper** `errors/engine-floor` calls directly when it has no script to run at all. ([`errors/log-write`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-write))
- **Five levels, and the mapping to syslog is fixed** — An ordinary enum, and the syslog mapping is fixed — 7, 6, 4, 3, 2 — because `syslog` is a `errors/engine-floor` target and a severity is not optional there. ([`errors/log-level`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-level))
- **A record's fields are named and typed, not a stringly bag** — `fields` is a **named, typed** structure inside `errors/diagnostic-record`, never `array<string, mixed>` at the core. ([`errors/log-fields`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-fields))
- **A repeat is bounded at the sink that suffers from it: a disk-bounded target coalesces before the write, and an indexed one groups at read time** — A run of identical records is bounded at the sink that would suffer from it, and each sink answers for what is scarce in it: a disk-bounded target coalesces before the write, and an indexed target stores every occurrenc… ([`errors/a-repeat-is-bounded-at-the-sink-that-suffers`](rules/errors.md#errors-a-repeat-is-bounded-at-the-sink-that-suffers))
- **`[errors] deprecated` makes a use of deprecated code write a log record or throw while it runs, and is `"ignore"` by default in every mode** — `[errors] deprecated` decides what a use of deprecated code does while it runs: `"ignore"`, `"log"` or `"throw"`, and `"ignore"` by default in every mode. ([`errors/a-use-of-deprecated-code-may-log-or-throw`](rules/errors.md#errors-a-use-of-deprecated-code-may-log-or-throw))
- **Ambiguous input is refused whole, never repaired** — An input is **ambiguous** when two conforming readers can disagree about what it says. ([`errors/ambiguous-input-refused`](rules/errors.md#errors-ambiguous-input-refused))
- **The closed list of what makes an HTTP message ambiguous** — Refused on a request Novis receives **and on a response Novis's outbound client receives**:… ([`errors/http-message-defects`](rules/errors.md#errors-http-message-defects))
- **A cookie name is bytes, and a prefix is enforced once** — `Core\Request::cookie(name)` matches **byte for byte**. ([`errors/cookie-name-bytes`](rules/errors.md#errors-cookie-name-bytes))
- **A multipart body is capped by part count, not only by size** — `[limits] max_multipart_parts` defaults to **1000** and counts every part, field parts included. ([`errors/multipart-part-count`](rules/errors.md#errors-multipart-part-count))
- **A path component that does not spell what it resolves to is refused, on every platform** — `Core\IO::within` — the launderer, and the one place the base directory is known — refuses a component that… ([`errors/path-component-refusals`](rules/errors.md#errors-path-component-refusals))

## Tooling

- **A file whose first two bytes are `#!` starts in code mode, and its first line is trivia** — `?>` still switches to text mode and writes literal bytes to standard output, and a later `<?nvs` reopens code mode (`statements/nvs-is-the-only-open-tag`). ([`tooling/shebang-opens-code-mode`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-shebang-opens-code-mode))
- **There is no REPL and none is planned; `nvs run`, `nvs test` and `Core\Debug::dump` are the answer** — `nvs` gains no `repl` subcommand and no interactive evaluator, and the subcommand roster is not reopened for one. ([`tooling/no-repl`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-no-repl))
- **Reflection and source parsing are built into `Core`, and `Core\Ast` is the compiler's own parser** — `Core\Reflect` and `Core\Ast` are built-in `Core` domain classes, present in every Novis program with nothing to install: read-only structural introspection over a program's own classes, interfaces, enums, functions, pr… ([`tooling/reflection-and-source-parsing-are-core-features`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-reflection-and-source-parsing-are-core-features))
- **Against Python, Novis claims the tool that gets handed over; "faster than Python" and "replaces Python" are forbidden** — The claim Novis makes against Python is the one Python is worst at: **the tool that gets handed to somebody else.** It is `programs/audience`'s existing purchase pointed at the command line — a second audience below the… ([`tooling/python-claims`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-python-claims))
- **Every execution context binds `echo` to a sink, and the default sink is the terminal** — A program reads which row it is in with `Core\Env::context()`, whose seven cases are these rows with the fourth split into `Schedule`, `Job` and `Test` (`core-classes/env-context`). ([`tooling/echo-always-has-a-sink`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-echo-always-has-a-sink))
- **Terminal output is a sink, and every control byte is substituted visibly regardless of qualifier or tty** — Standard output and standard error are sinks. ([`tooling/terminal-output-is-a-sink`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-terminal-output-is-a-sink))
- **`Cli\Text` is the terminal's one raw path, and both of its constructors neutralize their input** — `Cli\Text` is peer to `Core\Html\Markup` and the only value the terminal sink writes raw. ([`tooling/text-is-the-one-raw-path`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-text-is-the-one-raw-path))
- **An `ESC` in a string literal in the source is a compile error that names `Core\Cli\Text`** — An `ESC` byte in a string literal in the source is a compile error, `E0011`, at the character or escape that writes it, and its message names the fix: style terminal output with `Core\Cli\Text`. ([`tooling/an-escape-in-source-text-is-a-compile-error`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-an-escape-in-source-text-is-a-compile-error))
- **Styling is a value type — `Cli\Style` and `Cli\Color` — and never a fifth grammar** — The library's grammar count is fixed at four — a regex pattern, a `printf` template, a CLDR date pattern and a `pack` format (`core-api/shape-rules` R11, each a sink under `security/every-grammar-is-a-sink`). ([`tooling/styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-styling-is-a-value-not-a-grammar))
- **The terminal profile resolves once per process, and a stream that is not a terminal gets no styling** — Whether each standard stream is a terminal, the colour depth — honouring `NO_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, `FORCE_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb`, and enabling Windows virtual terminal processing where it exists — and the width and… ([`tooling/the-terminal-profile-resolves-once`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-terminal-profile-resolves-once))
- **`Cli::displayWidth` measures the string the sink will write, in grapheme-cluster columns** — `Cli::displayWidth(string): uint` answers UAX #11 terminal columns for **the string the sink will write, not the one it was handed**. ([`tooling/display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-display-width-measures-what-the-sink-writes))
- **There is no raw handle onto standard output or standard error, and no cursor, clipboard or title primitive** — The terminal's substitution is uniform, so a `Core\IO\File` over descriptor 1 or 2 would not be a convenience beside the sink — it would be the way around it, available to exactly the computed-escape case `tooling/termi… ([`tooling/no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-no-raw-handle-onto-standard-output))
- **Only the main task of a CLI program reads the terminal: a prompt anywhere else answers its default or throws, and `Core\Cli::arguments` is empty in a request** — Only the main task of a CLI program reads the terminal. ([`tooling/the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-tty-belongs-to-the-main-task))
- **In-place output is a scoped live region the runtime paints, never a cursor primitive** — `Cli::live<T>(callable(Cli\Live): T $body): T` hands its body a `Cli\Live` with `->set(array<Cli\Text> $lines)`; `Cli::progress<T>(uint $total, callable(Cli\Progress): T $body): T` hands it a `Cli\Progress` with `->adva… ([`tooling/in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-in-place-output-is-a-scoped-live-region))
- **A prompt is a `Core\Cli` member that reads the controlling terminal, and `secret` originates a `secret`** — `Cli::ask`, `Cli::confirm`, `Cli::select<T>`, `Cli::multiSelect<T>` and `Cli::secret` are `Core` members, because raw mode is unreachable from userland with the FFI door shut (`security/no-ffi`) and an extension runs in… ([`tooling/a-prompt-is-a-core-member`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-prompt-is-a-core-member))
- **A prompt never blocks: no terminal or no answer in five minutes takes the `default` or throws `Cli\NotInteractive`** — With no controlling terminal, a prompt returns its `default` if one was given and otherwise throws `Cli\NotInteractive`. ([`tooling/a-prompt-never-blocks`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-prompt-never-blocks))
- **Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region are restored on a throw, a fatal, a panic and a signal** — Raw mode, a hidden cursor and a live region must be undone on a throw, on a fatal, on an internal panic and on a signal. ([`tooling/the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-terminal-is-restored-on-every-exit-path))
- **`#[Command]` builds the command table while compiling, and a duplicate name or an unbindable option fails the build** — `#[Command]` builds the command table while compiling, over the same program enumeration `routing/routes-are-compiled-not-registered` uses for the route table (`programs/implementing`). ([`tooling/commands-are-compiled`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-commands-are-compiled))
- **A command parameter is a positional argument unless it carries `#[Option]`, and its type converts and launders the word** — inference from defaults or types. ([`tooling/a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-parameter-is-an-argument-unless-it-is-an-option))
- **`Core\Command::run` dispatches to the handler the first word names, and help and completions are generated from the table** — `Core\Command::run(): uint` is the entry point: it matches the command line against the compiled table, dispatches to the handler the first word names, and returns the process exit status — a handler's `void` is `0`, an… ([`tooling/command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-command-run-dispatches-and-help-is-generated))
- **`nvs fmt` has one style, takes no configuration, and its output is a pure function of the file it is given** — `nvs fmt` rewrites a `.nvs` file into one canonical layout. ([`tooling/fmt-is-one-canonical-style`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-is-one-canonical-style))
- **The base style is PER: four-space indentation, K&R braces on control structures, Allman braces on declarations, and one canonical modifier order** — Four-space indentation and no tabs; one statement per line; a file ends with exactly one newline and no line carries trailing whitespace. ([`tooling/fmt-base-style-is-per`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-base-style-is-per))
- **`nvs fmt` never breaks or joins a line to fit a width: whether a construct spans one line or several is the line break its author wrote** — `nvs fmt` never breaks a line because it is long and never joins lines onto one. ([`tooling/fmt-never-reflows`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-never-reflows))
- **A list is on one line or has one item per line, and a line break its author wrote at the list's own level is what breaks it** — A list has two layouts: every item on one line, or one item per line. ([`tooling/fmt-a-list-is-one-line-or-one-item-per-line`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-a-list-is-one-line-or-one-item-per-line))
- **A `->` call chain is on one line or has one call per line, and a line break its author wrote before any arrow is what breaks it** — A chain of two or more `->` or `?->` calls has two layouts: on one line, or with every arrow starting a line of its own. ([`tooling/fmt-a-broken-call-chain-is-one-call-per-line`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-a-broken-call-chain-is-one-call-per-line))
- **An `&&`, `||`, `??` or `.` chain is on one line or has one operand per line with the operator first, and a broken control-structure condition puts its parentheses on lines of their own** — A run of `&&`, `||` or `??` has two layouts: on one line, or one operand per line with the operator at the start of the line. ([`tooling/fmt-a-broken-operator-chain-is-one-operand-per-line`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-a-broken-operator-chain-is-one-operand-per-line))
- **A broken chain of any binary operator has one operand per line with the operator first, a broken chain inside one is one level further in, and a `.` chain keeps its author's lines** — Every chain of a binary operator has the layout `tooling/fmt-a-broken-operator-chain-is-one-operand-per-line` gives `&&`, `||` and `??`: on one line, or one operand per line with the operator at the start of the line, o… ([`tooling/fmt-every-binary-operator-breaks-operator-first`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-every-binary-operator-breaks-operator-first))
- **A list item that is a broken operator chain, call chain or ternary breaks the innermost list that holds it** — A list item that is a broken operator chain, a broken `->` call chain or a broken ternary breaks the innermost list that holds it: the list's opener ends its line, as `tooling/fmt-a-list-is-one-line-or-one-item-per-line… ([`tooling/fmt-a-broken-item-breaks-its-list`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-a-broken-item-breaks-its-list))
- **A ternary is on one line, or its `?` and its `:` each start a line one level in** — A ternary is on one line, or its `?` and its `:` each start a line one level in from the line its condition starts on. ([`tooling/fmt-a-broken-ternary-has-a-line-per-branch`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-a-broken-ternary-has-a-line-per-branch))
- **Every control structure's header is on one line, or its `(` ends its line, its parts start lines one level in, and its `)` starts a line of its own** — The parenthesised header of every control structure — `if`, `elseif`, `while`, `do … while`, `switch`, `match`, `foreach` and `for` — has two layouts. ([`tooling/fmt-every-control-header-breaks-like-a-condition`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-every-control-header-breaks-like-a-condition))
- **Every expression kind and control structure has a broken layout or is listed as keeping its author's line breaks, and a test fails on one that is neither** — Every expression kind and every control structure the grammar has is in exactly one of two lists in `nvs fmt`, `LAID_OUT` and `AUTHORS_BREAKS` in `crates/nvs-fmt/src/chain.rs`. ([`tooling/fmt-every-construct-has-a-broken-layout`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-every-construct-has-a-broken-layout))
- **Every run between two tokens on one line is nothing or one space, decided by the two tokens' roles, and a formatted file lexes to the token kinds its source did** — Every whitespace run between two tokens on one line is decided by what the two tokens are, and it is either nothing or exactly one space. ([`tooling/fmt-one-run-between-two-tokens`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-one-run-between-two-tokens))
- **No two blank lines follow each other in code, and no blank line sits at the inside edge of a body, a list or a match arm list** — No two blank lines follow each other in code, and no blank line sits right after a line that ends in an opening `{`, `(` or `[`, or right before a line that starts with its closing `}`, `)` or `]`. ([`tooling/fmt-at-most-one-blank-line`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-at-most-one-blank-line))
- **A string literal is rewritten to single quotes unless it interpolates or contains a single quote, and heredoc bodies and comments are never touched** — A string literal is rewritten to single quotes, with two exceptions that both use double quotes instead: a literal that interpolates — only a double-quoted string or a heredoc can — and a literal containing a single quo… ([`tooling/fmt-quotes`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-quotes))
- **A comma-separated list that spans more than one line gets a trailing comma, and a list on one line never does** — Every comma-separated list that spans more than one line gets a trailing comma after its last element: call arguments, parameter lists, array literals, shape-type fields, anonymous objects, `match` arm lists including t… ([`tooling/fmt-trailing-commas`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-trailing-commas))
- **Consecutive `use` declarations are sorted by full path, ascending and case-sensitive, with no blank line between them** — Consecutive `use` declarations are sorted lexicographically by their full path, ascending and case-sensitive, with no blank line between them. - **Every construct PER never saw — qualifiers, `lateinit`, `fn` anonymous functions, `match`, anonymous objects, shape types, enum cases, html templates, a `?>` on its own line — has exactly one layout** — Each construct with no PER precedent has one layout, chosen once:… ([`tooling/fmt-novis-constructs`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-novis-constructs))
- **`nvs fmt` lower-cases a mis-cased reserved spelling only where that spelling has no other legal meaning — a duration unit and the open tag, never a keyword or an identifier** — `nvs fmt` normalizes a mis-cased reserved spelling to its lower-case form only where that mis-cased spelling has no other legal meaning. ([`tooling/fmt-normalizes-only-reserved-spellings`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-normalizes-only-reserved-spellings))
- **`nvs fmt` never inserts a visibility keyword** — `core-api/written-visibility` makes an omitted visibility keyword a compile error, and `nvs fmt` never inserts the keyword. ([`tooling/fmt-never-inserts-visibility`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-never-inserts-visibility))
- **`nvs fmt` never reorders class members, because declaration order is observable in what a program prints and sends** — Methods, properties, class constants and enum cases keep the order their author wrote when `nvs fmt` runs, because declaration order is observable: `core-classes/derive-property-list` makes a derived codec's encode orde… ([`tooling/fmt-never-reorders-members`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-never-reorders-members))
- **Class members have one order, and an editor action and `nvs code order` write it on request** — The body of a class and of an interface has one member order, the same in every project. ([`tooling/class-members-have-one-order`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-class-members-have-one-order))
- **`nvs fmt` is a fixed point over the input bytes: byte-stable on every machine, and deliberately not source-independent** — `nvs fmt` is a fixed point: reformatting its own output changes nothing, across the whole corpus. ([`tooling/fmt-is-idempotent`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-is-idempotent))
- **`nvs fmt` is a separate opt-in tool: no compiler command runs it, an unformatted file is never a diagnostic, and an editor composes it with quick fixes in the client** — Nothing wires `nvs fmt` into `nvs check`, `nvs run`, `nvs test` or any other compiler command. ([`tooling/fmt-is-never-a-diagnostic`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-is-never-a-diagnostic))
- **`nvs fmt` rewrites in place; `--check` writes nothing and exits non-zero naming every file that would change; `--diff` prints the diff instead** — `nvs fmt <path>...` rewrites the named files in place. ([`tooling/fmt-check-writes-nothing`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-check-writes-nothing))
- **`nvs fmt` exits `1` when a file would change and `2` when a file is refused** — `nvs fmt` exits `0` when it found nothing to report, `1` when `--check` or `--diff` found a file that would change, and `2` when a file was refused: it does not parse, or it could not be read or written. ([`tooling/fmt-exit-status-says-what-it-found`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-fmt-exit-status-says-what-it-found))
- **A doc comment is exactly `///`; `////` and longer runs are ordinary comments, and `#` never is one** — A line comment opened by exactly three slashes is a doc comment, lexed as its own trivia kind. ([`tooling/doc-comment-is-three-slashes`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-doc-comment-is-three-slashes))
- **A `///` run attaches to the declaration below it across no blank line, and a doc comment attached to nothing is a diagnostic** — A run of `///` lines is one doc comment, and it attaches to the next declaration. ([`tooling/doc-comment-attaches-to-the-next-declaration`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-doc-comment-attaches-to-the-next-declaration))
- **A doc comment is Markdown plus `@see` and `@example`, each of which must resolve, and any other `@tag` is a diagnostic** — The body of a doc comment is Markdown. ([`tooling/doc-comment-tags-are-see-and-example`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-doc-comment-tags-are-see-and-example))
- **Nothing requires a doc comment by default; `nvs check --strict-docs` reports a public member without one, and no autofix can satisfy it** — `nvs check` is silent about documentation. ([`tooling/strict-docs`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-strict-docs))
- **A `// TODO:` comment is a list the editor and `nvs check --todos` print, never a diagnostic, and `nvs check` has `--deny` and `--fix`** — A `//` line comment whose text, after the slashes and spaces, starts with `TODO:` in capitals is a todo, and the rest of the line is its text. ([`tooling/a-todo-is-a-comment-the-tools-list`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-todo-is-a-comment-the-tools-list))
- **`nvs doc <entry>` writes one Markdown page per class from the JSON and has no source of truth of its own** — `nvs doc <entry>` writes one Markdown page per class from the JSON `tooling/meta-json-takes-a-program` emits. ([`tooling/nvs-doc-renders-and-decides-nothing`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-nvs-doc-renders-and-decides-nothing))
- **`nvs meta --json` is the one machine-readable source of documentation, every renderer consumes it, and no renderer is authoritative for content** — `nvs meta --json` (`tooling/meta-json`) is the single machine-readable source of documentation, and every renderer consumes it:… ([`tooling/one-json-several-renderers`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-one-json-several-renderers))
- **`nvs meta --json` prints the whole `Core` registry as one JSON document, and a field with nothing written is an absent key rather than an empty one** — `nvs meta --json` prints the `Core` registry as one JSON document: every class with its members and its constants, and the enums beside them at top level — top level because the registry's roster is, an enum having no o… ([`tooling/meta-json`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-meta-json))
- **`nvs meta --json <entry>` emits that program's own declarations beside the `Core` registry, in the registry's own shape** — `nvs meta --json` with no argument prints the `Core` registry, a static compile-time table, exactly as `tooling/meta-json` states. ([`tooling/meta-json-takes-a-program`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-meta-json-takes-a-program))
- **`nvs agent` answers a coding agent from the registry and the embedded reference chapters in four commands, and the check loop is part of the surface** — `nvs agent` is the surface a coding agent reads the language through, and it is four commands that answer from what the binary already carries — the registry, and the reference chapters embedded in it: `primer` prints t… ([`tooling/an-agent-asks-the-binary`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-an-agent-asks-the-binary))
- **`nvs agent index` prints one derived line per registered member, carrying its signature and the capability it is gated on, and one per chapter heading** — `nvs agent index` prints exactly one line for every member the registry holds, one for every enum, exception and attribute beside them, and one for every chapter of the reference the binary embeds and every heading in it. ([`tooling/the-index-is-one-line-per-member`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-index-is-one-line-per-member))
- **`nvs agent index` carries one derived line per configuration key, command, flag and diagnostic code, and `find` reaches each by the name a user types** — `nvs agent index` carries one line for every configuration key, every command and subcommand, every flag, and every diagnostic code, beside its lines for members and headings, and `find` and `show` reach each of them un… ([`tooling/the-index-names-every-key-command-and-code`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-index-names-every-key-command-and-code))
- **Every diagnostic code carries a plain card that `nvs agent show` prints, and a terminal rendering names that command once** — Every diagnostic code carries a card beside its `Code::new` declaration: one to three plain sentences saying what the error means and how to fix it, and a short wrong-then-right example where the sentences alone would l… ([`tooling/a-diagnostic-code-carries-its-card`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-diagnostic-code-carries-its-card))
- **The primer is generated, and every example it shows and every diagnostic code it names is proven against the compiler that ships with it** — Every claim the primer makes is proven against the compiler that ships with it: each example in it is run and must print what the primer says it prints, and each diagnostic code it names must be one that compiler declar… ([`tooling/a-primer-claim-is-executed`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-primer-claim-is-executed))
- **`nvs agent init` writes one pointer per harness and keeps it current with the installed binary, and no adapter ever states a language fact** — `nvs agent init` installs the surface into a project by writing an `AGENTS.md` stanza, which is harness-neutral, and beside it what the coding agent that runs it needs — found from the environment variable that agent se… ([`tooling/an-adapter-carries-protocol-and-never-language`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-an-adapter-carries-protocol-and-never-language))
- **`nvs agent changes --since <version>` prints the changelog sections the binary carries, and a released binary carries its own** — `nvs agent changes` prints what changed between two versions of Novis, from `CHANGELOG.md` embedded whole in the binary. ([`tooling/nvs-agent-changes-prints-the-changelog`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-nvs-agent-changes-prints-the-changelog))
- **`nvs code` answers questions about one project by name from the editor's own index, reads every file, and only `rename`, `move` and `order` write** — `nvs code` has eleven verbs over one project.
