- **Usage telemetry and the update check are two independent opt-ins, both off by default, and neither ever implies the other** — Adoption is measured by two independent consents, both off by default. ([`tooling/telemetry-is-two-opt-ins`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-telemetry-is-two-opt-ins))
- **A counter is `invocation.<subcommand>` or `internal-error.<subcommand>` from the compiled-in command table, or its `unknown` bucket, the payload adds only `first` and `days_active` to the version, system and week, and nothing derived from traffic is ever counted** — Any `nvs` invocation may increment counters in the local file — a write, never a connection. ([`tooling/telemetry-counters-are-a-closed-set`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-telemetry-counters-are-a-closed-set))
- **`nvs telemetry show` prints the exact payload the next upload would send, and the schema, the endpoint contracts and the aggregated data are all published** — `nvs telemetry show` prints the exact payload the next upload would send, before anything is sent, and its bytes equal what the listener then receives. ([`tooling/telemetry-show-prints-the-payload`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-telemetry-show-prints-the-payload))
- **An upload carries only the previous finished week, rides a short-lived user-initiated command at most weekly, and a process that has bound a socket never uploads** — Only the **previous, finished week's** aggregate is ever sent — never a live stream — at most once a week, at a randomized point inside the eligible window. ([`tooling/a-serving-process-never-uploads`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-serving-process-never-uploads))
- **An upload gets three seconds, is abandoned with its counters kept when that expires or the collector asks to retry, is dropped when the collector refuses it, says so, and never changes the carrying command's exit status** — An upload has a **three-second budget** end to end. ([`tooling/a-failed-upload-never-fails-the-command`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-failed-upload-never-fails-the-command))
- **`nvs update-check` always reports the telemetry switch, the local and latest versions, and with telemetry on its upload history; `--json` is stable and the exit status is always 0** — `nvs update-check`'s output always carries whether telemetry is on or off, the local version and the latest released version. ([`tooling/update-check-states-the-whole-picture`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-update-check-states-the-whole-picture))
- **The telemetry collector is `apps/telemetry/`, a Novis program in this repository that names no host, and it runs and is tested end to end on one machine** — The service that receives telemetry is `apps/telemetry/`, a Novis web application in this repository, in the shape of `apps/notes/`. ([`tooling/the-telemetry-collector-is-a-novis-program`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-telemetry-collector-is-a-novis-program))
- **`POST /v1/report` accepts one JSON report of at most 4 KiB that matches the closed schema, and refuses anything else with a status the client acts on** — `POST /v1/report` takes one `application/json` body of at most 4 KiB, the exact bytes `nvs telemetry show` printed (`tooling/telemetry-show-prints-the-payload`), in the shape `tooling/telemetry-counters-are-a-closed-set… ([`tooling/a-telemetry-report-is-checked-against-a-closed-schema`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-telemetry-report-is-checked-against-a-closed-schema))
- **The collector adds each report to weekly totals per version, os and arch in one transaction, and never stores the report itself** — The collector adds an accepted report to running totals in one SQLite transaction, and the report is never written anywhere: not to a table, a file, a queue or a log. ([`tooling/the-collector-keeps-weekly-totals-only`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-collector-keeps-weekly-totals-only))
- **The collector never stores a sender's address: it limits the rate on a keyed hash held in memory, and its server and proxy write no address to any log** — No sender's address is written to disk, by the program, the Novis server or the TLS proxy in front of it. ([`tooling/the-collector-never-stores-an-address`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-collector-never-stores-an-address))
- **Every total the collector keeps is public, on server-rendered pages with no script, no cookie and no third-party request, and as JSON and CSV under CC0** — The collector publishes every total it keeps, and the project reads the same pages and files as anyone else. ([`tooling/telemetry-totals-are-public`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-telemetry-totals-are-public))
- **The repository's tools are one Bun + TypeScript program, `bun nv`, and `smol-toml` is its only runtime dependency** — Every tool that builds, checks, renders or drives this repository is a subcommand of one program, `bun nv <command>`, written in TypeScript and run by Bun at the version `package.json` pins. ([`tooling/the-repository-tools-are-one-bun-program`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-repository-tools-are-one-bun-program))
- **A fact a repository tool reads is one JSON record under `data/`, its type declared once and its text written by one writer** — A fact a repository tool reads — a goal, the chain, a rule's structure, a gap, a playbook bullet, a plan field — is one JSON file under `data/`, holding one entity. ([`tooling/a-repository-fact-is-one-json-record`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-repository-fact-is-one-json-record))
- **A file rendered from the records is committed, marked generated and never edited, and a conflict in one is resolved by rendering it again** — A file a tool writes from the records is committed, so GitHub and a reader without Bun see it. ([`tooling/a-rendered-file-is-committed-and-never-edited`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-rendered-file-is-committed-and-never-edited))
- **The chain in the goals README names the live goal, and a reached goal's file is deleted with none of its checks carried** — The loop's live goal is the first slug of the `chain:` list in the front matter of `docs/goals/README.md`, committed like every other file. ([`tooling/the-chain-names-its-live-goal`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-the-chain-names-its-live-goal))
- **A check runs only when the change reaches what its green runs were observed to use, and the pipeline runs and records on the one `covws` debug build** — The acceptance sweep, `bun nv verify`, `bun nv affected` and `bun nv proofs` start only the atoms a change reaches, read from what each atom's green runs were observed to use. ([`tooling/a-check-runs-only-when-the-change-reaches-its-footprint`](rules/tooling.md#tooling-a-check-runs-only-when-the-change-reaches-its-footprint))

## The editor

- **The resilient parse is the one grammar's AST plus a trivia layer and an offset index, never a second tree** — There is one grammar and one tree. ([`ide/one-grammar-one-tree`](rules/ide.md#ide-one-grammar-one-tree))
- **Every token and every trivium, concatenated in offset order, reproduce the file byte for byte** — Concatenating every token's and every trivium's source text, in offset order, must equal the file byte for byte. ([`ide/tokens-plus-trivia-reproduce-the-file`](rules/ide.md#ide-tokens-plus-trivia-reproduce-the-file))
- **A node the parser invented says so — `MemberName::Missing` and a spanned `ExprKind::Error` — and an empty span is never the signal** — Where a production synthesises a node at the point of a failure, the node says so. ([`ide/recovery-is-explicit`](rules/ide.md#ide-recovery-is-explicit))
- **The parser always returns a tree, a node it invented says so, and an offset maps to the innermost node even inside a malformed region** — A live editor spends most of its time on a syntactically invalid document — mid-statement, an unclosed brace, a half-typed identifier — so completion and hover that go dark on the first error rarely work when they matter. ([`ide/the-tree-survives-a-syntax-error`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-tree-survives-a-syntax-error))
- **Position encoding is negotiated, every offset conversion lives in `nvs-diagnostics`, and a document's bytes are never normalised** — Position encoding is negotiated per LSP 3.17: the server offers `utf-8` and `utf-16`, takes `utf-8` when the client's `general.positionEncodings` offers it, and falls back to `utf-16`, which is what VS Code sends. ([`ide/positions-have-one-home`](rules/ide.md#ide-positions-have-one-home))
- **`SyntaxIndex.at(offset)` answers the innermost node and its ancestors, and is rebuilt per analysis** — `SyntaxIndex` (`crates/nvs-syntax/src/index.rs`) is built by one walk over the tree and answers `at(offset) -> NodePath`: the innermost node containing the offset plus its ancestors. ([`ide/the-index-answers-the-cursor`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-index-answers-the-cursor))
- **A full re-analysis of a ~1,000-line document stays under a named bound, and the guard is a test rather than an assumption** — A full re-analysis of a ~1,000-line document stays under a named bound, and the guard has the shape `benches/abi-probe/tests/perf_guards.rs` already uses: a soft bound that warns and a hard bound, ten times it, that fai… ([`ide/a-full-reanalysis-stays-under-a-bound`](rules/ide.md#ide-a-full-reanalysis-stays-under-a-bound))
- **`nvs ast --json` has a frozen node schema, is resilient by default, and carries no literal's text, so it holds no `secret` bytes** — `nvs ast --json` has a frozen schema, because the AST panel needs a stable shape and `{stmts:#?}` — Rust's derived `Debug` — has none: any field reordering in any AST struct changes it. ([`ide/ast-json-schema-is-frozen`](rules/ide.md#ide-ast-json-schema-is-frozen))
- **`nvs-lsp` and `editors/vscode` are one crate and one package that grow in place; no prototype is built to be discarded** — `crates/nvs-lsp` and `editors/vscode` are one crate and one package, and every editor feature extends them in place. ([`ide/one-crate-and-one-extension-grow-in-place`](rules/ide.md#ide-one-crate-and-one-extension-grow-in-place))

- **The debugger UI is only as deep as the capabilities `nvs dap` reports, so the adapter's capability list is the debugger's scope** — `nvs dap` is wired into VS Code's existing debugger UI, and every feature below renders in a UI that already exists — it appears only if the adapter reports the corresponding capability at `initialize`. ([`ide/the-debugger-ui-is-as-deep-as-the-adapter`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-debugger-ui-is-as-deep-as-the-adapter))
- **Nothing but the protocol writes to the server's stdout; logging goes to stderr and `window/logMessage`** — stdio *is* the wire. ([`ide/stdout-belongs-to-the-protocol`](rules/ide.md#ide-stdout-belongs-to-the-protocol))
- **On a version mismatch at `initialize` the client says so in the status item and does not start** — `nvs lsp` reports its version at `initialize`. ([`ide/the-extension-refuses-a-binary-it-does-not-understand`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-extension-refuses-a-binary-it-does-not-understand))
- **Every process the extension starts runs from a verified copy of the binary that is never older than the build on disk, so the file the user named is never held** — The VS Code extension never runs the binary `nvs.path` or `PATH` names: every process it starts — the server, the Tasks, the formatter, the AST panel and the test controller — runs from a verified copy of that binary in… ([`ide/the-extension-runs-a-copy-of-the-binary`](rules/ide.md#ide-the-extension-runs-a-copy-of-the-binary))
- **The extension holds no language logic, and its `package.json` dependencies are checked against an allowlist by its own tests** — The extension may hold no language logic — no parser, no formatter, no type table — and this is enforced rather than intended: its `package.json` `dependencies` are checked against an allowlist by its own test suite, so… ([`ide/dependencies-are-allowlisted`](rules/ide.md#ide-dependencies-are-allowlisted))
- **The editor conceals a `secret` value by default, and the ranges come from the language server rather than a client guess** — A `secret` value is concealed in the editor by default. ([`ide/redaction-ranges-come-from-the-server`](rules/ide.md#ide-redaction-ranges-come-from-the-server))
- **Only the bytes are concealed — a literal token or an interpolation slot, never an identifier or an annotation** — A range is answered when it is a string, heredoc or `bytes` literal token whose static type carries `secret`, or an interpolation slot inside one whose interpolated expression does. ([`ide/redaction-covers-bytes-only`](rules/ide.md#ide-redaction-covers-bytes-only))
- **A reveal is per range, window-local, and does not survive the editor closing** — A reveal is per range, window-local, and dropped when the editor for that document closes. ([`ide/reveal-is-explicit-and-window-local`](rules/ide.md#ide-reveal-is-explicit-and-window-local))
- **What the editor's concealment cannot cover is written down, because a redaction trusted past its reach is worse than none** — The concealment is cosmetic, and what it cannot cover is written down and shipped in the tool's own documentation, because a redaction trusted past its reach is worse than none. ([`ide/redaction-does-not-reach`](rules/ide.md#ide-redaction-does-not-reach))
- **`tainted` ships no default editor decoration, and the marker is opt-in** — `tainted` gets a semantic-token modifier and **no default decoration**. ([`ide/tainted-has-no-default-decoration`](rules/ide.md#ide-tainted-has-no-default-decoration))
- **Hovering a `tainted` or `secret` value shows its path inside the method, from where the qualifier entered to the cursor with the launderer marked, and only the language server has the checker record it** — Hovering a value whose type carries `tainted` or `secret`, or an argument where such a value reaches a sink, shows the path the qualifier took inside the method: where it entered, each step that carried it, and the call… ([`ide/a-hover-shows-where-a-tainted-or-secret-value-came-from`](rules/ide.md#ide-a-hover-shows-where-a-tainted-or-secret-value-came-from))

## Testing

- **A test is a method marked `#[Test]`, and its table is built while compiling** — A test is an ordinary `public` method carrying `#[Test]`, on an ordinary class. ([`testing/test-attribute`](rules/testing.md#testing-test-attribute))
- **`nvs run` and `nvs build` lower no test, and `nvs check` type-checks every one** — A `#[Test]` method may be declared in any file — beside the class it tests, or in a separate tree. ([`testing/tests-never-reach-a-build`](rules/testing.md#testing-tests-never-reach-a-build))
- **Every test runs in its own isolate and shares nothing but compiled code with its siblings** — Each test runs on an isolate of its own: it shares compiled code with its siblings and nothing else — not a static, not a cache entry, not an open handle. ([`testing/isolate-per-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-isolate-per-test))
- **A test reaches `private` members of classes declared in its own file, and nowhere else** — A test method may reach `private` and `protected` members of classes declared **in the same file**. ([`testing/private-in-the-same-file`](rules/testing.md#testing-private-in-the-same-file))
- **An assertion names its subject first and compares two values of one type** — The assertion surface is static members on `Core\Test`, each taking its **subject first**: `assertEquals($actual, $expected)`, with one trailing options shape, nothing mutating and failure throwing. ([`testing/assertions-are-typed`](rules/testing.md#testing-assertions-are-typed))
- **A failed assertion is a catchable `Throwable` and a ledger entry the test cannot erase** — `Core\Test\Failure` is an ordinary `Throwable`, and catching one is not merely allowed but necessary: a composite assertion, a retry wrapper, a soft-assert block and any test *of* an assertion all need to intercept one. ([`testing/failure-ledger`](rules/testing.md#testing-failure-ledger))
- **The constructor is the test's setup, and there is no second before-hook** — The constructor is the test's setup, and a stronger one than a `setUp` method can be: definite property initialization guarantees every property is assigned before any test body runs. ([`testing/constructor-is-setup`](rules/testing.md#testing-constructor-is-setup))
- **`#[AfterEachTest]` runs on each attempt's own object, and is told which test ran and how it ended** — `#[AfterEachTest]` marks a `public` instance method returning `void`, and the runner calls it on the same object the test ran on, inside that test's isolate, after every attempt, whether the attempt passed or failed. ([`testing/after-each-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-after-each-test))
- **`#[Fixture]` is built once per class and injected into a test by the type it returns** — `#[Fixture]` marks a `public static` method, and what it supplies is its declared return type. ([`testing/fixtures`](rules/testing.md#testing-fixtures))
- **`#[BeforeClass]` and `#[AfterClass]` run once around a class's tests, and the second runs whenever the first started** — `#[BeforeClass]` and `#[AfterClass]` mark `public static` methods returning `void` that run once around a test class's tests, in the parent, and `#[AfterClass]` runs whenever `#[BeforeClass]` started. ([`testing/class-hooks`](rules/testing.md#testing-class-hooks))
- **A test class has at most one hook of each kind, and a subclass inherits hooks, fixtures and tests like any method** — A test class has at most one `#[BeforeClass]`, one `#[AfterClass]` and one `#[AfterEachTest]`, and a subclass inherits each of them, each `#[Fixture]`, each `#[Test]` and each `#[Property]` the way it inherits any method. ([`testing/hook-inheritance`](rules/testing.md#testing-hook-inheritance))
- **`nvs test` runs tests in parallel across every core, captures each test's output, and guarantees the hooks' order but not data consistency** — `nvs test` runs test isolates in parallel across every core, as many at once as `--jobs` allows, and `--jobs` defaults to the machine's hardware threads as it already does for `.nvst` cases. ([`testing/tests-run-across-every-core`](rules/testing.md#testing-tests-run-across-every-core))
- **`[limits] wall_time` bounds each test on its own, and `#[Test(timeout: ...)]` replaces it for one test** — Each test runs under a wall-time limit: `[limits] wall_time` applies to every test on its own, and `#[Test(timeout: "5s")]` replaces it for one test. ([`testing/a-test-has-a-wall-time-limit`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-test-has-a-wall-time-limit))
- **`#[Test(tags: [...])]` labels a test, `--tag`/`--skip-tag` select by label, and `--shard N/M` runs one of M stable disjoint parts** — `#[Test(tags: ["slow", "db"])]` labels a test, `--tag` and `--skip-tag` select by label, and `--shard N/M` runs the Nth of M disjoint parts of the selection. ([`testing/tags-and-shards-select-what-runs`](rules/testing.md#testing-tags-and-shards-select-what-runs))
- **`--fail-fast` stops starting tests after a failure, `--rerun-failed` runs the last run's failures, and `--shuffle` randomises start order with a printed seed** — `nvs test --fail-fast` stops starting tests after the first failure, `--rerun-failed` runs only the tests the last run failed, and `--shuffle` starts tests in a random order and prints the seed. ([`testing/a-run-can-stop-early-rerun-failures-and-shuffle`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-run-can-stop-early-rerun-failures-and-shuffle))
- **`nvs test --watch` reruns the selection each time a file the program requires changes** — `nvs test --watch` runs the selected tests, then runs them again each time a file the program requires changes, until it is interrupted. ([`testing/watch-reruns-on-an-edit`](rules/testing.md#testing-watch-reruns-on-an-edit))
- **`#[TestWith]` is matched against the parameters by name and by type, and each row is its own case** — `#[TestWith(...)]` carries an anonymous object that the checker matches against the method's parameters… ([`testing/data-rows`](rules/testing.md#testing-data-rows))
- **A double is a shape of callables, structurally checked against an interface** — A double is a shape of callables, structurally checked against an interface: `Core\Test::double<Clock>({now: fn(): Instant => ...})` **is** a `Clock` and may be passed wherever one is taken. ([`testing/doubles`](rules/testing.md#testing-doubles))
- **A call to a double is asserted after the exercise, never expected before it** — A double records the calls made to it, and the test asserts on that record afterwards with ordinary assertions, in the order the test reads: `Core\Test::assertCalled($mailer, Mailer::send, {times: 1, with: [...]})` and… ([`testing/interaction-after-the-fact`](rules/testing.md#testing-interaction-after-the-fact))
- **`at:` and `seed:` fix the clock and the generator of the test's own isolate** — `#[Test(at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z", seed: 42)]` fixes the clock and the random generator of that test's own isolate: `Core\Time::now()` answers exactly that instant, and the seeded generator and the identifier members d… ([`testing/determinism-declared-on-the-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-determinism-declared-on-the-test))
- **A task still running when a test returns fails that test** — The whole suite runs inside one task, so a test's isolate is a child of it and a `Core\Task::all` written in a test has a calling task to put its own children under. ([`testing/task-tree-and-virtual-clock`](rules/testing.md#testing-task-tree-and-virtual-clock))
- **`#[Test(db:)]` opens a transaction on the test's own context and rolls it back** — `#[Test(db: "test")]` opens a transaction against the named connection before the test and rolls it back after. ([`testing/db-transaction`](rules/testing.md#testing-db-transaction))
- **A test request is dispatched in-process through the compiled route table, and its input arrives `tainted`** — `Core\Test::request(...)` builds a request and runs it through the compiled route table and the real middleware chain — no socket, no port, microseconds per test. ([`testing/in-process-request`](rules/testing.md#testing-in-process-request))
- **One registered answer makes every outbound call in that test come from the table, and an unmatched one throws rather than reaching the network** — Once a test registers one answer with `Core\Test::answerHttp(string $url, uint $status, {json?, body?, headers?, tls?})`, **every** outbound call that test makes is answered from the table, and an unmatched one throws a… ([`testing/an-outbound-call-is-answered-from-a-table`](rules/testing.md#testing-an-outbound-call-is-answered-from-a-table))
- **`Core\Test`'s table answers a WebSocket handshake, plays the frames it was given and records what the program sent, and an unmatched socket throws rather than connecting** — A test answers an outbound socket from `Core\Test`'s table, never from a listener. ([`testing/an-outbound-socket-is-answered-by-a-scripted-peer`](rules/testing.md#testing-an-outbound-socket-is-answered-by-a-scripted-peer))
- **`#[Property]` derives its generators from the parameters' declared types** — `#[Property]` runs a method against generated inputs, and the generators are **derived from the parameters' declared types** by the same declaration walk a codec is derived from, user classes included. ([`testing/property-testing`](rules/testing.md#testing-property-testing))
- **A snapshot is a literal in the test body, and the updater rewrites that literal and nothing else** — `Core\Test::assertMatchesInline($value, "...")` holds the expectation in the source file, and `nvs test --update` splices the produced value into that literal. ([`testing/inline-snapshots`](rules/testing.md#testing-inline-snapshots))
- **A mutation run asks whether any test would have noticed the code being wrong** — A mutation run makes a small, deliberate change to the code, re-runs the tests, and records whether anything failed. ([`testing/mutation-testing`](rules/testing.md#testing-mutation-testing))
- **A test that asserts nothing fails, a skip states a reason, and a retry is reported flaky rather than green** — A test that asserts nothing fails — the ledger already knows the count, and `Core\Test::assertDoesNotThrow(callable)` is how a test states "this must merely not throw", explicitly. ([`testing/runner-is-strict`](rules/testing.md#testing-runner-is-strict))
- **One verdict, three renderings, a machine format owns stdout alone, and the JSON one locates every test it reports** — Human output is the default and is written as the run goes, which is what keeps a long suite legible. ([`testing/report-formats`](rules/testing.md#testing-report-formats))
- **`nvs test` writes line, function and branch coverage as lcov, Clover and Cobertura, from one hit table every context of the run counts into** — `nvs test --coverage-lcov <FILE>`, `--coverage-clover <FILE>` and `--coverage-cobertura <FILE>` write which lines and branches a program's `#[Test]` run reached, and a run may write any of them together. ([`testing/coverage-report`](rules/testing.md#testing-coverage-report))
- **`.nvst` proves the language; `#[Test]` is how a program written in Novis tests itself** — `.nvst` is a whole-program, expected-stdout conformance case, and it is how **Novis's own conformance to its specification** is proven. ([`testing/nvst-is-separate`](rules/testing.md#testing-nvst-is-separate))
- **A directory handed to `nvs test` that holds `.nvs` files is one program requiring every one of them in name order, and a file in it that requires the bootstrap gives it its `autoload` map** — A directory handed to `nvs test` that holds `.nvs` files is one program: the runner writes an entry that requires every `.nvs` file under the directory that no other file under it requires, subdirectories walked, in nam… ([`testing/a-directory-of-programs-is-one-test-program`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-directory-of-programs-is-one-test-program))
- **One slice writes all of a feature's proofs together** — One slice takes one feature and writes **all of its feature proofs together**. ([`testing/one-slice-is-one-feature`](rules/testing.md#testing-one-slice-is-one-feature))
- **`docs/examples/` is the only copy of every example, and the website reads it in place** — `docs/examples/` is the only copy of every example, and the website build reads it in place. ([`testing/examples-live-in-the-repository`](rules/testing.md#testing-examples-live-in-the-repository))
- **A website page lists the features it covers, and the session that changes one rereads and re-stamps its pages** — Every handwritten website page lists in `covers:` the proofs roster's ids of the features it explains, and `website/site.lock.json` records the hash each feature had when the page was last reread against it. ([`testing/website-pages-are-stamped`](rules/testing.md#testing-website-pages-are-stamped))
- **The website's Tools area has an overview and one page for each developer tool, every page about running a tool lives there, and a page that moved there leaves nothing behind** — The website has a Tools area, the fourth after Guides, Syntax and Reference and before In-Depth, with an overview page and one page for each developer tool: the debug viewer, the debugger, the profiler, the editor, the… ([`testing/the-tools-area-has-a-page-for-each-tool`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-tools-area-has-a-page-for-each-tool))
- **A terminal block on a website page shows commands run in a fixture and what `nvs` printed, and `bun nv site --check snippets` fails when the output changes** — A terminal block shows commands run in a fixture directory and what `nvs` printed for each, with its exit code. ([`testing/a-terminal-block-shows-what-nvs-printed`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-terminal-block-shows-what-nvs-printed))
- **A website replay plays what `nvs lsp` returned for its steps, and `bun nv site --check` fails when the server now returns something else** — A replay on a website page shows an editor session that turns one snippet's starting text into the snippet, and every answer it shows from the language server is one `nvs lsp` returned for those steps. ([`testing/a-replay-plays-what-the-language-server-returned`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-replay-plays-what-the-language-server-returned))
- **A website replay can rename, apply a code action, show the code lenses, the call hierarchy and a hover card, each recorded from `nvs lsp` and checked like a completion list** — A replay (`testing/a-replay-plays-what-the-language-server-returned`) has five more kinds of step. ([`testing/a-replay-renames-applies-an-action-and-shows-a-lens`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-replay-renames-applies-an-action-and-shows-a-lens))
- **A website debugger replay plays what `nvs dap` returned for a session's breakpoints and steps, and `bun nv site --check snippets` fails when it now returns something else** — A debugger replay on a website page shows a debug session over one snippet: where it stopped, the call stack, and the variables with their values. ([`testing/a-debugger-replay-plays-what-nvs-dap-returned`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-debugger-replay-plays-what-nvs-dap-returned))
- **A website screenshot is taken by `bun nv site --shoot` from a real run, and the text beside it fails `bun nv site --check shots` when the run would now show something else** — A screenshot on a website page is taken from a real run by `bun nv site --shoot`, and nothing else writes one. ([`testing/a-screenshot-is-taken-from-a-real-run`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-screenshot-is-taken-from-a-real-run))
- **A hostile case passes when nothing came apart, and a compile diagnostic is never a pass** — A hostile case is judged by a contract, never by frozen output. ([`testing/hostile-case-contract`](rules/testing.md#testing-hostile-case-contract))
- **A feature is finished when its feature proofs exist: a description, a test from both sides, three examples, a measured figure and its growth, an attack and its help in the binary** — A feature is finished when its **feature proofs** exist, not when it works. ([`testing/feature-proofs`](rules/testing.md#testing-feature-proofs))
- **The roster of features is read from the registry and the reference chapters, never kept as a list** — The roster of features is read from live sources and kept nowhere. ([`testing/roster-is-derived`](rules/testing.md#testing-roster-is-derived))
- **An example, an attack and a bench are attributed by path; a test is attributed by a marker** — An example, an attack and a bench are attributed by **where they sit**: the trees share one relative path per feature, so nothing has to be registered anywhere. ([`testing/proof-attribution`](rules/testing.md#testing-proof-attribution))
- **A proof that fails is fixed or recorded as a known gap, and never weakened** — An attack that breaks the member it was written against, and an example that disagrees with the binary, are the program working. ([`testing/a-failing-proof-is-fixed-or-recorded`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-failing-proof-is-fixed-or-recorded))
- **Every member of a capability-bearing class declares a capability or declares none, and there is no allowlist** — A class is **capability-bearing** when any of its members has a row in the capability table. ([`testing/capability-completeness-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-capability-completeness-test))
- **The third-party notice is committed, and a check fails when the lockfile moved without it** — `bun nv gen-attribution --check` regenerates the third-party notice and compares it, failing when the lockfile has moved and the notice has not. ([`testing/attribution-is-diffed-in-ci`](rules/testing.md#testing-attribution-is-diffed-in-ci))
- **`[debug] mode` is the ceiling as well as the default, and writing a trace or a profile is its own capability** — `[debug] mode` in `nvs.toml` states the default **and** the ceiling in one value: `[]` is off, and any subset of `coverage`, `branch`, `trace` and `profile` is a ceiling a request may narrow and can never widen. ([`testing/debug-mode-directive`](rules/testing.md#testing-debug-mode-directive))
- **Coverage, tracing and profiling are one per-request flag word checked at fixed probe sites, never a second compiled tier** — `Ctx` carries one small mutable bitset — coverage, branch, trace and profile — and codegen emits an unconditional load-and-branch against it at exactly two kinds of site, present in every compiled unit whether or not an… ([`testing/debug-probes`](rules/testing.md#testing-debug-probes))
- **Each probe starts and stops mid-request, and exports what existing tooling already reads** — `Core\Debug` starts and stops each probe from inside a request — coverage with an optional branch half, a trace to a named sink, a profile to another — and reads coverage back as a path-to-line-to- count map. ([`testing/debug-surface`](rules/testing.md#testing-debug-surface))
- **Under `nvs dap` the baseline compiler runs with a debug switch: every local is in a described stack slot and every statement is a stop site** — Under `nvs dap`, the baseline compiler compiles the program with one switch on, and nothing else sets it. ([`testing/a-debugged-program-is-compiled-with-a-debug-switch`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-debugged-program-is-compiled-with-a-debug-switch))
- **A stop pauses every task of the debugged request at its next stop site, suspends that request's deadlines, and leaves every other request running** — When a task of a debugged request or program reaches an armed stop site, every task of that request's tree stops at its own next stop site, and the debugger is told once, with each task as a thread. ([`testing/a-stop-pauses-the-whole-task-tree`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-stop-pauses-the-whole-task-tree))
- **The conformance suite runs with the probes on, and once per optimisation level** — The conformance suite runs **at least once with coverage and tracing probes enabled**, and **once per Cranelift optimisation level**, so neither is a shape only production ever takes. ([`testing/probes-on-is-a-tested-configuration`](rules/testing.md#testing-probes-on-is-a-tested-configuration))
- **Every redeclaration a subclass can write is a generated conformance cell, and every cell runs or is refused as its rule says** — Every way a subclass or an implementor can declare a member again over its parent's is a conformance case, generated from one table. ([`testing/redeclaration-matrix`](rules/testing.md#testing-redeclaration-matrix))
- **`[debug] store` is off by default and can only subtract, so no run mode or log level ever turns debug records on** — `[debug] store` decides whether debug records are persisted at all, is off by default, and can only subtract — no run mode, no log level and no other directive turns it on. ([`testing/writing-a-debug-record-to-disk-is-its-own-gate`](rules/testing.md#testing-writing-a-debug-record-to-disk-is-its-own-gate))
- **A debug record reaches the service through a sealed spool file that one writer owns, never over a socket** — A debug record reaches the service by being written to a file the writing core owns alone, never over a socket, and the service reads a spool file only once it has been sealed. ([`testing/the-debug-stream-reaches-the-service-through-the-disk`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-debug-stream-reaches-the-service-through-the-disk))
- **A request recorded in development keeps its method, path, query, headers, the body it read and its response, with the four credential headers and every field decoded into a `secret` property replaced before anything is written** — With `[debug] store` on, a request served in `development` records its method, path, query, headers and the body bytes the program read, up to `[limits] request_body`, and its response's status, headers and body, up to… ([`testing/a-recorded-request-keeps-its-input-with-credentials-replaced`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-recorded-request-keeps-its-input-with-credentials-replaced))
- **`nvs debug` runs the debug service for one data folder, and a development `nvs serve` with `[debug] store` on starts it and stops it on exit** — `nvs debug` runs the debug service — the ingester and the viewer — for one data folder, and a development `nvs serve` with `[debug] store` on starts it as a child process and stops it when the server exits. ([`testing/nvs-debug-is-the-service-and-a-development-server-starts-it`](rules/testing.md#testing-nvs-debug-is-the-service-and-a-development-server-starts-it))
- **The ingester owns every write to the index and runs without a browser, and the viewer only ever reads** — The ingester owns every write to the index and runs from the moment the service starts, whether or not a browser has ever connected; the viewer is a reader that never opens a log file, parses a line or scans a directory. ([`testing/the-ingester-runs-whether-or-not-anyone-is-looking`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-ingester-runs-whether-or-not-anyone-is-looking))
- **The debug index is one SQLite file whose tables hold every query the viewer makes, full-text search and exception groups included, and it forgets a request past `[debug] index_age` or `[debug] index_max`** — The index is one SQLite file, `debug/index.sqlite` in the data folder, whose tables hold every query the viewer makes, and the ingester deletes what is older than `[debug] index_age` or past `[debug] index_max`, the old… ([`testing/the-debug-index-holds-what-the-viewer-reads-for-a-bounded-time`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-debug-index-holds-what-the-viewer-reads-for-a-bounded-time))
- **A malformed line becomes a visible record and an unreadable file is quarantined under a backoff, so ingestion never stops** — A malformed line becomes a record that says so and an unreadable file is quarantined under a backoff, so nothing on disk can stop the ingester. ([`testing/a-bad-line-degrades-and-a-bad-file-is-quarantined`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-bad-line-degrades-and-a-bad-file-is-quarantined))
- **The viewer renders the correlated request stream and hands every artifact with an existing viewer to it** — The viewer renders the correlated request stream and the log, and every artifact that an existing tool already renders is handed to that tool rather than drawn. ([`testing/the-viewer-shows-the-stream-and-hands-off-every-artifact`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-viewer-shows-the-stream-and-hands-off-every-artifact))
- **The viewer searches the text of every request, dump, log line, query and exception, and a search can be saved and linked** — One search box searches the text of every request, dump, log line, query and exception in the index, and any search can be saved under a name and opened again from a link. ([`testing/the-viewer-searches-every-record-and-saves-a-filter`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-viewer-searches-every-record-and-saves-a-filter))
- **The viewer groups exceptions into one row per class and throw site, with its count, first and last time, and its requests** — The exceptions view shows one row per exception class and throw site, with how many times it was thrown, when it was first and last thrown, and links to the requests that threw it. ([`testing/an-exception-is-one-row-per-class-and-site`](rules/testing.md#testing-an-exception-is-one-row-per-class-and-site))
- **The viewer compares two requests side by side, and resends a recorded request to the development server only after the developer confirms** — Two requests open side by side with what differs marked, and a recorded request is sent again to the development server only after the developer confirms it in a dialog that names what will be sent. ([`testing/two-requests-compare-and-a-replay-asks-first`](rules/testing.md#testing-two-requests-compare-and-a-replay-asks-first))
- **Every `file:line` the viewer shows opens that line in the developer's editor, VS Code by default** — Every `file:line` the viewer shows is a link that opens that line in the developer's editor, through the editor's own URL scheme, and VS Code's `vscode://file/` is the default. ([`testing/a-site-in-the-viewer-opens-in-the-editor`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-site-in-the-viewer-opens-in-the-editor))
- **`nvs debug to-test` prints a `Core\Test::request` case from a recorded request that asserts its status, key headers and body, with a placeholder where the spool redacted a credential** — `nvs debug to-test <trace-id>` reads a recorded request and its response from the debug service's index and prints a test: one class with one `#[Test]` method that sends the same request through `Core\Test::request` (`t… ([`testing/a-recorded-request-becomes-a-test`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-recorded-request-becomes-a-test))
- **`#[Bench]` reports counted semantic work, and CI may gate on the counts but never on wall-clock** — `#[Bench]` reports counted semantic work — statements executed, calls made, allocations, bytes attributed, GC cycles — read off the same probe sites coverage and tracing use, in a counting mode beside their timing one (… ([`testing/bench-counters`](rules/testing.md#testing-bench-counters))
- **A per-PR guard and the historical dashboard are separate measurements, and never one** — Two performance measurements exist and they are never one. ([`testing/perf-two-mechanisms`](rules/testing.md#testing-perf-two-mechanisms))
- **A member's record is four counts that compare on any machine and one clock that compares on its own, re-measured only when its implementing file's code moves** — A member's record is four counts and one clock, taken in one sweep over one bench program. ([`testing/member-perf-ledger`](rules/testing.md#testing-member-perf-ledger))
- **The historical leg runs under callgrind on Linux or WSL, and nowhere else** — The historical leg runs under `valgrind --tool=callgrind`, which has no native Windows build, so it runs on Linux or WSL and nowhere else. ([`testing/valgrind-on-wsl`](rules/testing.md#testing-valgrind-on-wsl))
- **One workflow holds every job, and three lanes decide which of them a run needs** — One workflow file holds every CI job, and a schedule trigger plus a `full` flag decide which of them a given run needs. ([`testing/ci-lanes`](rules/testing.md#testing-ci-lanes))
- **One table decides what a diff runs, and the platform matrix is never one of the gates** — The first job compares the push's or the pull request's base against `HEAD` and emits one boolean per lane; every other job's `if:` is a single comparison against one of them. ([`testing/lane-table`](rules/testing.md#testing-lane-table))
- **A run with no base commit to diff against runs every lane** — A first push to a branch, a force-push and a shallow clone all leave the lane computation without a base commit it can diff against. ([`testing/unknown-base-runs-everything`](rules/testing.md#testing-unknown-base-runs-everything))
- **Miri, the fuzzers and the unsafe audit run nightly and at release, and the fuzz corpus persists** — The memory-safety and fuzzing evidence — the interpreter-under-Miri run, the fuzz smoke runs and the unsafe audit — runs in the nightly and at release, and not on a push. ([`testing/the-deep-lane`](rules/testing.md#testing-the-deep-lane))
- **A job a lane defers is skipped by its own `if:`, never filtered out of the workflow** — Every lane gate is a job-level `if:`, never a workflow-level path filter. ([`testing/a-deferred-job-is-skipped-never-absent`](rules/testing.md#testing-a-deferred-job-is-skipped-never-absent))
- **Each workflow has one run going on `main` at a time** — A run on `main` that a newer run of the same workflow replaces is cancelled, so `CI` and `Website` each have one run going on `main` at a time. ([`testing/one-run-on-main`](rules/testing.md#testing-one-run-on-main))

## Security and isolation

- **Running another script is an in-process isolate that shares nothing with its parent but compiled code** — `spawn script` runs another `.nvs` file — or a static method — as an isolated unit of work inside this process. ([`security/isolate-shares-nothing`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-shares-nothing))
- **A value crosses an isolate boundary as one graph copy, and a callable, an alias or a host handle does not cross at all** — Arguments in and the result out are **deep-copied, or moved when the refcount is 1** — the identical mechanism and identical restrictions as `spawn worker`. ([`security/isolate-values-cross-by-copy`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-values-cross-by-copy))
- **A request and everything it spawns share one budget, accounted at the tree's root** — A request and everything it spawns form one tree, and limits are accounted against the tree's root. ([`security/isolate-budget-is-the-trees`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-budget-is-the-trees))
- **A child isolate's failure arrives as data on the result and never unwinds into its parent** — A child's failure arrives as **data on the result**, never as an exception unwinding into the parent. ([`security/isolate-failure-is-a-value`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-failure-is-a-value))
- **An isolate's output is captured by default and carries the parent's sink carrier** — `output: 'capture'` is the default: the child's output lands on the result and is charged to the tree's `max_output`. ([`security/isolate-output-is-captured`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-output-is-captured))
- **An isolate ends by draining its roots through the one release worklist and then sweeping what a cycle held up** — When an isolate ends — returning, throwing, breaching a limit, or being cancelled — its context's roots are released through one iterative worklist. ([`security/isolate-teardown-is-a-drain-then-a-sweep`](rules/security.md#security-isolate-teardown-is-a-drain-then-a-sweep))
- **An isolate's arena is an ownership root, not an address range** — An isolate's arena is its context together with the set of values reachable from that context's roots. ([`security/arena-is-an-ownership-root`](rules/security.md#security-arena-is-an-ownership-root))
- **An inbound request is the root isolate of its own tree, and there is one isolate implementation** — There is a single `Isolate` type, and **an inbound HTTP request is the root isolate of a request tree**. ([`security/one-isolation-implementation`](rules/security.md#security-one-isolation-implementation))
- **Executing code is its own capability, a script in the app folder needs no grant, and the entry path is canonicalised and then prefix-checked** — Spawning an isolate asks `script.spawn`, a grant naming the roots that code may be executed *from*. ([`security/script-spawn-capability`](rules/security.md#security-script-spawn-capability))
- **Request, server and session state throws where there is no inbound request, rather than answering empty** — `Core\Request`, `Core\Server` and `Core\Session` **throw** where the context is answering no inbound request, rather than returning empty values. ([`security/request-state-throws-in-an-isolate`](rules/security.md#security-request-state-throws-in-an-isolate))
- **Nothing a request does is observable by another request except through an explicit, capability-gated store** — Nothing a request does is observable by another request except through an explicit, capability-gated store. ([`security/no-cross-request-state`](rules/security.md#security-no-cross-request-state))
- **Four doors are closed by construction, and no configuration reopens any of them** — Four mechanisms that dynamic web runtimes commonly have are absent from Novis by construction: native code loading (`security/no-ffi`), scheme dispatch on a path (`security/a-path-is-not-a-url`), cross-request state (`s… ([`security/closed-doors`](rules/security.md#security-closed-doors))
- **No userland mechanism loads native code into the process** — There is no `FFI`-equivalent, no `com_dotnet`-equivalent, and no mechanism by which userland code causes native code to be loaded into the process. ([`security/no-ffi`](rules/security.md#security-no-ffi))
- **There is no `eval`, and no `Core` member compiles a string produced at run time** — There is no `eval`, no string-argument `assert`, and no `Core` member that compiles and runs a string produced at run time. ([`security/no-eval`](rules/security.md#security-no-eval))
- **A path is a filesystem path: no member dispatches on a scheme prefix, and nothing may register one** — No `Core` member that takes a path interprets a scheme prefix, and there is no registry by which userland or an extension adds one. ([`security/a-path-is-not-a-url`](rules/security.md#security-a-path-is-not-a-url))
- **A reflective call faces exactly the visibility check ordinary code at that site would, and there is no `setAccessible`** — Reading **metadata** — a member's existence, name, declared type, visibility, attributes, doc comment — is always available, because that is introspection of the program's *shape*. ([`security/reflection-enforces-visibility`](rules/security.md#security-reflection-enforces-visibility))
- **Reflection and AST parsing are capability-free, because neither reaches the world outside the process** — Reflection and source parsing are pure in-memory operations over a program's own compiled shape or its own supplied string. ([`security/reflection-needs-no-capability`](rules/security.md#security-reflection-needs-no-capability))
- **The capability check lives inside the function that performs the effect, and that door is the only way out of the process** — The check is **not** a line in a member's body that an author remembers to write, **not** at the call site in emitted code, and **not** in a dispatcher. ([`security/capability-check-at-the-door`](rules/security.md#security-capability-check-at-the-door))
- **A capability question is a grant and a scope, asked of the request's own configuration snapshot** — At the point of a call the question has exactly two parts: the **grant** — is this capability present at all in the effective configuration — and the **scope** — does *this argument* fall inside what was granted: a path… ([`security/capability-question-is-grant-and-scope`](rules/security.md#security-capability-question-is-grant-and-scope))
- **What each `Core` member needs is declared once in one table, and nothing at run time reads it** — What each `Core` member needs is declared once, in one table: a class, a member, and an optional capability, with one row for each capability a member can ask. ([`security/capability-declaration-is-one-table`](rules/security.md#security-capability-declaration-is-one-table))
- **Every capability name that exists is on one roster, and a name outside it is refused where it is written** — Every capability name that exists is on one roster, in one place, with the reasoning for what it permits named beside it. ([`security/capability-roster-is-closed`](rules/security.md#security-capability-roster-is-closed))
- **Authority is a property of the namespace enclosing the code, never of the nesting depth or the name being called** — Authority is the namespace **enclosing the code**, not the nesting depth of the statement and not the name being called. ([`security/authority-is-the-enclosing-namespace`](rules/security.md#security-authority-is-the-enclosing-namespace))
- **The application's grant table is `[grants]` in its own `package.toml`, keyed on namespace prefixes, and a capability it names must be on the roster** — The application's grant table is keyed on namespace prefixes and is the `[grants]` table of the application's own `package.toml` (`packaging/package-toml-is-a-tool-input`), never a package's manifest. ([`security/grants-are-keyed-on-a-namespace`](rules/security.md#security-grants-are-keyed-on-a-namespace))
- **The longest matching grant key wins, and a subtree is spelled out because it reaches code that does not exist yet** — Lookup reuses the resolution rule a developer already learned. ([`security/longest-prefix-wins`](rules/security.md#security-longest-prefix-wins))
- **A namespace matching no grant line holds the application's own authority, and a fetch leaves nothing unmatched** — A namespace matching no grant line holds what the application holds — the operator's ceiling. ([`security/an-unmatched-namespace-holds-the-application`](rules/security.md#security-an-unmatched-namespace-holds-the-application))
- **A path scope is canonicalise-then-prefix over whole components, and a path that does not exist yet is its deepest existing ancestor** — A path-bearing capability resolves by one comparison: **canonicalise both sides, then compare whole components.** Before either, the argument is judged by its text: a Windows alias (`errors/path-component-refusals`) is… ([`security/path-scope-canonicalise-then-prefix`](rules/security.md#security-path-scope-canonicalise-then-prefix))
- **A read, a write, a removal, a stat or a listing walks its resolved path one level at a time from the root, following no link, so the grant it checked is the path it acts on** — A door that opens a file resolves its path once, checks the grant on that resolved path as it is written, and opens it one level at a time from the root, each level from the handle of the one above it, following no link. ([`security/writes-open-beneath-a-handle`](rules/security.md#security-writes-open-beneath-a-handle))
- **A denied capability is a catchable `RuntimeError` naming the capability, never a fatal** — A denied capability throws a `RuntimeError`, and a program may catch it and degrade. ([`security/denial-is-a-runtime-error`](rules/security.md#security-denial-is-a-runtime-error))
- **A capability is required or optional, and only a required one refuses to build** — A package's manifest splits what it asks for into `required` and `optional`. ([`security/optional-capability-degrades`](rules/security.md#security-optional-capability-degrades))
- **Two layers enforce a capability and only the static one grants; nothing anywhere widens** — Two layers enforce a capability. ([`security/no-runtime-grant`](rules/security.md#security-no-runtime-grant))
- **A member that needs no capability pays nothing, and one that does pays only beside a syscall** — A member that needs no capability pays nothing at all: no table lookup, no branch, no field on its row, no code emitted at its call sites. ([`security/capability-costs-nothing-unasked`](rules/security.md#security-capability-costs-nothing-unasked))
- **A dependency's authority is granted by the application one line at a time, and a declaration grants nothing** — A package **declares** what it requests, split into required and optional. ([`security/package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time`](rules/security.md#security-package-authority-is-granted-one-line-at-a-time))
- **Running a program needs `process.exec` in server work, and there is no shell to interpolate into** — Running another program is a capability, `process.exec`, asked at the door (`security/capability-check-at-the-door`). ([`security/process-exec-capability`](rules/security.md#security-process-exec-capability))
- **`net.connect` carries an address policy that denies the private ranges, and an exception is one written IP address** — `net.connect` is not a boolean and not merely a host list. ([`security/net-address-policy`](rules/security.md#security-net-address-policy))
- **The grant follows what the program is doing rather than the transport: reaching out is `net.connect`, binding is `net.listen`, and neither widens the other** — Which network capability an opening asks is decided by **what the program is doing**, not by which transport it does it over. ([`security/net-listen-is-a-separate-grant-from-net-connect`](rules/security.md#security-net-listen-is-a-separate-grant-from-net-connect))
- **The address policy lives in the capability, so every client obeys it and none of them may hold its own** — Every client — the HTTP client, the raw socket layer, a program-supplied database target, and any socket a host import hands to an extension — is subject to the same policy, enforced at the point the connection is made… ([`security/the-policy-lives-in-the-capability`](rules/security.md#security-the-policy-lives-in-the-capability))
- **`tainted` is a compile-time qualifier on `string`, `bytes` and a shape of them, spellable in any declaration and erased before codegen** — `tainted string` and `tainted bytes` join the type grammar as a qualified form of the two scalar types, and `tainted {…}` writes the same fact over a whole shape of them. ([`security/tainted-qualifier`](rules/security.md#security-tainted-qualifier))
- **Every accessor that hands a program bytes from outside answers the `tainted` form, and the list of them is enumerable** — Every member of the request, server, session, environment and CLI accessors, and a script's own arguments, answers the `tainted` form of whatever it already returned. ([`security/tainted-sources`](rules/security.md#security-tainted-sources))
- **A tainted operand poisons every operation it takes part in, and only a checked conversion launders for free** — Any operation combining a tainted operand with an untainted one — concatenation, interpolation, a string member, an array of scalars — produces a tainted result. ([`security/taint-propagation`](rules/security.md#security-taint-propagation))
- **A `string` or `bytes` parameter is a sink when its content becomes an instruction a parser executes** — That one line derives every worked case, which is the test of it being the right predicate rather than a restatement. ([`security/sink-predicate`](rules/security.md#security-sink-predicate))
- **A `Core` parameter nobody classified refuses a tainted argument, and refuses to ship at all** — A `Core` member whose `string`/`bytes` parameter carries no classification **rejects a tainted argument**. ([`security/unclassified-parameter-refuses-tainted`](rules/security.md#security-unclassified-parameter-refuses-tainted))
- **Every grammar the library parses is a sink, and none of the four gets a launderer** — The library parses exactly four grammars — a regex pattern, a format template, a date pattern, and a byte-packing format — and every one of them is an instruction under `security/sink-predicate`. ([`security/every-grammar-is-a-sink`](rules/security.md#security-every-grammar-is-a-sink))
- **A regex pattern is a sink with no launderer; the subject is data and may be tainted** — A regex **pattern** requires the plain, unqualified `string`. ([`security/regex-pattern-is-a-sink`](rules/security.md#security-regex-pattern-is-a-sink))
- **An outbound URL or address is a sink, and a tainted one is refused where it is written** — The URL parameter of an HTTP client's request members, and the address parameter of a raw connect, are unqualified: a `tainted` value at either position is a compile-time diagnostic, exactly as at a query text parameter. ([`security/outbound-url-is-a-sink`](rules/security.md#security-outbound-url-is-a-sink))
- **A metric label value refuses `tainted`, and there is deliberately no launderer for one** — A metric label value is a sink: a query parameter, a header, a path segment or a database column cannot become a label. ([`security/metric-label-refuses-tainted`](rules/security.md#security-metric-label-refuses-tainted))
- **A log field is data, so it takes a tainted value and wants one** — A log field is data: the writer is a structured serializer, so a field is framed by the serializer and never by string concatenation into a line. ([`security/log-is-not-a-sink`](rules/security.md#security-log-is-not-a-sink))
- **The only way out of `tainted` is a `Core` member whose contract names the one sink it is safe for** — Short of a checked conversion, the only way to remove `tainted` is a `Core` member whose contract states which **one** sink it is safe for: an HTML escape for HTML text, an identifier quote for a dynamic table or column… ([`security/launderers-are-sink-named`](rules/security.md#security-launderers-are-sink-named))
- **A launderer answers its sink's carrier when that sink launders on its own and the transform is not idempotent, and a plain type otherwise** — A `Core` member that removes `tainted` answers its sink's **carrier type** rather than the plain type when **both** hold: its sink launders automatically — a value reaches that sink and is transformed with no call writt… ([`security/launderer-answers-a-carrier`](rules/security.md#security-launderer-answers-a-carrier))
- **Capturing a sink yields that sink's carrier, never a plain `string`** — Capturing output answers **the carrier of the sink in force**, not a plain `string`. ([`security/capture-answers-the-carrier`](rules/security.md#security-capture-answers-the-carrier))
- **A route capture is laundered by the parameter's own type, and a `string` capture stays tainted** — Every capture in a route path corresponds to a parameter of the same name, and the parameter's declared type is what the segment is converted to during matching. ([`security/route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type`](rules/security.md#security-route-capture-is-laundered-by-its-type))
- **A derived codec adds no qualifier rule, a JSON decoder fills a `secret` property, and a call that encodes one does not compile** — A derived codec introduces no qualifier rule of its own. ([`security/derived-codec-qualifiers`](rules/security.md#security-derived-codec-qualifiers))
- **`Core\Taint::assertTrusted` is the one generic way out, and it carries a written reason at the call site** — `Core\Taint::assertTrusted(tainted string, string $reason): string` is the one generic escape from the qualifier, for the case where the developer has validated the value themselves and needs to say so. ([`security/assert-trusted`](rules/security.md#security-assert-trusted))
- **A response body is written by one typed member, and mixing `echo` with one of them does not compile** — A response body is written by one of seven typed members, each owning a body shape and setting its own content type. ([`security/response-body-is-one-typed-member`](rules/security.md#security-response-body-is-one-typed-member))
- **A pooled database connection is proven clean before it is reused, and a failed reset destroys it** — A connection released at request teardown returns to a per-core pool, and **a released connection is reset before it is reusable**. ([`security/db-pool-reset-is-a-boundary`](rules/security.md#security-db-pool-reset-is-a-boundary))
- **A pooled LDAP connection is bound as its block for its whole life, and `authenticate` binds on a connection of its own** — A pooled `Ldap\Connection` is bound as its block's identity for its whole life, and `authenticate` binds on a connection of its own and closes it. ([`security/ldap-pool-is-bound-as-its-block`](rules/security.md#security-ldap-pool-is-bound-as-its-block))
- **A simple bind with an empty password or a NUL byte in it is refused by the client before it is sent** — A simple bind with an empty password, or with a password that contains a NUL byte, is refused by the client before a byte of the password is sent, as the error kind `InvalidCredentials`. ([`security/ldap-empty-password-is-refused`](rules/security.md#security-ldap-empty-password-is-refused))
- **An LDAP bind without TLS needs `tls = "none"` in the block and the host on `[capabilities.ldap] cleartext`** — A simple bind is sent over TLS — LDAPS, or StartTLS on `ldap://` — unless the block or `Ldap\Settings` says `tls = "none"` and the host is on `[capabilities.ldap] cleartext`. ([`security/ldap-cleartext-bind-is-granted-per-host`](rules/security.md#security-ldap-cleartext-bind-is-granted-per-host))
- **`secret` is a second, independent compile-time qualifier, written before `tainted` and in that order alone** — `secret` is a second, independent compile-time qualifier on `string` and `bytes`. ([`security/secret-qualifier`](rules/security.md#security-secret-qualifier))
- **Nothing grants `secret` ambiently; it appears where a developer wrote it, and at one member that is its own contract** — Unlike `tainted`, **nothing in Novis grants `secret` ambiently.** The five host accessors are why `tainted` can attach itself automatically — every one is a named, enumerable place untrusted data enters (`security/taint… ([`security/secret-has-no-ambient-source`](rules/security.md#security-secret-has-no-ambient-source))
- **A `secret` operand poisons its own axis independently of `tainted`, and a checked conversion strips it** — Any operation combining a `secret` operand with a non-`secret` one produces a `secret` result — the poisoning shape `security/taint-propagation` defines, applied to this axis **independently**. ([`security/secret-propagation`](rules/security.md#security-secret-propagation))
- **Every output sink refuses a `secret` value outright, and no auto-escape or neutralisation bypasses one** — Every **output** sink refuses a `secret` value, and no neutralisation bypasses one: HTML and response output refuse outright with no auto-escape, terminal output refuses with no carrier bypass, a log field refuses, a se… ([`security/secret-sinks-refuse`](rules/security.md#security-secret-sinks-refuse))
- **A `secret` value is refused at the one graph copy, so it reaches neither `serialize` nor any spawn** — A `secret` value is refused at the one recursive graph-copy operation, for both of its callers alike — serialization to bytes and every crossing into a task, a worker or an isolate — rather than drawing a new distinctio… ([`security/secret-crosses-no-boundary`](rules/security.md#security-secret-crosses-no-boundary))
- **Comparing two `secret` values with `==` lowers to a constant-time helper, decided by the compiler** — `$provided == $expected`, where both operands are statically `secret`, lowers to a **constant-time** comparison helper rather than the short-circuiting one every other operand pair uses. ([`security/secret-comparison-is-constant-time`](rules/security.md#security-secret-comparison-is-constant-time))
- **A `secret` operand is compared but never rendered, and no flag lifts the redaction** — An assertion diff is simultaneously output, a log line, a dump and a `Throwable` message — all four of the things a `secret` value may not become (`security/secret-sinks-refuse`). ([`security/secret-in-a-test-report`](rules/security.md#security-secret-in-a-test-report))
- **No rendering the toolchain itself produces prints a `secret` in the clear, the AST dump included** — A `secret` value may not become output, a log line, a dump or a `Throwable` message (`security/secret-sinks-refuse`), and the toolchain is held to the bar it enforces on everyone else: no command this project ships prin… ([`security/redaction-reaches-the-tools-own-renderings`](rules/security.md#security-redaction-reaches-the-tools-own-renderings))
- **Everything an extension manifest may declare is a restriction, so a hostile manifest cannot make a calling program less safe** — Every declaration an extension manifest may carry is a **restriction**: it either rejects a call that would otherwise compile, or adds a qualifier the caller must discharge. ([`security/extension-manifest-only-tightens`](rules/security.md#security-extension-manifest-only-tightens))
- **An extension's files and outbound HTTP are the intersection of its entry's grant, its manifest's request and its caller's own grant** — What an extension may read, write or call at a given moment is the **intersection** of three sets, each of which only narrows: what the operator grants on the extension's own `[[extension]]` entry, what the extension's… ([`security/extension-grants-are-an-intersection`](rules/security.md#security-extension-grants-are-an-intersection))
- **An extension call is an ordinary operation for taint, so contagion is the default and needs no declaration** — An extension call is an ordinary operation for the purposes of taint. ([`security/extension-contagion`](rules/security.md#security-extension-contagion))
- **An extension manifest may declare exactly two things: a parameter that refuses `tainted`, and a return that is always `tainted`** — A manifest may say two things, and only these two. ([`security/extension-declares-sink-or-source`](rules/security.md#security-extension-declares-sink-or-source))
- **No extension may remove the `tainted` qualifier, in any manifest spelling** — There is **no manifest form** whose declared effect removes `tainted`. ([`security/extension-cannot-launder`](rules/security.md#security-extension-cannot-launder))
- **A `secret` value is refused at every extension boundary, in either direction** — A `secret` value passed to an extension is a compile-time diagnostic, and no manifest may declare a `secret` return. ([`security/secret-does-not-cross-an-extension`](rules/security.md#security-secret-does-not-cross-an-extension))
- **The image component declares no qualifier deviation and requests no capability** — The image component declares **no qualifier deviation**: ordinary contagion is exactly right, so a thumbnail of a `tainted` upload is `tainted` and reaches HTML output through the existing sinks like any other value, wh… ([`security/image-component-declares-nothing`](rules/security.md#security-image-component-declares-nothing))
- **There is one TLS client in the tree, and a driver reaches it over a generic transport rather than building a second** — There is one TLS client in the tree, with one answer to "whose certificates do you believe" and one place a configured anchor bundle plugs into. ([`security/one-tls-client`](rules/security.md#security-one-tls-client))
- **Verification is relaxed only where a `capabilities.tls` grant names the host and the call asks for it, and no such grant has a `true` spelling** — Certificate verification on an outbound call is strict by default and is relaxed only when two independent things agree: a `[capabilities.tls]` grant names the host, and the call itself asks. ([`security/tls-trust-is-relaxed-only-under-a-host-grant`](rules/security.md#security-tls-trust-is-relaxed-only-under-a-host-grant))
- **A closed roster of application-layer security protocols lives in `Core`, and nothing joins it without meeting the test** — A closed roster of application-layer security protocols lives in `Core`: signed and encrypted cookies (authenticated encryption only, with key rotation), CSRF tokens, TOTP, JWT — signed and verified under a shared key,… ([`security/protocol-roster`](rules/security.md#security-protocol-roster))
- **Three conditions and one boundary decide what may join the roster, and a flow never does** — Three conditions must all hold for a protocol to belong in `Core`. ([`security/protocol-admission-test`](rules/security.md#security-protocol-admission-test))
- **The algorithm comes from the key and never from the token** — The algorithm comes from the key, never from the token. ([`security/algorithm-comes-from-the-key`](rules/security.md#security-algorithm-comes-from-the-key))
- **A JWT without an expiry, or past one, fails verification, and no flag disables the check** — A JWT without an expiry, or past one, fails verification. ([`security/jwt-expiry-is-mandatory`](rules/security.md#security-jwt-expiry-is-mandatory))
- **Verification answers a value or throws, and no member exposes a raw comparison for the caller to get wrong** — Verification returns claims or throws. ([`security/verification-throws-and-compares-in-constant-time`](rules/security.md#security-verification-throws-and-compares-in-constant-time))
- **A verified signature proves origin, not safety: claims come back `tainted`** — Claims returned from token verification are **`tainted`**. ([`security/verification-does-not-launder`](rules/security.md#security-verification-does-not-launder))
- **`Core\Jwe` speaks compact JWE with `A256GCM` alone, and the static that built the key picks the algorithm** — `Core\Jwe` reads and writes compact JWE with `A256GCM` alone, and the static that built the key is what picks the key-management algorithm. ([`security/jwe-compact-subset`](rules/security.md#security-jwe-compact-subset))
- **A token another party issued verifies against a key found by `kid`, never one that is tried, and its claims come back as a `tainted` shape** — `Core\Jwt` verifies a token another party issued against a key it **finds** by `kid`, never one it tries, and answers the claims as a `tainted` shape. ([`security/jws-issued-subset`](rules/security.md#security-jws-issued-subset))
- **The server refuses an unsafe verb without a valid CSRF token, and the opt-out is written on the route itself** — The server refuses an unsafe verb — the four that change state — without a valid token, using the match it already made to know which handler is which. ([`security/csrf-is-on-by-default`](rules/security.md#security-csrf-is-on-by-default))
- **The compiler proves a route's access decision was written, never that it was honoured** — The compiler verifies that a route's access attribute is there and that the name inside it resolves. ([`security/access-is-checked-for-presence-not-meaning`](rules/security.md#security-access-is-checked-for-presence-not-meaning))
- **A span is rejected when it ends with a directional scope still open, decided by two counters** — Nine code points open or close a directional scope: four embedding and override forms closed by one terminator, and three isolate forms closed by another. ([`security/bidi-predicate`](rules/security.md#security-bidi-predicate))
- **The lexer refuses an unterminated control and the sinks substitute it, and nobody writes a second predicate** — The predicate has one implementation and several callers. ([`security/bidi-boundaries`](rules/security.md#security-bidi-boundaries))
- **Zero-width characters, homoglyphs and the full bidirectional algorithm are deliberately outside the check** — Three neighbouring hazards are deliberately outside the check, and saying so is what stops a future session from adding a fourth mechanism. ([`security/bidi-scope-is-the-whole-target`](rules/security.md#security-bidi-scope-is-the-whole-target))
- **`hash` writes Argon2id and nothing else, and no member takes an algorithm argument** — Hashing writes one algorithm and nothing else, and **no member gains an algorithm argument**. ([`security/hash-writes-argon2id-only`](rules/security.md#security-hash-writes-argon2id-only))
- **A stored password hash is read from a roster of exactly two shapes, and the roster grows only by amendment** — Verification accepts exactly two stored shapes: the modern hash this library writes, and a bcrypt hash under the `$2y$`, `$2a$` or `$2b$` prefix — one algorithm under three tags, verified identically. ([`security/bcrypt-read-roster`](rules/security.md#security-bcrypt-read-roster))
- **`needsRehash` measures weaker rather than different, so every bcrypt hash asks to be rewritten** — `needsRehash` answers whether the stored hash is **weaker** than what hashing writes now, not whether its parameters differ. ([`security/needs-rehash-answers-weaker`](rules/security.md#security-needs-rehash-answers-weaker))
- **A stored bcrypt cost above 17 is refused before any work is done** — A stored bcrypt hash carries its own cost, and the cost is the base-2 logarithm of the round count — a CPU-time lever one `UPDATE` away from anyone who can write the table. ([`security/bcrypt-cost-ceiling`](rules/security.md#security-bcrypt-cost-ceiling))
- **bcrypt's 72-byte truncation is replicated exactly, because the stored row was written under it** — bcrypt hashes at most 72 bytes of a password and stops at a NUL byte. ([`security/bcrypt-truncation`](rules/security.md#security-bcrypt-truncation))
- **A stored value outside the read roster throws, and the message never quotes the bytes** — A stored value outside the read roster — garbage, a refused prefix, or a hash naming any other algorithm — **throws** rather than answering `false`, and the message never quotes the bytes (`security/secret-sinks-refuse`). ([`security/an-unreadable-stored-hash-throws`](rules/security.md#security-an-unreadable-stored-hash-throws))
- **A session id the store did not issue is rejected, always, with no toggle** — `Core\Session::start()` accepts a presented id only if its own store issued it and it is still live. ([`security/a-session-id-the-store-did-not-issue-is-rejected`](rules/security.md#security-a-session-id-the-store-did-not-issue-is-rejected))

## Concurrency

- **Concurrency is the `Core\Task` roster over the runtime's own single scheduler** — Concurrency is `Core\Task` and nothing else. ([`concurrency/one-scheduler`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-scheduler))
- **Every task is a child of the task that started it, shares that request's accounting, and dies with it** — Every task starts as a child of the task that started it. ([`concurrency/a-child-belongs-to-the-calling-task`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-child-belongs-to-the-calling-task))
- **A child spawned `on: "worker"` is started on another core first and on its parent's core last, copies at every node in both directions, and is still its parent's child** — A child spawned `on: "worker"` is **started** on a core other than its parent's whenever one is idle, and on its parent's own core only when every other core is busy. ([`concurrency/on-worker-runs-the-child-on-another-core`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-on-worker-runs-the-child-on-another-core))
- **`Core\Task::all` answers a shape with the argument's own field names, each field keeping its own type** — `Core\Task::all({...}, {limit?, deadline?}): S` takes a shape whose every field is a zero-argument callable, runs them concurrently, and answers **a shape with the same field names, each field carrying that field's own… ([`concurrency/all-answers-a-typed-shape`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-all-answers-a-typed-shape))
- **An `all` field answers its own callable's declared return type, and a callable declaring none answers `mixed`** — Each field of a `Core\Task::all` argument answers **its own callable's declared return type**. ([`concurrency/an-all-field-answers-what-its-callable-declares`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-an-all-field-answers-what-its-callable-declares))
- **`Core\Task::map` answers an array of the callback's own return type, in the input's keys and order** — `Core\Task::map(array<T> $items, callable $fn, {limit?, deadline?}): array<U>` runs one callback per element concurrently. ([`concurrency/map-preserves-keys-and-order`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-map-preserves-keys-and-order))
- **`{limit, deadline}` is the whole of what bounds a group, and there is no `timeout` member and no `race`** — `all` and `map` take one trailing options shape with the same two fields. ([`concurrency/limit-and-deadline-are-the-only-bounds`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-limit-and-deadline-are-the-only-bounds))
- **Control never leaves `all` or `map` with a child still running** — `all` and `map` do not return while a child is still running. ([`concurrency/nothing-is-still-running-when-a-call-returns`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-nothing-is-still-running-when-a-call-returns))
- **A cancelled task runs no `catch`, no cleanup and no handler, and cancellation is not a `Throwable`** — A cancelled task is torn down by the runtime where it parked. ([`concurrency/cancellation-runs-no-user-code`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cancellation-runs-no-user-code))
- **A deadline bounds when cancellation is asked for, not when the call returns** — A `deadline` bounds when cancellation is **requested**, not when the call returns. ([`concurrency/a-deadline-bounds-the-cancel-not-the-return`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-deadline-bounds-the-cancel-not-the-return))
- **`Core\Task::afterResponse` runs once the response is complete, still charged to the request tree** — `Core\Task::afterResponse(callable $fn, {deadline?}): void` registers work to run once the request is done with:… ([`concurrency/after-response-outlives-the-connection`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-after-response-outlives-the-connection))
