- **Only the request's own task may defer work, and deferred work may not defer more** — Only the request's own task may register deferred work. ([`concurrency/only-the-request-registers-deferred-work`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-only-the-request-registers-deferred-work))
- **Deferred work may read the request but not write the response, and its uncaught throw reaches the log alone** — The response is on the wire before deferred work runs, so **the deferred callable may not touch it**. ([`concurrency/deferred-work-cannot-write-the-response`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-deferred-work-cannot-write-the-response))
- **`[deferred]` carries two bounds: a `System` `max_concurrent` and a `Runtime` `deadline`** — which is a host-sizing decision and not a request-local one, so a request cannot raise it. ([`concurrency/deferred-is-bounded-by-two-directives`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-deferred-is-bounded-by-two-directives))
- **Past `[deferred] max_concurrent`, `afterResponse` throws at the call site rather than queueing** — Past `[deferred] max_concurrent`, `Core\Task::afterResponse` throws a `RuntimeError` **at the call site**. ([`concurrency/a-full-deferred-executor-throws`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-full-deferred-executor-throws))
- **A value outlives the request that made it only by being put into a named store** — A value outlives the request that made it only by being **put into a named store**. ([`concurrency/cross-request-state-is-explicit`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cross-request-state-is-explicit))
- **`Core\Cache::memory()` is one store per serving process, coherent across its cores, capped in `nvs.toml` and gone when the process ends** — `Core\Cache::memory()` hands back one store per **serving process**: coherent across every core of that process, held in memory only, capped by `[cache.memory] max_size`, and gone when the process ends. ([`concurrency/the-memory-tier-is-one-store-per-process`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-memory-tier-is-one-store-per-process))
- **The cache boundary is a copy in and a copy out, so nothing a program can reach is read-modify-write** — What crosses the cache boundary is a copy in and a copy out. ([`concurrency/put-and-get-are-the-whole-boundary`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-put-and-get-are-the-whole-boundary))
- **A value is copied into the cache and copied back out, by the same graph copy the isolate boundary uses** — `put` copies a value out of the request heap into the cache; `get` copies one back in. ([`concurrency/a-cached-value-is-copied-across-the-boundary`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-cached-value-is-copied-across-the-boundary))
- **A cross-request store's bytes go on a balance of their own, and no request is charged or credited for them** — A request is measured against its own allocations, so the bytes of a store that outlives requests move a balance of their own and no request is charged or credited for them. ([`concurrency/a-cross-request-stores-bytes-are-its-own-balance`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-cross-request-stores-bytes-are-its-own-balance))
- **Anything a program relies on the value of goes to the shared tier, and the memory tier is not offered for it** — The memory tier is coherent across the cores of one process and no further: a second process on the same machine, or a machine beside it, finds nothing the first wrote, and any entry may be absent at any time. ([`concurrency/the-memory-tier-cannot-hold-what-must-be-coherent`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-memory-tier-cannot-hold-what-must-be-coherent))
- **A secret reaches a cache only as ciphertext, through `putSecret` and `getSecret` and a key ring** — A `secret` value meets a cache through exactly two members — `putSecret(string $key, secret string $value, Duration $ttl, array<secret bytes> $keys)` and `getSecret(string $key, array<secret bytes> $keys, {fill?, wait?}… ([`concurrency/a-secret-is-cached-only-sealed`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-secret-is-cached-only-sealed))
- **On a miss, one caller per process runs `fill` while the others wait, and a failure is never shared** — On a miss, `getSecret`'s `fill` runs in **exactly one caller per process**, in that caller's own request and under its own capabilities, while every other caller on every core waits for it — each for at most its `wait`,… ([`concurrency/a-secret-fill-runs-once-per-process`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-secret-fill-runs-once-per-process))
- **A persistent connection is a root isolate, and the request that upgraded it ends** — An upgraded connection is a **root isolate**, not a suspended request: its own arena, its own globals and statics, its own `[limits]` budget, its own capability grants, and its own entry in the timeline and the metric s… ([`concurrency/a-connection-is-a-root-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-is-a-root-isolate))
- **An upgrade names compiled code — a file or a static method — and never a callable** — `Core\Socket::upgrade('sockets/chat.nvs', args: {room: $room})` takes a spawned script's operand and nothing else: a file path, resolved and root-checked exactly as that construct's is, or a static method written `Chat:… ([`concurrency/an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-an-upgrade-is-spawn-shaped))
- **An upgrade's `args`, `limits`, `grants` and `on` are a spawned script's options as ordinary named arguments** — An upgrade takes `args`, `limits`, `grants` and `on` — the same four options a spawned script spells after its operand, with identical meaning and identical spelling (`limits: {memory: "8M"}`). ([`concurrency/an-upgrades-options-are-spawn-scripts`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-an-upgrades-options-are-spawn-scripts))
- **Inside a connection, code is an ordinary loop, and `receive()` answering `null` is what ends it** — Inside a connection, code is an ordinary loop — `while (var $msg = $conn->receive()) { … }` — with no handler interface, no event registration and no second control-flow style. ([`concurrency/a-connection-is-a-loop`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-is-a-loop))
- **`receive()` is the one wait, and it answers the peer or a subscribed topic, whichever arrives first** — `receive()` is the **one** wait a connection takes, and it answers whichever of two sources arrives first: a frame from the peer, or a value published to a topic this connection subscribed to (`core-classes/topic`). ([`concurrency/receive-is-the-one-wait`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-receive-is-the-one-wait))
- **What a peer sent arrives `tainted`, and `Core\Validate` is the only way to launder it** — A received frame's payload arrives `tainted`. ([`concurrency/a-peer-frame-is-tainted`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-peer-frame-is-tainted))
- **A stream that ends with its response is a streaming response; one that outlives it is a connection isolate** — The line between a streaming response and a connection is **what the stream outlives**, and it is worth stating sharply because it is the one place two spellings could appear for one job. ([`concurrency/a-stream-that-outlives-its-request-is-a-connection`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-stream-that-outlives-its-request-is-a-connection))
- **`Core\Socket` and `Core\Sse` are two hand-overs onto one isolate, and each reports the one it is missing** — `Core\Socket::upgrade` and `Core\Sse::upgrade` open the same isolate through two different hand-overs, so a request carries **two cells and not one**. ([`concurrency/two-doors-one-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-two-doors-one-isolate))
- **Every bound on an open connection is finite with nothing configured** — Every bound on an open connection is finite before anything is configured: connections per process, maximum frame size, maximum message size, idle timeout, total lifetime, send timeout and subscriber queue depth. ([`concurrency/connection-bounds-are-finite`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-connection-bounds-are-finite))
- **An open connection runs to completion on the code it started with, and an edit reaches only the next one** — A connection isolate holds the compiled unit it started with. ([`concurrency/a-connection-keeps-its-compiled-unit`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-connection-keeps-its-compiled-unit))
- **A shutdown or a reload closes a connection with a defined code after a drain, never with a reset** — A graceful shutdown and a configuration reload close connections with a defined code after a drain period, so a client's reconnect logic sees a clean close rather than a reset. ([`concurrency/a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-drain-closes-a-connection-cleanly))
- **A `push` on the queue's connection commits with the write that caused it, or neither happens** — `Core\Queue::push` on the queue's own connection enlists in whatever transaction that connection already has open. ([`concurrency/enqueue-commits-with-your-write`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-enqueue-commits-with-your-write))
- **`Core\Queue`'s four request-path members are each asked about a job or about a queue, never about a row number** — `Core\Queue` is `push`, `status`, `cancel` and `stats` — the four members a request asks, and the four that take no capability. ([`concurrency/queue-four-members`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queue-four-members))
- **A `tag` names a group of jobs and a `key` admits one pending job, and they are two columns because they are opposites** — `push`'s `tag` names a group of jobs and `key` admits at most one pending job, and they are two columns because they are opposites at the point they touch. ([`concurrency/a-tag-groups-jobs-and-a-key-dedupes-them`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-tag-groups-jobs-and-a-key-dedupes-them))
- **A job names a script file, and its payload crosses as a copied value** — A job names a script file — not a class, not a callable, not a static method. ([`concurrency/a-job-names-a-file`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-names-a-file))
- **A job's budget and grants are recorded when it is enqueued, and narrowed from that context rather than widened** — `push` takes the job's `limits` — the memory, CPU and time its isolate may spend — and its `grants`, and both are recorded with the row. ([`concurrency/a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-jobs-budget-and-grants-are-recorded-at-enqueue))
- **A worker claims a job with one statement the database arbitrates, so a fleet needs no lease protocol** — A worker claims a job with a single statement that selects the oldest due job in its queues and marks it in the same moment: `for update skip locked` on PostgreSQL and MySQL, `readpast` on SQL Server, and an immediate t… ([`concurrency/claiming-is-one-statement`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-claiming-is-one-statement))
- **A job between attempts is `Pending`, and there is no `Failed` state to ask about** — `Queue::State` is `Pending`, `Claimed`, `Succeeded`, `Dead` and `Cancelled`. ([`concurrency/a-job-between-attempts-is-pending`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-between-attempts-is-pending))
- **Delivery is at-least-once, and idempotency is the job's own obligation** — A job may run twice, and that is stated rather than implied. ([`concurrency/delivery-is-at-least-once`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-delivery-is-at-least-once))
- **Attempts are finite, backoff is exponential and jittered, and an exhausted job is kept rather than discarded** — A job's attempts are finite with nothing configured, because an unbounded retry is an unbounded wait wearing a different name. ([`concurrency/attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-attempts-are-finite-and-a-dead-letter-is-kept))
- **A job that exceeds its budget is a failed attempt, reported as that and retried like any other** — A job that exceeds its memory, CPU or time budget has had a **failed attempt**. ([`concurrency/a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-budget-overrun-is-a-failed-attempt))
- **`cancel` answers whether it won the race, and it changes the job's state rather than deleting the row** — `cancel` answers a `bool`, and the `bool` says whether *this* call is what took the job out of the queue. ([`concurrency/cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-cancel-is-a-race-it-can-lose))
- **A queue row is removed by `delete` or `purge`, never while claimed, and never dead-lettered or pending unless the call says so** — A queue row is removed by `delete`, which names one job by its receipt, or by `purge`, which names a queue and a filter — and neither ever removes a claimed job, a dead-lettered one, or a pending one unless the call say… ([`concurrency/queue-deletion-is-explicit-and-bounded`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queue-deletion-is-explicit-and-bounded))
- **A job runs as a root isolate, and there is no second execution path** — A job runs as a **root isolate**: its own arena, its own budget, its own grants, sharing only compiled code. ([`concurrency/a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-job-runs-as-a-root-isolate))
- **Which process runs a job is configuration, and every spelling drives the identical isolate** — Whether jobs run inside the server process or in a worker of their own is configuration, not a different mechanism. ([`concurrency/who-runs-a-job-is-configuration`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-who-runs-a-job-is-configuration))
- **`nvs serve` runs the accept loop, the schedule ticker and the queue's workers in one process, and the drain stops all three** — `nvs serve` is one process running three things — the accept loop, the `[[schedule]]` ticker and the queue's workers — on the scheduler it already turns, and the drain stops all three. ([`concurrency/one-process-serves-requests-schedules-and-jobs`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-process-serves-requests-schedules-and-jobs))
- **A durable payload refuses `secret`, and a `tainted` value comes back `tainted`** — A durable row is an output, and an output refuses `secret` (`security/secret-qualifier`). ([`concurrency/a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-payload-refuses-secret-and-keeps-its-qualifiers))
- **A `push` on a connection other than the queue's is not transactional, and is counted rather than assumed away** — A `push` issued while a transaction is open on a *different* connection than the queue's is not transactional. ([`concurrency/foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-foreign-connection-enqueue-is-counted))
- **An idle queue worker asks its queue once a second, and a push in the same process wakes it once the job is committed** — A queue worker that finds no due job waits one second before it asks the database again, and a `Core\Queue::push` in the same process wakes it as soon as the job is committed. ([`concurrency/a-push-wakes-an-idle-worker`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-push-wakes-an-idle-worker))
- **Queued work is durable, retried and declared by the application; scheduled work is a clock tick and none of those** — Two things run outside a request, and they are not variants of one mechanism. ([`concurrency/queued-work-is-not-scheduled-work`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-queued-work-is-not-scheduled-work))
- **There is no broker backend and no pluggable driver, because a driver makes transactional enqueue optional** — There is no Redis, NATS, SQS or AMQP backend, and no pluggable driver interface. ([`concurrency/no-broker-and-no-driver-interface`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-no-broker-and-no-driver-interface))
- **A connection is one future, driven to completion by the coroutine that owns it** — A connection is one future, and the coroutine that accepted it drives that future to completion in a loop of *clear the flag, poll, park*. ([`concurrency/one-future-per-connection`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-future-per-connection))
- **A waker decides nothing; it is permission to make one more poll happen** — Waking sets an atomic flag and, if a permission is installed, delivers it. ([`concurrency/a-waker-is-one-permission-to-poll`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-waker-is-one-permission-to-poll))
- **One wake permission is installed per drive, and a fresh one is issued only after it fires** — A wake permission is taken per **drive**, not per park. ([`concurrency/one-permission-per-drive`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-one-permission-per-drive))
- **A wake from another core queues an id on the task's own core and never migrates it** — What crosses a thread boundary is a task id and a poke of one core's poller, and nothing else — no reference to a scheduler, a stack or an arena. ([`concurrency/a-wake-never-moves-a-task`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-wake-never-moves-a-task))
- **A wake handle dropped unused wakes its task, unless that task is the one dropping it** — A wake handle dropped unused wakes the task it names, unless that task is the one dropping it. ([`concurrency/a-handle-given-up-by-its-task-wakes-nothing`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-handle-given-up-by-its-task-wakes-nothing))
- **A cancellation ends the drive: torn down where it parked, or told once and answered** — A cancellation ends the drive. ([`concurrency/a-cancelled-drive-never-parks-again`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-cancelled-drive-never-parks-again))
- **Where a drive parks is decided once when it starts, and off a core it blocks the thread** — Where a drive parks is decided once, when it starts, because a task never migrates and so the answer cannot change underneath it. ([`concurrency/the-park-route-is-chosen-once`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-park-route-is-chosen-once))
- **A task registers before it suspends, treats a wake as a hint, and leaves the reactor holding nothing when it ends** — Five rules govern a task that waits on I/O, and the first two are ordering rules a reader will otherwise get backwards. ([`concurrency/the-parking-contract`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-parking-contract))
- **A stream issues the syscall first and parks only on `WouldBlock`, so a warm socket pays nothing** — A read is: issue the syscall; on success return; on `WouldBlock` register, suspend, and loop. ([`concurrency/try-the-syscall-then-park`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-try-the-syscall-then-park))
- **The reactor reports readiness on every platform, Windows included, so a stream is written once** — The reactor reports **readiness**, never completion, on every platform: epoll on Linux, kqueue on the BSDs and macOS, and on Windows a poll of `\Device\Afd` through the completion port, which turns it into a readiness s… ([`concurrency/the-reactor-reports-readiness`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-the-reactor-reports-readiness))
- **A parking stream is a plain `Read` and `Write`, so nothing up the call chain is coloured** — A parking socket implements nothing but `std::io::Read` and `std::io::Write`. ([`concurrency/a-stream-is-an-ordinary-io-stream`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-stream-is-an-ordinary-io-stream))
- **A task's stack is 1 MiB of reserved address space, resident only where it is touched, and pooled per worker** — A task's stack is 1 MiB of **reserved** address space with a guard page. ([`concurrency/a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-task-stack-is-reserved-wide-and-pooled))
- **A task's recursion limit is armed from the real bounds of the stack it was handed** — A task's recursion limit is armed from the base and length of the stack it was actually handed, not asserted from a compiled-in ceiling. ([`concurrency/a-tasks-recursion-limit-comes-from-its-own-stack`](rules/concurrency.md#concurrency-a-tasks-recursion-limit-comes-from-its-own-stack))

## The Core API

- **`Core` means always present, so nothing outside Tier 0 may register a name under it** — Nothing outside Tier 0 may register a class under the `Core` namespace, and nothing whose presence a build flag can remove is registered there at all. ([`core-api/core-means-always-present`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-core-means-always-present))
- **A library candidate is placed by six ordered tests, not by PHP's extension list** — A candidate for the standard library is placed by six tests, applied in order, rather than by where another library happened to put it. ([`core-api/tier-placement`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-tier-placement))
- **A candidate lands in exactly one of five placements: Core, Native, Ext, Dropped or answered** — The six tests (`core-api/tier-placement`) put a candidate in exactly one of five places:… ([`core-api/five-placements`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-five-placements))
- **Every subsystem's tier is recorded once in the roster, including the ones no milestone has built** — Every subsystem has a recorded placement, including the ones no milestone has scheduled, because an entry nobody will build is more useful named than pending. ([`core-api/tier-roster`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-tier-roster))
- **The `Core` namespace is the compiler's: nothing may declare under it and its rosters are closed while compiling** — `Core` and everything nested under it is reserved. ([`core-api/reserved-namespace`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-reserved-namespace))
- **No class under `Core` can be extended or implemented, and a `Core` instance member checks its receiver's class** — No `extends` or `implements` clause may name a class under `Core`, and the link pass refuses each one as `E0329` before any type is checked. ([`core-api/core-classes-are-sealed`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-core-classes-are-sealed))
- **A domain class is a singular noun and its object types nest under it** — A domain class is named with a singular noun, and the object types it constructs nest under it: `Core\Time`, `Core\Time\Instant`, `Core\Time\Duration`. ([`core-api/a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-domain-class-is-a-singular-noun))
- **Every `Core` member obeys the same twenty shape rules, R1–R20** — Every member of every `Core` class obeys all twenty shape rules below. ([`core-api/shape-rules`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-rules))
- **The subject is parameter 1 of every `Core` member, with no exceptions** — The thing a member operates on is its first parameter, including where the member also takes a callback or a needle: `Arr::map($array, $fn)`, `Str::replace($subject, $search, $replacement)`, `Arr::contains($haystack, $n… ([`core-api/subject-first`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-subject-first))
- **A member's verb predicts its return type, and `…OrNull`, `…Safe`, `…Ex` and every `try…` but `tryParse` are banned** — One verb means one thing, so a member's name predicts its return type. ([`core-api/verb-lexicon`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-verb-lexicon))
- **A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name, and which pair to reach for is a rule rather than taste** — A symmetric operation gets a symmetric name: `encode`/`decode`, `split`/`join`, `pack`/`unpack`, `escape`/`unescape`, `trimStart`/`trimEnd`, `startsWith`/`endsWith`, `indexOf`/`lastIndexOf`, `first`/`last`. ([`core-api/symmetric-names`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-symmetric-names))
- **One name has one signature, and two behaviours need two names** — One name has one signature. ([`core-api/one-name-one-signature`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-name-one-signature))
- **A member name is a full word; only a class name may abbreviate, and only from a closed list** — A member name is a full word. ([`core-api/members-are-full-words`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-members-are-full-words))
- **An identifier's casing is fixed by its category and a mismatch is a hard compile error** — Every user-written identifier is checked against exactly one pattern for its category, and a mismatch is a hard compile error — not a lint, not a warning. ([`core-api/identifier-casing`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-identifier-casing))
- **Only the leading character's case is checked, so `HTTPClient` and `HttpClient` both pass** — Only the first character's case is checked. ([`core-api/casing-checks-the-leading-character`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-casing-checks-the-leading-character))
- **There is no suppression mechanism for a casing error, in any category** — There is no configuration, no per-project override and no suppression annotation for a casing error. ([`core-api/casing-has-no-suppression`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-casing-has-no-suppression))
- **Every member declaration writes exactly one visibility keyword, and there is no implicit `public`** — Every member declaration in a class, interface or anonymous-class body writes exactly one of `public`, `protected` or `private` — properties, class constants and methods alike, including a property carrying only `readon… ([`core-api/written-visibility`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-written-visibility))
- **An asymmetric property writes both halves, so a bare `private(set)` does not compile** — An asymmetric property writes both halves: `public private(set) string $name;`. ([`core-api/asymmetric-visibility-is-a-pair`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-asymmetric-visibility-is-a-pair))
- **`var $x;` and a bare `int $x;` in a class body report the missing visibility, not a statement error** — A class body containing `var $x;`, a bare `int $x;` or a bare `static int $x;` reports the missing visibility and names what to write, rather than falling through to the local-declaration grammar and reporting something… ([`core-api/legacy-property-shapes-name-the-visibility`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-legacy-property-shapes-name-the-visibility))
- **A constructor parameter is not a member, because visibility is what promotes one** — A constructor parameter carrying no visibility is a plain parameter, complete and correct, and the missing-visibility error does not fire on it. ([`core-api/a-parameter-is-not-a-member`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-parameter-is-not-a-member))
- **A class participates in a wire format only where it writes so, never structurally** — A class takes part in a wire format only where it says so. ([`core-api/written-participation`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-written-participation))
- **Every `Core` member declares whether it is a sink, a launderer, contagious or neutral** — Every `Core` member states, as a column of its signature rather than as a footnote, whether it is a… ([`core-api/qualifier-behaviour-is-declared`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-qualifier-behaviour-is-declared))
- **No `Core` member mutates its argument and none takes a reference** — No `Core` member mutates an argument and none takes a reference. ([`core-api/nothing-mutates`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-nothing-mutates))
- **Every `Core` value type is immutable, so no mutable twin exists to choose between** — Every `Core` value type is immutable, so there is no mutable twin to choose between. ([`core-api/no-mutable-immutable-twins`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-mutable-immutable-twins))
- **No `Core` member reads ambient state: there is no default timezone, locale, array pointer or error global** — No `Core` member reads state the call site did not give it. ([`core-api/no-ambient-state`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-ambient-state))
- **A `Core` member throws on failure and returns `?T` for absence; `false` is never an answer** — A `Core` member signals failure by throwing. ([`core-api/failure-throws`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-failure-throws))
- **No operation is reachable two ways, and a domain class's statics never mirror an object's own methods** — One operation is reachable exactly one way. ([`core-api/one-paradigm-per-operation`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-paradigm-per-operation))
- **A scalar and an `array<T>` never gain methods** — A scalar and an `array<T>` never gain methods. ([`core-api/no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-methods-on-scalars-or-arrays))
- **A mode is an enum, never a string or an integer constant, and only four grammars are exempt** — A member never takes a mode as a string or as an integer constant. ([`core-api/no-mode-strings`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-mode-strings))
- **A unit is a type: a duration is a `Duration` and a size is `uint` bytes** — A quantity carrying a unit is a type, not a number with a convention attached. ([`core-api/units-are-types`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-units-are-types))
- **A `string` member never takes an encoding argument** — No member taking a `string` takes an encoding argument. ([`core-api/no-encoding-argument`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-encoding-argument))
- **Every range is `(offset, ?length)`, and a negative counts from the end** — Every member taking a range takes `(offset, ?length)`, and `Core\Str` and `Core\Arr` share the convention exactly. ([`core-api/one-range-convention`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-range-convention))
- **A callback always receives `($value, $key)`, and may declare fewer parameters than the call site passes** — A callback a `Core` member invokes always receives `($value, $key)`, in that order, and a callable may declare fewer parameters than the call site passes (`types/callable-arity`). ([`core-api/callback-receives-value-and-key`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-callback-receives-value-and-key))
- **Every `Core` parameter is callable by the name its signature writes, and that name is compatibility surface** — Every parameter of every `Core` member may be written by name at the call site — the `$name` the member's signature writes in `nvs meta --json`, and the trailing bag under the one name `options` — under exactly the rule… ([`core-api/parameters-are-callable-by-name`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-parameters-are-callable-by-name))
- **A member's optional knobs are one trailing anonymous object, never a flag or a bitmask** — After the subject come the required arguments in dataflow order, and then **at most one** trailing optional anonymous object (`types/object-top`) whose shape is declared as a `type` alias. ([`core-api/options-bag`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-options-bag))
- **Required, optional and nullable are three separate questions: nullability belongs to the type and optionality to the default** — "Does `?T` mean the key may be absent, or that `null` is a legal value?" has a better answer than choosing: they are separate questions, and both already have a spelling. ([`core-api/required-optional-and-nullable`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-required-optional-and-nullable))
- **An options bag tells an omitted key from a written `null`** — A call site's two ways of not giving an options-bag field a value are two different requests. ([`core-api/omission-is-not-a-written-null`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-omission-is-not-a-written-null))
- **A bag or shape field is nullable exactly when its omission fills the never-written marker** — A field of an options bag or of a shape arm carries a default, and that default is what an omitting call site materializes. ([`core-api/a-nullable-field-omits-as-the-never-written-marker`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-nullable-field-omits-as-the-never-written-marker))
- **Wherever a `Core` member admits a written `null` it means remove, and `""` is never a removal spelling** — Wherever a `Core` member admits a written `null` — a bag field or an ordinary argument — it means… ([`core-api/a-written-null-removes`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-written-null-removes))
- **The never-written marker is not in the type system and is never handed to user code** — The never-written marker is not a value a program can hold, observe or name. ([`core-api/the-marker-never-reaches-a-program`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-the-marker-never-reaches-a-program))
- **The three-state bag changes which constant fills a slot and nothing else about the ABI** — The three-state bag changes *which constant fills one slot, for one kind of field*, and nothing else. ([`core-api/the-bag-abi-is-unchanged`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-the-bag-abi-is-unchanged))
- **The registry is the only source of a Core member, and a field it has not written is absent** — The registry is the only source of a `Core` member's surface and its reference documentation: its signature, its parameter names and types, its qualifiers, its options and its card (`core-api/reference-card`). ([`core-api/field-wise-precedence`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-field-wise-precedence))
- **A fixed-key shape parameter is one type carrying its arms, and it is only ever a whole parameter** — A required, positional, fixed-key shape parameter is declared as **one type carrying a non-empty list of arms**, each arm an ordered field list: one arm for the ordinary case, two or more for a discriminated union. ([`core-api/shape-parameter`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-parameter))
- **A shape's arms are pairwise disjoint, so exactly one accepts a written anonymous object and no field is declared a discriminant** — A written anonymous object is checked by asking which arm accepts it, where an arm accepts when the object's keys are exactly that arm's required keys plus any subset of its optional ones, each value assignable to its f… ([`core-api/shape-arms-are-disjoint`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-arms-are-disjoint))
- **The options bag and the shape parameter are two registry spellings of one checked type** — The trailing options bag and the fixed-key shape parameter are two registry spellings that intern into… ([`core-api/one-checked-shape-type`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-checked-shape-type))
- **A shape argument flattens into one argument per field of the merged list, so no shape exists at run time** — A shape argument expands at the call site into **one argument per field of the merged field list**: the arms in declaration order, each arm's fields in declaration order, a name a previous arm already emitted skipped. ([`core-api/shape-flattens-at-the-abi`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-flattens-at-the-abi))
- **A shape key reuses the options bag's two diagnostics, and a missing required key is an ordinary type mismatch** — A shape key reuses the options bag's two diagnostics, widened from "option" to "shape key": an argument that is not a written anonymous object, and a key the member does not declare. ([`core-api/shape-reuses-the-option-diagnostics`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-shape-reuses-the-option-diagnostics))
- **Anything with a lifetime is an object, and `Core` never hands back a handle** — Anything with a lifetime is an object. ([`core-api/a-lifetime-is-an-object`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-lifetime-is-an-object))
- **A signature's lifetime is a required key and `null` is the forever spelling** — A signature's lifetime is a **required key holding a nullable value**: both a written instant and a written `null` are spellings, and omitting the key does not compile. ([`core-api/a-lifetime-is-written`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-lifetime-is-written))
- **A signature is taken over a structured payload, never over assembled text, and a URL is signed through the canonical form its class already defines** — Signing takes a **structured payload**, never assembled text. ([`core-api/signing-is-over-a-payload`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-signing-is-over-a-payload))
- **Every way of failing a signature check is one refusal, and expiry is the single distinguishable one** — Every way of not being authentic is **one error with one sentence**: text that is not a token, a payload too short, one flipped bit, a key retired past the end of the ring, a missing signature parameter, two of them. ([`core-api/one-refusal-except-expiry`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-refusal-except-expiry))
- **Two members are not a second spelling when each takes a different thing and answers a different thing** — Two members are not a second spelling of one operation when **each takes a different thing and answers a different thing.** A payload signer takes a map and answers a token; a URL's own signing member takes a URL and an… ([`core-api/each-door-takes-a-different-thing`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-each-door-takes-a-different-thing))
- **Cross-request state is reached through a member per tier, each with its own contract, never one API with a flag** — Cross-request state is reached through **a member per tier, each with its own contract**, not one member with a flag. ([`core-api/two-cache-tiers`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-two-cache-tiers))
- **The whole temporary-file surface is one member handing out an owned directory** — One member is the whole temporary-file surface: it hands the caller an owned directory, and the program names files inside it with ordinary writes to paths it got back. ([`core-api/one-temporary-directory-member`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-one-temporary-directory-member))
- **The session roster is `start` and the members that work on the record it loaded, and a member called before `start` throws naming it** — The session surface is `start` plus the members that work on the record it loaded — read, write, remove, clear, regenerate, destroy, and the sealed pair `http-server/a-session-holds-a-secret-only-sealed` adds. ([`core-api/session-roster`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-session-roster))
- **An implemented `Core` member carries its reference card in the registry declaration beside its code** — An implemented `Core` member's reference documentation lives in its registry declaration, next to the code it documents: a short description of one or two sentences, a name and description per parameter — and for a shap… ([`core-api/reference-card`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-reference-card))
- **A PHP built-in is absent for one of four standing reasons** — A PHP built-in that has no successor here is absent for one of four standing reasons:… ([`core-api/removals`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-removals))
- **`Core`'s own API has no deprecation window before a release, and a removed name's error names its replacement** — While Novis is Pre-Alpha, a name `Core` removes from its own API is gone in the release that removes it: a member, a parameter, an attribute option or an option of an options bag. ([`core-api/no-deprecation-window-before-a-release`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-no-deprecation-window-before-a-release))
- **A moved `Core` name's error says where it went, and carries a safe fix that writes it** — When `Core` moves a name, code that still writes the old name does not compile, and the error says where the name went. ([`core-api/a-moved-name-says-where-it-went`](rules/core-api.md#core-api-a-moved-name-says-where-it-went))

## The Core classes

- **`Core\Cli::arguments` is how a program reads the words it was started with, at every depth** — `Core\Cli::arguments()` answers the words the program was started with, as an `array<tainted string>`. ([`core-classes/cli-arguments`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-cli-arguments))
- **`Core\Env::context()` names the kind of run the code is in, one `Core\Env::Context` case for each kind of run the echo table names** — `Core\Env::context(): Core\Env::Context` names the kind of run the calling code is in, with one case for each kind of run `tooling/echo-always-has-a-sink`'s table names:… ([`core-classes/env-context`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-env-context))
- **`Core\Script::args` is the value the current isolate was spawned with, and `null` where there was none** — `Core\Script::args(): mixed` is the deep-copied value the current isolate was spawned with, and `null` where there was none — a child spawned without the option, and the root script, which nothing spawned. ([`core-classes/script-args`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-script-args))
- **`Core\Process` is the one way to run another program, and there is no shell string anywhere in it** — `Core\Process` is the one way to run another program, and it is argv-only. ([`core-classes/process-is-argv-only`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-is-argv-only))
- **`run` waits by suspending the coroutine, and hands back the exit code with both captures as `bytes`** — `Core\Process::run(string $path, array<string> $argv, ProcessOptions $options)` spawns the process, waits for it to exit, and answers a result carrying the exit code and both captures. ([`core-classes/process-run`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-run))
- **`ProcessOptions` carries a working directory, a replaced environment and a timeout, and nothing else** — `ProcessOptions` carries three fields and no more: a working directory, an environment, and a timeout. ([`core-classes/process-options`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-options))
- **`spawn` answers a handle whose reads and writes suspend, covering `proc_open` and `passthru` in one type** — `Core\Process::spawn` takes the same path and argument array as `run` and answers a `Core\Process\Handle` instead of waiting: `readStdout`, `readStderr`, `writeStdin`, `wait`, `kill`. ([`core-classes/process-spawn`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-spawn))
- **A target only a second command-line parser could run is refused, on every platform** — A target the platform can only run by handing it to a second command-line parser — `.bat` and `.cmd` to `cmd.exe`, `.ps1` to `powershell.exe` — is refused before spawning, with a diagnostic naming the extension and the… ([`core-classes/process-refuses-a-shell-target`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-process-refuses-a-shell-target))
- **`Core\IO::writeStream` is where every stream reaches disk, and a failed write removes its partial file** — `Core\IO::writeStream(string $path, Iterable<bytes> $src, {max?, overwrite?})` is where a stream reaches disk, and every convenience that writes one delegates to it. ([`core-classes/io-write-stream`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-io-write-stream))
- **A temporary directory lives under a Novis-owned root and is deleted when its script ends, and the sweep never throws** — `Core\IO::temporaryDir()` is the whole temporary-file surface: it hands out an **owned directory** and the program names files inside it. ([`core-classes/temporary-dir-sweep`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-temporary-dir-sweep))
- **The orphan sweep is keyed on the owner being alive, never on age, and runs in exactly two places** — A process killed outright ran no end-of-script sweep. ([`core-classes/temporary-dir-orphan-sweep`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-temporary-dir-orphan-sweep))
- **A pattern runs on the linear engine unless it cannot, and the backtracking tier's step budget throws when exhausted** — Every pattern compiles to the **linear tier** if the linear engine can express it, and to the… ([`core-classes/regex-two-tiers`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-regex-two-tiers))
- **A pattern given as a string literal is validated and tiered while checking, and a malformed one is a compile error** — A pattern argument given as a string literal is validated and compiled while checking, under `expressions/intrinsic-constant-arguments`, and the tier it landed in is written down where later stages read it back. ([`core-classes/regex-compile-time-tiering`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-regex-compile-time-tiering))
- **Regex syntax is PCRE's with no `u` modifier, and a construct neither engine supports is diagnosed by name** — The accepted syntax is PCRE's, across both tiers, with three fixed points. ([`core-classes/regex-syntax`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-regex-syntax))

([`core-classes/pdf-css-subset`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset))
- **The CSS subset is `extensions/pdf/subset.json`, a table a test reads and the editor's data is generated from** — The CSS subset is **data**: `extensions/pdf/subset.json` lists every property, value function, at-rule, selector and PDF-specific HTML attribute the engine implements, each with a one-line plain description, and nothing… ([`core-classes/pdf-css-subset-table`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-css-subset-table))
- **A table across pages keeps its columns, repeats its header and footer, never cuts a line and closes its borders** — A table that runs over several pages follows **eight rules, each a default with no configuration**:… ([`core-classes/pdf-tables-across-pages`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-tables-across-pages))
- **A header, a footer or a slot is a Novis function called once per page, placed by a second call that never moves the body** — A header, a footer or a table slot that needs the program's own logic is a **Novis function called once per page** with that page's `Page`, returning ``html`…` `` markup. ([`core-classes/pdf-header-is-a-page-function`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-header-is-a-page-function))
- **The writer emits nothing a reader would execute, the invoice XML is its one attachment, and equal input gives byte-equal output** — The writer never emits JavaScript, launch actions, an open action, form fields, or any construct that makes a reader fetch or execute on open. ([`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-output-is-inert))
- **Every PDF is tagged, a chosen PDF/A or PDF/UA standard is validated, and a password encrypts with AES-256 alone** — with their `alt` text and the document's language come from the HTML, with no option to turn it off. ([`core-classes/pdf-standards-and-passwords`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-standards-and-passwords))
- **A Factur-X XML under PDF/A-3b is the one attachment a rendered PDF carries** — `Document::invoiceXml` embeds **exactly one Factur-X (ZUGFeRD) XML file**, under PDF/A-3b only, and it is the only attachment the writer ever emits (`core-classes/pdf-output-is-inert`). ([`core-classes/pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-factur-x-is-the-one-attachment))
- **Existing PDFs are placed, merged and read in `Novis\Pdf`, and an encrypted source throws** — Existing PDFs are **placed, merged and read in `Novis\Pdf`**; only rasterising a page is the image component's (`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`). ([`core-classes/pdf-reader-and-merge`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-reader-and-merge))
- **The Liberation fonts render a document with no font of its own, and a missing glyph is reported, never thrown** — The PDF component carries **Liberation Sans, Serif and Mono in regular, bold, italic and bold italic**, so a plain document renders with no font in its asset map. ([`core-classes/pdf-default-fonts`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-default-fonts))
- **A PDF page is a decode-only format of the image component: one page per `open`, priced by the pixel cap** — Rasterising a PDF page is a **decode-only format of the image component**, not a member of `Novis\Pdf`: a raster produced there would have to recross the boundary to enter the pipeline that is the whole point of loading… ([`core-classes/pdf-page-is-an-image-source`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-page-is-an-image-source))
- **An encrypted document and a detectable omission both throw, and reading and merging are `Novis\Pdf`'s** — An **encrypted document throws** a `ParseError` naming the encryption. ([`core-classes/pdf-decode-refusals`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-pdf-decode-refusals))
- **`Novis\Spreadsheet` is a built-in component that never touches disk, fetches nothing and executes nothing it reads** — `Novis\Spreadsheet` is the fourth component built into every `nvs` binary (`packaging/the-first-party-components-are-built-in`), sandboxed, always present under `Novis\`, with `Novis\Spreadsheet\Engine` as its manifest… ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-has-no-io`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-has-no-io))
- **`Novis\Spreadsheet` is `Workbook`, `Sheet`, `Written`, `Export`, `Reader`, `Template`, `Style`, `Cell`, `Formula`, `Chart` and `CellError`, with `Engine` the manifest class** — `Novis\Spreadsheet` is twelve classes and one enum, with `Engine` the manifest class whose static methods are `wit/spreadsheet.wit`'s exports and which no program calls directly:… ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-roster`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-roster))
- **A workbook is written as a stream to the target it was created for, one sheet after another, and finished with `finish()`** — A workbook is written as a stream to the target it was created for, and **streaming is the only way to write**: a row's values and styles are final once written, and there is no in-memory editable mode. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream))
- **Every Novis value writes as one cell type and every cell reads as one Novis type, and an `Instant` needs a zone** — Every Novis value writes as one cell type and every cell reads as one Novis type, by two fixed tables, so neither a write nor a read guesses from the value's content. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-value-types`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-value-types))
- **Only an explicit `Formula` value writes a formula cell, so an export built from user data is inert** — Only an explicit `Formula` value produces a formula cell. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-formula-is-a-value))
- **A `Style` layers column, row and cell, and a sheet with a header row is bold, bordered, frozen, filtered and auto-width by default** — A style is a `Style::of({...})` value, layered column, then row, then cell, and a sheet with a header row is styled by default: a bold header with a bottom border, frozen, filtered, and every column `width: 'auto'`. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-styles-and-defaults))
- **Merges, links, notes, validation, tables, conditional formats, images and charts may point at any written row until the sheet ends** — The parts xlsx writes after a sheet's rows or in a part of its own are `Sheet` calls that may point at any row already written, until the sheet is finished: merged ranges, hyperlinks, notes, data validation, outline gro… ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-sheet-end-parts`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-sheet-end-parts))
- **A template fill copies every part but the filled cells, repeats the rows a list marks, and shifts every reference below them** — `Template::open($source)->fill($data)` copies every part of a designed workbook unchanged except the cells it fills, writes a row marked by a list once per item, and moves every reference below it so the formulas, table… ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-template-fill`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-template-fill))
- **xlsx and xlsb are read through byte ranges a host import serves from the lent source, into typed rows keyed by their row numbers** — `Reader::open($source)` reads a `Core\IO\File` the program opened, or `bytes` it holds, and xlsx and xlsb are read as a stream of byte ranges, so a 100 MB upload never enters the guest whole; xlsm, xls and ods are read… ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-reads-as-a-stream))
- **A workbook crosses the boundary a batch at a time, never a cell at a time, and Excel's grid is the only limit it adds** — A workbook crosses the boundary a batch of rows at a time on write and a read-ahead block and a batch of rows at a time on read, **never a cell at a time**, and Excel's own grid and limits are the only limits the compon… ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-bulk-boundary`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-bulk-boundary))
- **The roster reads xlsx, xlsm, xlsb, xls, ods and CSV and writes xlsx and CSV, a macro is never written, and nothing evaluates** — The format roster is **read-wide and write-narrow**. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-evaluation-and-roster))
- **The writer and the template filler embed no executable content and no entropy, so equal input gives byte-equal output** — The writer emits no macros, no embedded executables and no launch-shaped content; hyperlinks exist only where the program wrote them. ([`core-classes/spreadsheet-output-is-inert`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-spreadsheet-output-is-inert))
- **`Core\Net` is one class over TCP, UDP and Unix sockets, reached through five entry points that park on the runtime's own reactor** — `Core\Net` is the whole socket surface: one class over three transports, TCP, UDP and Unix-domain sockets. ([`core-classes/net-one-api-three-transports`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-net-one-api-three-transports))
- **A `Core\Net` socket closes with the request that opened it, so there is no persistent connection and no pool across requests** — A socket opened through `Core\Net` closes with the request that opened it. ([`core-classes/net-a-socket-does-not-outlive-its-request`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-net-a-socket-does-not-outlive-its-request))
- **A datagram socket sends and receives messages and offers no ordering, retransmission or acknowledgement above them** — A `Core\Net` datagram socket sends and receives messages, reports what it sent and what arrived, and offers nothing above that: no ordering, no retransmission, no fragmentation and no acknowledgement. ([`core-classes/net-udp-carries-no-reliability-layer`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-net-udp-carries-no-reliability-layer))
- **There is no `Core\Net` socket pair: PHP's `stream_socket_pair` is dropped, because no process boundary can receive one** — `Core\Net` has no member that opens a connected pair of anonymous sockets, and PHP's `stream_socket_pair` is a `dropped` row. ([`core-classes/net-has-no-socket-pair`](rules/core-classes.md#core-classes-net-has-no-socket-pair))

## Observability

- **Production telemetry is read from the instrumentation that already exists, and adds no probe site to the measured path** — Production telemetry — the default metric series, the spans, the trace ids on a log line — is read from instrumentation the runtime already has: the per-statement and per-call probes of `testing/debug-probes`, and the `… ([`observability/the-runtime-exports-what-it-already-measures`](rules/observability.md#observability-the-runtime-exports-what-it-already-measures))
- **A trace id exists for every request whatever the sampling decision and is emitted on the response unless the configuration turns the header off, the request id is always one the server drew, and an inbound `X-Request-ID` is ignored** — A trace id is drawn for every request when its context is built, whatever the sampling decision. ([`observability/a-trace-id-exists-for-every-request`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-trace-id-exists-for-every-request))
- **`[trace] response_header` sends the `traceresponse` header by default and `false` removes it, while the trace id still exists for the request, its logs and its spans** — `[trace] response_header` decides whether a response carries the `traceresponse` header, is `true` by default in both modes, and `false` removes the header and nothing else. ([`observability/the-traceresponse-header-can-be-turned-off`](rules/observability.md#observability-the-traceresponse-header-can-be-turned-off))
- **A log record inside an active trace carries `trace_id` and `span_id`, and outside one omits both rather than writing them empty** — The JSON-Lines record `errors/log-write` defines gains `trace_id` and `span_id` whenever a trace is active. ([`observability/a-log-record-carries-trace-ids-when-a-trace-is-active`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-log-record-carries-trace-ids-when-a-trace-is-active))
- **`Core\Metrics` is three verbs for three kinds, always present, and accumulates whether or not an exporter is built** — `increment` for a counter, `observe` for a histogram, `gauge` for a point-in-time value: three verbs for three kinds. ([`observability/metrics-three-members`](rules/observability.md#observability-metrics-three-members))
- **Eleven series exist the moment an exporter is configured, with no application code written** — Eleven series are present the moment an exporter is configured, with no application code written:… ([`observability/default-series`](rules/observability.md#observability-default-series))
- **A metric name is fixed to one kind and one label set on first use, and a second kind throws naming both sites** — A metric name is fixed to one kind — counter, histogram or gauge — on its first use within a process, and its label *names* are fixed with it. ([`observability/a-name-is-fixed-to-one-kind`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-name-is-fixed-to-one-kind))
- **The `route` label carries the matched route's path pattern, never the request path** — The `route` label on the request series carries the matched route's **path pattern**, the mount-relative `#[Route]` `path` such as `/users/{id}`, from the compile-time table of `routing/routes-are-compiled-not-registere… ([`observability/route-label-is-the-path-pattern`](rules/observability.md#observability-route-label-is-the-path-pattern))
- **A metrics registry is per core, merged at scrape, and no program reads a metric** — Each core holds its own metrics registry, and a scrape merges them. ([`observability/a-registry-is-per-core-and-nothing-reads-it`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-registry-is-per-core-and-nothing-reads-it))
- **Past `max_series` a new series is refused and an existing one is never evicted** — `[metrics] max_series` bounds the number of distinct label combinations one **core** holds. ([`observability/past-max-series-a-new-series-is-refused`](rules/observability.md#observability-past-max-series-a-new-series-is-refused))
- **`[metrics]` and `[trace]` are `System` blocks, and a value neither exporter accepts is refused at boot** — Both blocks are **`System`** (`config/system-means-a-request-may-not-set-it`): where a process ships telemetry, and how much it costs to do so, is a deployment decision, and a request able to turn tracing on for itself… ([`observability/metrics-and-trace-blocks-are-system`](rules/observability.md#observability-metrics-and-trace-blocks-are-system))
- **Exactly four things become a span, and a `call` event never does** — A distributed trace is not the per-call trace `testing/debug-probes` produces, and conflating them would give a trace one span per function call, which no backend can store and no human can read. ([`observability/four-kinds-become-a-span`](rules/observability.md#observability-four-kinds-become-a-span))
- **A trace event carries one of five kinds — `call`, `gc`, `spawn`, `query`, `http` — and a `call` keeps its probe shape** — Every trace event carries a `kind` tag, and the tag is one of exactly five: `call`, `gc`, `spawn`, `query`, `http`. ([`observability/trace-events-carry-a-kind`](rules/observability.md#observability-trace-events-carry-a-kind))
- **A statement is a `query` trace event that carries its duration, driver, connection, truncated SQL and row counts, and never a bound parameter** — A statement is a `query` trace event, beside `call`, `gc` and `spawn`, instrumented in the driver's own statement routine and off the hot path exactly as those two are. ([`observability/a-query-is-a-trace-event`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-query-is-a-trace-event))
- **Every `Core\Db` call that sends a statement passes a compile-time site id, and a recorded query span carries the file and line it names** — The compiler passes each `Core\Db` member that sends a statement one more constant argument: the call site's id, an index into the program's query site table. ([`observability/a-query-span-names-its-call-site`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-query-span-names-its-call-site))
- **A `[db.<name>] slow_query` threshold writes a statement's span facts to `Core\Log`, and is off until a block writes one** — A `[db.<name>]` block may write `slow_query`, a duration such as `"200ms"` or `"1s"`; a statement on that connection that runs longer writes the same facts its trace event carries — duration, driver, connection, truncat… ([`observability/a-slow-query-is-logged-past-a-threshold`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-slow-query-is-logged-past-a-threshold))
- **A collector pause is a `gc` event recorded from the collector's run routine, never from the safepoint poll** — A stop-the-world collection run is a trace event of its own, `kind: gc`, recorded from **inside the cycle collector's run routine** and gated by the same `TRACE`/`PROFILE` bits `Ctx` already carries. ([`observability/gc-pause-is-its-own-event`](rules/observability.md#observability-gc-pause-is-its-own-event))
- **A spawn and its join are one `spawn` event naming the form it was, with an overhead split where the child reports its own time, and a child's own stream never crosses live** — Each spawn construct — `spawn`, `spawn worker`, `spawn script`, and `Core\Process::spawn`, whose child is the operating system's rather than an isolate — emits a `kind: spawn` event from its own runtime routine, and its… ([`observability/spawn-is-its-own-event`](rules/observability.md#observability-spawn-is-its-own-event))
- **An inbound `traceparent` is continued, and one the process cannot read starts a new trace rather than failing the request** — An inbound W3C `traceparent` header continues the trace: its trace id and parent span id are adopted, and its sampled flag is honoured. ([`observability/an-inbound-traceparent-is-continued`](rules/observability.md#observability-an-inbound-traceparent-is-continued))
- **`Core\Http\Client` sends `traceparent` while `[trace] propagate` is on, and the id it sends is the request's own** — `Core\Http\Client` sends `traceparent` on every outbound call while `[trace] propagate` is on, which is what makes a trace cross a service boundary at all. ([`observability/an-outbound-call-propagates-traceparent`](rules/observability.md#observability-an-outbound-call-propagates-traceparent))
- **Sampling is decided once at the root by `[trace] sample`, and an inbound trace that is already sampled is always continued** — Sampling is **head-based at the root**: `[trace] sample` is the probability, from `0.0` to `1.0`, that a *new* trace is recorded. ([`observability/sampling-is-head-based`](rules/observability.md#observability-sampling-is-head-based))
- **The exporter is a feature-gated Native subsystem, and `Core\Metrics` is Tier 0 in every build** — The exporter — the Prometheus scrape endpoint and the OTLP client — is a **Native, feature-gated** subsystem (`core-api/five-placements`), on by default in the server distribution, so a CLI binary or a single-file execu… ([`observability/the-exporter-is-a-feature-and-core-metrics-is-not`](rules/observability.md#observability-the-exporter-is-a-feature-and-core-metrics-is-not))
- **The OTLP and Prometheus paths are somebody else's specification, implemented here; the wiring and the registry are ours** — The OTLP path, including the W3C TraceContext propagator, and the Prometheus scrape path are somebody else's specification, and they are implemented against it behind the feature `observability/the-exporter-is-a-feature… ([`observability/the-exporters-are-crates`](rules/observability.md#observability-the-exporters-are-crates))
- **An exporter brings no second registry, no second scheduler and no second client, and a crate is taken only for an encoder** — An exporter brings no second registry, no second scheduler and no second client: a crate is taken for a half that needs none of those — an encoder — and never for a half that carries its own execution or its own socket. ([`observability/an-exporter-brings-no-second-scheduler-and-no-second-client`](rules/observability.md#observability-an-exporter-brings-no-second-scheduler-and-no-second-client))
- **The profiler's speedscope export is an evented timeline per context, with every trace event kind on it, beside its Callgrind export** — `nvs run --profile=speedscope` and `nvs test --profile=speedscope` write the run's trace events, of every kind `observability/trace-events-carry-a-kind` names, as speedscope's evented-profile JSON: an open and a close a… ([`observability/speedscope-timeline-export`](rules/observability.md#observability-speedscope-timeline-export))
- **A request reads its own memory as `memoryHeld`, `memoryPeak` and `memoryLimit` on `Core\Budget`, and the process's resident bytes are `Core\Os`'s** — A request reads its own memory as three members on `Core\Budget` — `memoryHeld()` is the bytes it holds right now, `memoryPeak()` the high-water mark of that figure for this request, and `memoryLimit()` the ceiling both… ([`observability/memory-is-three-numbers-on-core-budget`](rules/observability.md#observability-memory-is-three-numbers-on-core-budget))
- **The runtime records a request's memory high-water mark in every build, and a nested isolate restores the enclosing mark rather than clobbering it** — The runtime keeps a request's memory high-water mark in every build, updated where the live-byte balance is updated, and a nested `Ctx` restores the larger of its own mark and the one it displaced rather than clobbering… ([`observability/a-memory-peak-is-recorded-not-asked-for`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-memory-peak-is-recorded-not-asked-for))
- **A `[limits] memory_high_water` fraction writes one `Warn` when a request's memory peak crosses that share of its ceiling, and is off until a block writes one** — A `[limits]` block may write `memory_high_water`, a fraction between `0.0` and `1.0`; a request whose memory peak crosses that share of its effective ceiling writes one `Warn` to `Core\Log` at the end of the request, na… ([`observability/memory-high-water-writes-a-warn`](rules/observability.md#observability-memory-high-water-writes-a-warn))
- **`Core\Script::onExit` registers a request-local hook that runs FIFO as the last user code, and each hook receives one readonly `ExitReport`** — `Core\Script::onExit(callable $hook): void` registers a hook that runs as the **last user code of the script**. ([`observability/script-on-exit`](rules/observability.md#observability-script-on-exit))
- **The exit queue drains once — at a normal end, at `exit`, at an uncaught throw and at `Core\Script::finish()` — and the report says which ending it was** — Four endings fire the exit queue, and the report each hook receives says which:… ([`observability/three-endings-fire-the-exit-queue`](rules/observability.md#observability-three-endings-fire-the-exit-queue))
- **Exit hooks run after every `finally` and after the failure hooks, and before native teardown, with the heap alive and output where it was** — On the throw path the order is fixed: the unwind's `finally` blocks, innermost first; then `errors/on-uncaught-throw`'s handler; then this queue; then native teardown. ([`observability/exit-hooks-run-after-the-ladder-before-teardown`](rules/observability.md#observability-exit-hooks-run-after-the-ladder-before-teardown))
- **A `FATAL` and a cancellation run no exit hook — `Core\Fatal::onLimit` is the one observer of a limit breach** — Two terminations never fire the exit queue. ([`observability/a-fatal-and-a-cancellation-run-no-exit-hook`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-fatal-and-a-cancellation-run-no-exit-hook))
- **A hook observes the ending and never steers it: the report is fixed first, a throw is logged and abandoned, `exit` inside a hook throws, and the drain continues** — The report — reason and status — is fixed before the first hook runs, and nothing a hook does changes it. ([`observability/a-hook-observes-and-never-steers`](rules/observability.md#observability-a-hook-observes-and-never-steers))

## The HTTP server

- **The server is a development server or a proxied production origin, and nothing a proxy does earlier is in it** — The built-in server has exactly two deployments. ([`http-server/two-deployments-and-nothing-a-proxy-owns`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-two-deployments-and-nothing-a-proxy-owns))
- **Only `listen`, `socket_mode` and `workers` in `[server]` need a restart, `listen` is one flat array defaulting to `127.0.0.1:8000` in both modes, and the flag is the last word** — The whole block is `System`-class (`config/three-changeability-classes`): `header_timeout` and `keepalive_timeout` apply before any Novis code exists on a connection, so a `Runtime` class would be a promise the block co… ([`http-server/the-server-block-is-boot-class`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-server-block-is-boot-class))
- **A mount matches on `prefix` or `host`, names one `entry` or one `scan`, and a scan expands against the disk at boot and again whenever a scanned directory changes** — A mount matches on `prefix`, on `host`, or on both, and names **either** `entry` (one literal file) **or** `scan` (a glob); both or neither is a boot error. ([`http-server/a-mount-table-expands-at-boot`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-mount-table-expands-at-boot))
- **A mount's key set is `prefix`, `host`, `scan`, `entry` and `origin`; `mode`, limits and capabilities belong to the `[[app]]` block** — A `[[server.mount]]` carries no `mode`, no limits and no capabilities. ([`http-server/a-mount-carries-no-policy`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-mount-carries-no-policy))
- **`nvs serve` needs no file over a written mount table, serves that table whole with each entry under its own `[[app]]` blocks, and refuses a start that names nothing** — `nvs serve` takes its entry file as an optional argument over a configuration that writes `[[server.mount]]`, and a start that names none serves that mount table whole (`http-server/a-mount-table-expands-at-boot`). ([`http-server/the-served-file-is-optional`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-served-file-is-optional))
- **A `listen` entry beginning with a separator is a Unix socket, Unix-only, with `socket_mode`, and it is the transport a proxy should prefer** — A `[server] listen` entry beginning with a path separator names a Unix-domain socket; because no `host:port` can begin that way the overload is unambiguous, and `socket_mode` applies to those entries only. ([`http-server/a-unix-socket-listener`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-unix-socket-listener))
- **`[mode] ceiling` is `System`-class, bounds a runtime flip and not the startup value, and unset equals the mode the server started in** — `[mode] ceiling` states the most permissive mode any code on the host may select. ([`http-server/the-mode-ceiling-defaults-to-the-startup-mode`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-mode-ceiling-defaults-to-the-startup-mode))
- **A default that is unsafe inbound or unbounded outbound is a defect, not a neutral starting point** — A default that is unsafe inbound or unbounded outbound is a defect, not a neutral starting point a deployment is expected to improve on. ([`http-server/an-unsafe-or-unbounded-default-is-a-defect`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-unsafe-or-unbounded-default-is-a-defect))
