([`http-server/an-outbound-socket-is-bounded-by-idle-a-lifetime-and-a-message-cap`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-outbound-socket-is-bounded-by-idle-a-lifetime-and-a-message-cap))
- **An outbound socket negotiates no `permessage-deflate` and never reconnects on its own** — An outbound socket offers no `permessage-deflate` in its handshake, and a socket that ends stays ended: it reports why, and what to do next is the program's. ([`http-server/an-outbound-socket-has-no-compression-and-no-reconnect`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-an-outbound-socket-has-no-compression-and-no-reconnect))
- **Nothing a request can send terminates or wedges a worker: its blast radius is bounded at four named tiers, and the residue is one stated fault class** — A request's blast radius is bounded by construction at four named tiers, and the residue below them is one stated fault class rather than an unexamined gap:… ([`http-server/a-requests-blast-radius-is-bounded-at-four-tiers`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-requests-blast-radius-is-bounded-at-four-tiers))
- **A worker task's root is wrapped in `catch_unwind`: a panic beneath a request fails that request, and one outside any request retires the worker** — `errors/propagation`'s `nvs_helper!` wrapper contains a panic raised beneath a JIT frame. ([`http-server/containment-does-not-end-at-the-helper`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-containment-does-not-end-at-the-helper))
- **Every engine-side recursive descent over request data carries a depth counter and refuses past it, with a limit per decoder and `512` for JSON** — `errors/stack-depth` bounds recursion through Novis frames, where every user call is a real machine frame and the check is emitted at function entry. ([`http-server/engine-depth-is-bounded-per-decoder`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-engine-depth-is-bounded-per-decoder))
- **A helper whose runtime scales with its input polls the request's deadline flag through a bounded-loop combinator, or bounds its input instead** — The safepoint poll bounds Novis code because it sits between calls. ([`http-server/time-is-bounded-inside-a-helper`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-time-is-bounded-inside-a-helper))
- **No path reaches `abort()`: nothing on a teardown path panics, teardown is iterative, and an allocation sized by request data is fallible** — `panic = "unwind"` prevents the abort that `panic = "abort"` would cause. ([`http-server/no-path-reaches-abort`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-no-path-reaches-abort))
- **A core is never blocked on a syscall: filesystem calls, name resolution and waiting on a child go to a blocking pool bounded at twice the core count** — The runtime is one single-threaded scheduler pinned per core, and a request never migrates. ([`http-server/a-core-is-never-blocked-on-a-syscall`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-core-is-never-blocked-on-a-syscall))
- **A request that runs a 10 ms slice without waiting gives its core back at its next safepoint poll, behind readiness** — A core runs one task at a time, and a task runs until it waits. ([`http-server/a-request-that-computes-shares-its-core`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-request-that-computes-shares-its-core))
- **A watchdog reads the in-flight deadline each worker already keeps, and reports a core whose oldest deadline is past by a margin** — Every other bound answers a fault. ([`http-server/a-wedged-core-is-detected-by-its-deadline`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-wedged-core-is-detected-by-its-deadline))
- **A reported core stops accepting and `max_in_flight` counts its share as unavailable; a wedged worker is never killed in-process** — What a watchdog report does is **report and shed, never kill**: the affected core stops accepting new work, and `max_in_flight` accounts for its share as unavailable so the remaining cores are not asked to carry a ceili… ([`http-server/a-wedged-core-is-shed-never-killed`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-wedged-core-is-shed-never-killed))
- **A request whose client goes away runs to its end under its `wall_time`, or `disconnect_grace` when it has none, unless its method is listed in `cancel_on_disconnect`** — A request whose client goes away runs to its end, under every limit it already has, and its response is thrown away; a method listed in `[limits] cancel_on_disconnect` is cancelled at the drop instead. ([`http-server/a-request-outlives-a-client-that-goes-away`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-request-outlives-a-client-that-goes-away))
- **Every timeout, deadline and backoff in the engine is computed on a monotonic clock** — Every timeout, deadline and backoff in the engine is computed on a monotonic clock, never on wall time. ([`http-server/every-deadline-is-monotonic`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-every-deadline-is-monotonic))
- **The floor cannot fill the disk it writes to: a file target rotates under a retention bound, repeats coalesce into one record with a count, and a cache write failure compiles in memory** — `errors/engine-floor`'s floor writes unconditionally, which is correct, and a request that faults in a loop therefore writes in a loop. ([`http-server/the-floor-cannot-fill-the-disk`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-floor-cannot-fill-the-disk))
- **A page holding generated code is writable while written and executable only after being made read-only** — Pages holding generated code are mapped writable while being written and executable only after being made read-only. ([`http-server/a-jit-page-is-never-writable-and-executable-at-once`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-a-jit-page-is-never-writable-and-executable-at-once))
- **A memory-safety fault in `unsafe` code or a miscompile is the one residue: the process dies, the supervisor restarts it, and the answer is frequency, not a boundary** — What survives every other bound is **a memory-safety fault in `unsafe` code, or a miscompilation from the code generator**. ([`http-server/the-residue-is-one-named-fault-class`](rules/http-server.md#http-server-the-residue-is-one-named-fault-class))

## Routing

- **A route is a `#[Route]` compiled into the unit's table, its three runtime bugs are compile errors, and one method's routes share one path** — A route is declared where its handler is: `#[Route(path: "/users/{id}", method: Http\Method::Get)]` on a method, and the method is the route's identity. ([`routing/routes-are-compiled-not-registered`](rules/routing.md#routing-routes-are-compiled-not-registered))
- **`#[Route]` is `{path, method, slotted?}` on a method, recognized by name and never by shape, and the method is the route's identity** — `type Core\Route = {path: string, method: Core\Http\Method, slotted?: bool};` — an ordinary `attributes/inert-metadata` alias, attached the ordinary way, with one difference: the compiler acts on it only when the name *… ([`routing/route-attribute`](rules/routing.md#routing-route-attribute))
- **A path is fixed segments and three capture forms, each capture a whole segment naming a parameter** — A path is a string literal beginning at the root, validated while checking, whose segments are fixed segments or captures:… ([`routing/path-grammar`](rules/routing.md#routing-path-grammar))
- **There is no wildcard verb: `method` is required, singular, and one case of a closed enum** — There is no `Method::Any`, no omitted `method` and no multi-valued `method`. ([`routing/no-wildcard-verb`](rules/routing.md#routing-no-wildcard-verb))
- **Precedence is structural — a fixed segment beats a capture beats an optional beats a catch-all — never declaration order** — Where two routes of one verb both match a path, the one with more fixed segments wins, segment by segment: a fixed segment beats a `{name}`, which beats a `{name?}`, which beats a `{name...}`. ([`routing/precedence-is-structural`](rules/routing.md#routing-precedence-is-structural))
- **A capture narrows to a closed set with a set of allowed values or an enum-subset type, never with a regex** — A capture's type may be a **set of allowed `string` or `int` values**, or a **subset of an enum's cases** (`types/single-value-types`), beside the scalar and enum types a capture already converts to. ([`routing/a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-capture-narrows-to-a-closed-set))
- **An enum capture is spelled by a written backing value, and by its case name when the value was counted** — An enum capture matches on its case's **written** backing value, and on the **case name** when the value was counted rather than written, in a path segment and in a `#[Query]` value alike. ([`routing/an-enum-capture-is-spelled-by-its-backing-value-or-its-case-name`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-enum-capture-is-spelled-by-its-backing-value-or-its-case-name))
- **`{name?}` captures one trailing segment or none, and its parameter's default is what makes the absent case well-typed** — `{name?}` captures one whole segment or none. ([`routing/a-trailing-segment-may-be-absent`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-trailing-segment-may-be-absent))
- **A `#[Query]` parameter is declared with a capture's type list, and a default is what makes it optional** — `#[Query]` on a parameter of a `#[Route]` method declares that the parameter is bound from the request's query string, by the parameter's own name — the attribute carries nothing that could give it another key. ([`routing/a-query-parameter-is-declared-like-a-capture`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-query-parameter-is-declared-like-a-capture))
- **A `#[Query]` value that does not convert is a `400`, where a path capture the matcher cannot convert is a `404`** — A `#[Query]` parameter's value converts to its declared type and arrives unqualified, exactly as a path capture does, and fails differently. ([`routing/a-bad-query-value-is-a-400`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-bad-query-value-is-a-400))
- **A method is one `url()` target, one `Match::is` for every verb, and one `operationId` per verb** — A method whose repeated `#[Route]`s serve several verbs is one endpoint everywhere it is observed:… ([`routing/a-method-is-one-endpoint-everywhere`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-method-is-one-endpoint-everywhere))
- **A match is a route identity and typed parameters, and running a handler is a separate call the program makes** — The server matches a request once, before any application code, and `Core\Request::route()` is that match; `match` asks the same table about a verb and a path the program chose. ([`routing/matching-is-not-dispatching`](rules/routing.md#routing-matching-is-not-dispatching))
- **A match carries its row and typed parameters and nothing invocable, and typed `callable` would not change that** — `Core\Router\Match` carries the matched row, which `is` compares a method reference against, the typed captures the path filled, the declared verb and the access decision's name, and nothing invocable: no `->invoke()`,… ([`routing/a-match-is-not-invocable`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-match-is-not-invocable))
- **`Core\Router\Match::attribute<T>()` returns the one attribute payload on the matched route's method that satisfies the shape `T`, folded while compiling** — `$match->attribute<T>()` returns the one attribute payload on the matched route's method that satisfies the shape `T`, or `null` where none does. ([`routing/a-match-reads-an-attribute-as-data`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-match-reads-an-attribute-as-data))
- **A request is matched once, before any application code runs, and `Core\Request::route()` is that match** — The server matches the incoming request against the compiled table **once**, before any application code runs, and records the result on the request. ([`routing/matched-once-before-the-handler`](rules/routing.md#routing-matched-once-before-the-handler))
- **The server's match dispatches nothing, and a request the table does not claim is served by the program** — The server computes a name and typed parameters and stops there. ([`routing/the-servers-match-dispatches-nothing`](rules/routing.md#routing-the-servers-match-dispatches-nothing))
- **A missing path and a refused verb are different answers, and `methodsFor` is what tells them apart** — `Core\Router::methodsFor(tainted string $path): array<Http\Method>` tells a missing path from a refused verb. ([`routing/a-refused-verb-is-not-a-missing-path`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-refused-verb-is-not-a-missing-path))
- **`Core\Router::dispatch` calls the matched method, and one gate answers every request it refuses or that fails** — `Core\Router::dispatch(Core\Router\Gate $gate): void` calls the method of the route the server matched, and the gate the program passes answers every request that method does not run for. ([`routing/a-gate-answers-around-every-handler`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-gate-answers-around-every-handler))
- **`Core\Request::mount()` answers the prefix the door stripped and the tainted host captures, and it is never `null`** — `Core\Request::mount(): Core\Request\Mount` answers the two facts about the door a request came through: `prefix(): string` is what the mount stripped from the path before the program saw it, and `captures(): array<tain… ([`routing/a-request-reads-its-mount`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-request-reads-its-mount))
- **`Core\Router::url` is a launderer that takes its route as a method reference, and a reference and `$params` written in the code are checked against the compiled table** — `Core\Router::url(callable $route, array<string, mixed> $params = []): string` takes the route by its method reference — `Router::url(App::show, ['id' => 3])` — and reverses the table from that method. ([`routing/link-target-and-params-are-checked`](rules/routing.md#routing-link-target-and-params-are-checked))
- **A link carries the mount prefix the request arrived under, so one table serves at any mount** — `Core\Router::url` prepends the prefix of the mount the request arrived through, in front of the substituted path. ([`routing/link-carries-the-mount-prefix`](rules/routing.md#routing-link-carries-the-mount-prefix))
- **A `url()` key that is not a capture becomes a percent-encoded query string, and one that is neither a capture nor a declared `#[Query]` parameter does not compile** — A `$params` key handed to `Core\Router::url` or `urlAbsolute` that names no capture becomes a percent-encoded query string, spelled exactly as `Core\Uri::buildQuery` spells it: `url("posts.index", {page: 3, sort: "desc"… ([`routing/a-leftover-link-key-is-a-query-string`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-leftover-link-key-is-a-query-string))
- **`urlAbsolute` prepends a configured origin and never one sniffed from a request header** — `Core\Router::urlAbsolute(callable $route, array<string, mixed> $params = []): string` is `Core\Router::url` with the configured origin in front — the same laundered path, the same query-string rule (`routing/a-leftover… ([`routing/an-absolute-link-takes-a-configured-origin`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-absolute-link-takes-a-configured-origin))
- **An origin is declared per mount with `[app] origin` as the fallback, a request cannot set it, and a mount that calls `urlAbsolute` without one is a boot error** — The origin `urlAbsolute` prepends (`routing/an-absolute-link-takes-a-configured-origin`) is declared **per mount**, on the `[[server.mount]]` block, falling back to `[app] origin`. ([`routing/an-origin-is-per-mount-and-checked-at-boot`](rules/routing.md#routing-an-origin-is-per-mount-and-checked-at-boot))
- **The table is built by the program enumeration, and a program with no `#[Route]` builds none and pays nothing** — Finding routes is the question the program enumeration was built for — *what exists that nothing names* — and the route table is that enumeration filtered by `#[Route]`, reused wholesale with its consequences (`programs… ([`routing/table-is-opt-in`](rules/routing.md#routing-table-is-opt-in))
- **The API document is generated from the route table while compiling, so it cannot drift from the code** — The OpenAPI 3.1 document is a rendering of the compiler's own route table. ([`routing/api-document-is-generated-from-the-route-table`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-document-is-generated-from-the-route-table))
- **A route's request body is the type its handler decodes with `Core\Request::jsonAs` or `postAs`, read from the handler's own call** — The compiler records each `Core\Request::jsonAs<T>()` and `Core\Request::postAs<T>()` call written directly in a route handler's body, and the route's row carries what it found: the body is `T`, as JSON for `jsonAs` and… ([`routing/a-request-body-is-read-from-the-handlers-own-call`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-request-body-is-read-from-the-handlers-own-call))
- **A security scheme is declared in code by `#[Api\Scheme]`, and every `#[Api]` `security` name must be a declared one** — A security scheme is declared in the program, by a compiler-recognized `#[Api\Scheme]` on a class, and every name an `#[Api(security: [...])]` writes must be one the program declares. ([`routing/a-security-scheme-is-declared-in-code`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-security-scheme-is-declared-in-code))
- **`nvs build --openapi` writes OpenAPI 3.1 as a build artifact, and two builds of one source are byte-identical** — `nvs build --openapi <file>` runs the program through the same front end `nvs check` uses and writes the OpenAPI 3.1 document, pretty-printed, to standard output. ([`routing/api-document-is-a-deterministic-build-artifact`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-document-is-a-deterministic-build-artifact))
- **`nvs api diff` classifies every change as breaking, additive or cosmetic, and exits non-zero on a breaking one** — `nvs api diff <old.json> <new.json>` compares two generated documents as JSON values rather than as text, prints one line per change worst-first, and exits non-zero if any change is **breaking**. ([`routing/api-diff-fails-a-breaking-change`](rules/routing.md#routing-api-diff-fails-a-breaking-change))
- **A `#[Route]` missing its `path` gets a quick fix that offers a derived one, and nothing derives a path on its own** — Nothing derives a `path` from the declaring class. ([`routing/a-quick-fix-writes-a-derived-path`](rules/routing.md#routing-a-quick-fix-writes-a-derived-path))

## Configuration

- **The configuration file is `nvs.toml`, and it is TOML** — The server configuration is a TOML file named `nvs.toml`, read into the directive registry through the `toml` crate and `serde` — at boot, and again on each reload, which parses and validates a whole replacement before… ([`config/the-file-is-nvs-toml-and-it-is-toml`](rules/config.md#config-the-file-is-nvs-toml-and-it-is-toml))
- **A size or a duration is a quoted string carrying its suffix, a count is an integer, and `false` removes a ceiling** — A size or a duration is written as a **quoted string carrying its suffix** — `memory = "128M"`, `cpu_time = "5s"` — never as a bare integer of implied units. ([`config/a-size-or-duration-is-a-quoted-string-with-its-suffix`](rules/config.md#config-a-size-or-duration-is-a-quoted-string-with-its-suffix))
- **A list is a TOML array, a repeated record is an array of tables, and a dotted key is table nesting** — A directive holding several values is a TOML array, and a directive that is a repeated record with more than one field is an array of tables:… ([`config/lists-are-arrays-and-repeated-records-are-arrays-of-tables`](rules/config.md#config-lists-are-arrays-and-repeated-records-are-arrays-of-tables))
- **A duplicate key is an error, and so is an unknown one — per file** — The same key set twice in one file is refused (`E0604`), and so is a key the registry does not know (`E0601`) — both name the file and the line. ([`config/a-duplicate-key-is-an-error-and-so-is-an-unknown-one`](rules/config.md#config-a-duplicate-key-is-an-error-and-so-is-an-unknown-one))
- **The block roster is closed, and each block's directives are argued by the rule that adds it** — The set of top-level blocks is closed, and the typed tree refuses any other with the unknown-key diagnostic (`config/a-duplicate-key-is-an-error-and-so-is-an-unknown-one`). ([`config/every-block-is-argued-where-it-is-added`](rules/config.md#config-every-block-is-argued-where-it-is-added))
- **`nvs.toml` is a deployment file, never a project manifest, and it is never found by walking up** — `nvs.toml` is a root-owned deployment file. ([`config/nvs-toml-is-not-a-project-manifest`](rules/config.md#config-nvs-toml-is-not-a-project-manifest))
- **The root of the tree is every `--config` in order, else `./nvs.toml`, else the data folder's `nvs.toml`, else the shipped defaults** — Four steps, first hit wins:… ([`config/the-root-is-config-else-nvs-toml-else-the-shipped-defaults`](rules/config.md#config-the-root-is-config-else-nvs-toml-else-the-shipped-defaults))
- **A host with no configuration file runs on the shipped defaults, which are a complete configuration and not an error** — When no `--config` is given and neither `./nvs.toml` nor the data folder's `nvs.toml` exists, the host runs on the **shipped defaults**, and those are a complete and valid configuration rather than a failure to find one… ([`config/no-configuration-file-is-a-complete-configuration`](rules/config.md#config-no-configuration-file-is-a-complete-configuration))
- **The resolved root is stored once at boot as the absolute path it was given, announced with every file it reached, and resolved again through its links on reload** — Whichever step won is **stored once, at boot, as the absolute path it was given, never its canonical path**. ([`config/the-resolved-root-is-announced-and-stored`](rules/config.md#config-the-resolved-root-is-announced-and-stored))
- **`[[include]]` takes a `path` or a `dir`, never both and never neither, and a `dir` is not a glob** — `[[include]]` is a top-level array of tables, and an entry carries `path` **or** `dir`, never both and never neither:… ([`config/include-takes-a-path-or-a-dir`](rules/config.md#config-include-takes-a-path-or-a-dir))
- **An include cycle is refused with the chain named, and nesting past eight is refused as depth** — An include tree that reaches a file already on the chain is refused with the whole chain named (`E0606`), and nesting deeper than eight files is refused as depth under the same code — not as a cycle, because it may not… ([`config/an-include-cycle-is-refused-and-nesting-is-capped-at-eight`](rules/config.md#config-an-include-cycle-is-refused-and-nesting-is-capped-at-eight))
- **The tree is one ordered stream, a later assignment wins, and every override is recorded with both origins** — The tree flattens to a single sequence: for each `--config` file in order, that file's own keys, then its includes depth-first in list order; then the next `--config` file. ([`config/later-wins-and-every-override-is-recorded`](rules/config.md#config-later-wins-and-every-override-is-recorded))
- **A value array is replaced wholesale by a later file; `[[table]]` entries accumulate across the tree** — `key = [...]` is one value, and a later value wins — so `[debug] mode`, `[capabilities] script.spawn` and `debug.trace` are **replaced wholesale** by a later file. ([`config/a-value-array-replaces-and-a-table-appends`](rules/config.md#config-a-value-array-replaces-and-a-table-appends))
- **A relative path resolves against the directory of the file it is written in; a command-line path against the working directory** — Every path-valued directive — `opcache.file_cache_dir`, `capabilities.script.spawn`, `debug.trace`, `[[extension]] path`, `[[server.mount]] root`, `[db.<name>] path`, `[storage.<name>] root`, `password_file`, an `[[app]… ([`config/a-relative-path-resolves-against-the-file-it-is-written-in`](rules/config.md#config-a-relative-path-resolves-against-the-file-it-is-written-in))
- **Any file in the tree may set any directive, `System` class included** — Because `config/ownership-is-the-trust-boundary` is uniform, **any file in the tree may set any directive**, `System` class included: capabilities, `[limits.hard]`, `[mode] ceiling` and `[[extension]]` entries are as le… ([`config/any-file-in-the-tree-may-set-any-directive`](rules/config.md#config-any-file-in-the-tree-may-set-any-directive))
- **Every file the configuration reads, and its directory, must be owned by the runtime account or root and writable by nobody else** — must not be group- or world-writable.** Its containing directory must pass the same check, ownership included and not only the mode: an entry can be replaced by whoever can write the directory holding it, whatever the f… ([`config/ownership-is-the-trust-boundary`](rules/config.md#config-ownership-is-the-trust-boundary))
- **The ownership check runs on `nvs serve`, on reload and in `config check --as` for the serving account; `nvs run`, plain `config check` and `config dump` read without it, and an unchecked file can grant nothing** — The ownership check runs where its question can be answered: `nvs serve` and reload, on the host and as the account that will serve, `nvs config check --as <account>`, which names that account, and `nvs service install`… ([`config/the-ownership-check-runs-where-it-can-be-answered`](rules/config.md#config-the-ownership-check-runs-where-it-can-be-answered))
- **`optional = true` covers absence and nothing else, and an absent include is checked at the directory that would hold it** — the ownership check, or that fails to parse is a hard refusal — otherwise a stray `chmod` silently drops half a configuration and the server comes up looking healthy. ([`config/optional-covers-absence-and-moves-the-check-to-the-directory`](rules/config.md#config-optional-covers-absence-and-moves-the-check-to-the-directory))
- **A secret directive has a `_file` sibling, exactly one of the pair is set, and the file's whole content is the value** — A directive the registry marks **secret** — `[db.<name>] password`, `[mail.<name>] password`, `[ldap.<name>] password`, `[http.client.proxy] password`, `[http] csrf_key` and `[cache.shared] password` — gains a `_file` s… ([`config/a-secret-is-a-file-whose-content-is-the-value`](rules/config.md#config-a-secret-is-a-file-whose-content-is-the-value))

## Packaging

- **A compiled unit is one immutable file whose address is its content and its environment** — The on-disk artifact cache is a fan-out directory of immutable files, one per compiled unit:… ([`packaging/an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-artifact-is-one-immutable-content-addressed-file))

- **A compiled-unit cache entry is read into memory, never mapped** — The compiled-unit cache is **read into memory**, never mapped. ([`packaging/the-artifact-cache-is-read-not-mapped`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-artifact-cache-is-read-not-mapped))
- **A warm hit skips codegen and nothing else, and it must beat the compile it replaces** — A warm hit parses, checks and lowers the same source in full; only the Cranelift walk and the pages it would have produced come off the disk instead. - **`nvs --help` opens with the README's own title and the version, commit and commit date of the build answering** — `nvs --help` opens with two lines and no third:… ([`packaging/the-banner-states-the-build`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-banner-states-the-build))
- **`nvs.exe` carries the logo as its icon and the manifest's facts as its version information, and a debug build carries its own icon** — `nvs.exe` is linked with an icon and with version information, so Explorer, the taskbar, Task Manager, a file's *Properties → Details* and the firewall prompt `nvs serve` raises all name the program as Novis and say whi… ([`packaging/the-windows-binary-says-what-it-is`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-windows-binary-says-what-it-is))
- **The third-party notice is generated from the dependency graph, fails closed, and is never written by hand** — Novis is MIT and links some eighty permissive components, every one of which conditions redistribution on reproducing something — MIT and BSD the copyright line and the license text, Apache-2.0 additionally its `NOTICE`… ([`packaging/the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-third-party-notice-is-generated-never-written-by-hand))
- **The notice and Novis's own license are compiled into the binary from the same tree** — `crates/nvs-cli/src/info.rs` embeds `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` and `LICENSE` with `include_str!`, so the notice and the binary it describes are produced from one tree in one compile and cannot drift. ([`packaging/the-notice-is-embedded-in-the-binary`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-notice-is-embedded-in-the-binary))
- **No flag on `nvs` is inherited from PHP; `-h` and `-V` are the Unix baseline and `-o` the only short flag Novis declares** — elsewhere buys a few users one familiar keystroke and charges every reader of `--help` for it afterwards. ([`packaging/the-cli-surface-is-novis-own`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-cli-surface-is-novis-own))
- **A doc comment clap renders is written for the person reading `--help`, and cites nothing they cannot open** — Every doc comment clap renders — a subcommand's, a nested subcommand's, an argument's — is text a person reads in `nvs --help`, and it is written for that person and nobody else. ([`packaging/help-text-speaks-to-its-reader`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-help-text-speaks-to-its-reader))
- **`nvs info` is the one call for build, host and licensing facts, and the one spelling of it** — "What is this binary, what is in it, and what may I do with it?" is one question asked by one person at one moment, so it is one call. ([`packaging/nvs-info-is-the-one-call`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nvs-info-is-the-one-call))
- **A package's name is its two-segment root namespace `Vendor\Package`, `acme/http` is that name lowercased, and the first publish under a vendor owns the vendor** — A package's name is its root namespace, which has exactly two segments, `Vendor\Package` — `Acme\Http` — and every file in the package declares that namespace or one under it (`packaging/a-package-file-stays-under-its-d… ([`packaging/a-package-name-is-vendor-slash-name`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-name-is-vendor-slash-name))
- **A package is an immutable source archive whose identity is its BLAKE3 digest** — A package's **identity is the BLAKE3 digest of its archive** — the hash the artifact cache already uses, so the toolchain carries no second one. ([`packaging/a-package-is-its-digest`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-is-its-digest))
- **`package.toml` is read by the `nvs pkg` commands, and the compiler reads its `[grants]` table and nothing else of the application's file** — `package.toml` is read by the `nvs pkg` commands, and the compiler reads **one table of the application's file, `[grants]`**, and nothing else of it. ([`packaging/package-toml-is-a-tool-input`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-package-toml-is-a-tool-input))
- **Every file in a package declares the package's namespace or one under it, or it does not compile** — Every file in a package declares the package's namespace, `Vendor\Package`, or one under it, and a file that declares anything else is a **compile error** naming the file, the namespace it declared and the package it ha… ([`packaging/a-package-file-stays-under-its-declared-prefix`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-file-stays-under-its-declared-prefix))
- **A fetched package is reached by an ordinary `autoload` line in a committed, generated `vendor/packages.nvs`** — `nvs pkg fetch` materialises the graph under `vendor/` and writes **one generated Novis source file**, `vendor/packages.nvs`, containing nothing but ordinary declarations:… ([`packaging/a-fetched-package-is-an-autoload-line`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-fetched-package-is-an-autoload-line))
- **Nothing in a package runs before your program does** — no point in the fetch, resolve, verify or compile pipeline at which a package's code executes. ([`packaging/nothing-runs-before-the-program`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nothing-runs-before-the-program))
- **A package ships no `nvs.toml`, and none of its `require` or `autoload` paths reaches outside its own directory** — Two things a package may not do to the tree it lands in. ([`packaging/a-package-cannot-reach-its-host`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-cannot-reach-its-host))
- **From `0.1.0` on, a minor or patch release never breaks the public API of the release before it, and `nvs` checks that at publish without running code** — A package version is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, read literally, and from `0.1.0` onward a minor or patch release never breaks the public API of the release before it. ([`packaging/only-a-major-may-break-the-api`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-only-a-major-may-break-the-api))
- **Resolution selects the highest minimum any package asked for, across majors, never a pending version, and nothing upgrades itself** — Every dependency names the **minimum version** it needs, and the version selected for a package is the… ([`packaging/resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-resolution-takes-the-highest-minimum))
- **`package.lock` records every package's digest, a mismatch is a hard error, and `--locked` fetches nothing the lock does not name** — selected version, source and digest, and with the requested capabilities, repository, commit and owners that `nvs pkg update` compares against (`packaging/a-vendor-resolves-from-one-registry`). ([`packaging/the-lockfile-holds-every-digest`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-lockfile-holds-every-digest))
- **Each vendor resolves from exactly one registry set in `package.toml`, by default `https://registry.novis-lang.org`, and never from the first registry that has the name** — Each vendor resolves from exactly one registry, set in `package.toml`, and every vendor not named there resolves from `https://registry.novis-lang.org`. ([`packaging/a-vendor-resolves-from-one-registry`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-vendor-resolves-from-one-registry))
- **A git dependency pins an exact commit, and only the root application may declare one** — A git dependency pins an exact commit, and only the root application may declare one. ([`packaging/a-git-dependency-is-root-only`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-git-dependency-is-root-only))
- **The registry service and website are the Novis application `apps/registry/`, and its byte work is the same Rust the client runs, in `nvs` subcommands** — The registry service and its website are a Novis web application in this repository, `apps/registry/`, and the byte-level work it needs is Rust in `nvs` subcommands the service runs — the same code the client runs. ([`packaging/the-registry-is-a-novis-program`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-registry-is-a-novis-program))
- **The registry's hosting is one settings file: stores, file hosts, backup and download logs, with a publish durable on every store before it is visible** — The registry's hosting is configuration. ([`packaging/registry-hosting-is-configuration`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-registry-hosting-is-configuration))
- **A registry account is passkeys and one-time recovery codes, with no email, no SMS, no password, no forge binding and no human recovery** — A registry account is one or more passkeys and a set of one-time recovery codes shown once at sign-up, with **no email, no SMS and no password**, and it is bound to no forge. ([`packaging/a-registry-account-is-a-passkey`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-registry-account-is-a-passkey))
- **An account that shows no passkey sign-in or reminder answer for 60 fixed days can no longer publish, and token use never counts** — An account must show activity within 60 days, or it can no longer publish; **token use never counts as activity**. ([`packaging/an-account-stays-active-by-proof-not-by-token`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-account-stays-active-by-proof-not-by-token))
- **Every owner is notified of each publish, token, owner change, unlist and retraction through Web Push or a webhook they verified, and an account with no verified channel cannot publish** — Every owner is notified of each publish, new token, owner change, unlist and retraction through the channels that owner set up — **Web Push** and **webhooks** — and an account with no verified channel cannot publish and… ([`packaging/an-owner-is-notified-without-email`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-owner-is-notified-without-email))
- **A publish token is scoped to one vendor or package, expires within a year, starts with `nvsreg_`, and is stored only as a hash** — Publishing uses a token scoped to one vendor or one package, which expires after one year at most, starts with `nvsreg_`, and is stored by the registry only as a hash. ([`packaging/a-publish-token-is-scoped-and-expires`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-publish-token-is-scoped-and-expires))
- **The registry builds each archive itself from a public git commit as a deterministic uncompressed tar, and `nvs pkg publish` uploads no file** — The registry builds every archive itself from a git commit: `nvs pkg publish` sends a repository URL, a commit, a version and the package's directory within the repository, and uploads no file. ([`packaging/the-registry-builds-the-archive-from-git`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-registry-builds-the-archive-from-git))
- **A package archive carries its `src/` source, `package.toml`, its license and readme, and the files `files` names, within 16 MiB and 5,000 files whose paths work on every platform, and the package reads them without a grant** — A package archive carries every `.nvs` file under `src/`, `package.toml`, the license and readme files at the package root, and exactly the files `package.toml`'s `files` list names, and nothing else. ([`packaging/a-package-carries-only-its-source-and-what-it-lists`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-package-carries-only-its-source-and-what-it-lists))
- **A file too large for a package is a `[[download]]` entry pinned by HTTPS URLs, SHA-256 and size, which the fetch downloads, checks and places without running or unpacking anything** — A package names each file too large for its archive in a `[[download]]` table of its `package.toml`, pinned by HTTPS URLs, a SHA-256 hash and a size, and `nvs pkg fetch` downloads it, checks it and places it at its path… ([`packaging/an-external-file-is-pinned-by-url-sha256-and-size`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-external-file-is-pinned-by-url-sha256-and-size))
- **`nvs pkg publish` names a commit, the registry refuses what the package may not carry, and it never overwrites a published `name@version`** — `nvs pkg publish` names a repository, a commit and a version, and the registry never overwrites a published `name@version`. ([`packaging/publishing-never-overwrites`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-publishing-never-overwrites))
- **A release published with a token alone is pending for seven fixed days, fetchable by exact version and never selected, unless an owner confirms it with a passkey** — A release published with a token alone is **pending for seven days**, and an owner's passkey confirmation on the website releases it at once. ([`packaging/a-release-waits-seven-days-unless-an-owner-confirms`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-release-waits-seven-days-unless-an-owner-confirms))
- **The registry keeps an append-only C2SP transparency log of every event it acts on, and a client verifies inclusion and consistency before using an archive** — The registry keeps an **append-only transparency log** in the C2SP formats — tlog-tiles, with checkpoints as signed notes under an Ed25519 key — and a client verifies an archive's inclusion and the log's consistency wit… ([`packaging/the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-registry-keeps-an-append-only-log))
- **An owner may unlist a package or a version with a passkey, which hides it from search and keeps it fetchable, logged and reversible** — An owner may **unlist** a package or one version with a passkey: it is hidden from search and listings, its page says it is unlisted, and it stays fetchable. ([`packaging/an-owner-may-unlist`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-owner-may-unlist))
- **A known-bad version is retracted, never deleted, a token-sent retraction waits seven days, and `nvs pkg audit` names the minimum bump that clears it** — An owner marks a known-bad version **retracted** with a reason and a fixed-in version, and the bytes stay fetchable forever. ([`packaging/a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-known-bad-version-is-retracted-not-deleted))
- **The registry's operator may only withhold a version's bytes, for malware or a legal order, as a signed and logged advisory, and never deletes, edits or reassigns** — The registry's operator may only **withhold** a version's bytes, for malware or a legal order, and always as a signed, logged advisory that states its reason. ([`packaging/the-operator-only-withholds`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-operator-only-withholds))
- **Registry search sorts by the reader's choice, ranks only on facts the registry witnessed and on downloads, and counts downloads without storing an address** — The registry's search matches text, then sorts by an order the reader chooses: by default a mix of witnessed work and downloads, and also by date, by activity, by downloads or by name. ([`packaging/search-sorts-by-the-readers-choice`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-search-sorts-by-the-readers-choice))
- **Until 0.1.0 ships any dependency updates at any time, and the version contract starts with the commit that tags 0.1.0** — Two regimes, and the tree is in the first. ([`packaging/the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-version-contract-starts-at-0-1-0))
- **A version number describes the enumerated surface, and the Rust crate APIs, the artifact cache, diagnostic prose and MSRV carry no promise** — A version number is meaningless unless the thing it describes is listed. ([`packaging/the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-versioned-surface-is-enumerated))
- **One `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` for the whole workspace, and below 1.0 the breaking slot moves left** — `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, **one number for the whole workspace**, and the number `nvs --version` prints… ([`packaging/below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-below-1-0-the-breaking-slot-moves-left))
- **A change a dependency forced ships as a patch, a minor or a major by who can see it, never by how big the diff was** — One question classifies a change a dependency forced: **who can see it?** Not how big the diff was, not how many crates moved. ([`packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot))
- **A dependency break that a program author could see goes down a seven-step ladder, and shipping it is the last step** — A dependency change that would land in the last rows of `packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot` does not go there directly. ([`packaging/a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-dependency-break-is-absorbed-never-forwarded))
- **A forced user-facing break survives one minor release as a warning naming its replacement, and is removed in the next major** — Where a deprecation cycle is possible — meaning the old and new behaviour can coexist for one release — the old spelling survives one **minor** release emitting a **compiler warning that names its replacement**, and is… ([`packaging/a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-forced-break-is-announced-before-it-lands))
- **A dependency move never fixes a guard test by editing its threshold, and it regenerates the attribution file in the same commit** — The dependency sweep re-runs a battery whose full order and conditional legs are the sweep procedure's to state. ([`packaging/a-dependency-move-proves-two-things`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-dependency-move-proves-two-things))
- **Each dependency bump is its own commit, classified in its message** — Each dependency — or one coherent group that genuinely must move together, such as the `cranelift-*` crates — gets **its own commit**, with its classification from `packaging/who-can-see-it-decides-the-release-slot` in… ([`packaging/one-bump-one-commit`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-one-bump-one-commit))
- **Being current has a schedule, a stale dependency is a defect, and a human fires every pass — never an agent, cron or CI** — Being current is a standing obligation, so it has a schedule. ([`packaging/the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-sweep-is-fired-by-a-human))
- **A third-party extension is a sandboxed WebAssembly component, never a shared library loaded with `dlopen`** — Third-party code is added to a running Novis as a **WebAssembly component** — a `.nvsx` file — and never as a native shared library. ([`packaging/an-extension-is-a-sandboxed-wasm-component`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-extension-is-a-sandboxed-wasm-component))
- **The image, intl and PDF components are built into every `nvs` binary, sandboxed, and always present under `Novis\`** — The image, intl, PDF and spreadsheet components are `.nvsx` bytes embedded in every `nvs` binary and loaded before any `[[extension]]` entry. ([`packaging/the-first-party-components-are-built-in`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-first-party-components-are-built-in))
- **A built-in component's engine class is internal to its component, and a call to it from a program does not compile** — A built-in component's manifest class — `Novis\Image\Codec`, `Novis\Intl\Icu`, `Novis\Pdf\Engine`, `Novis\Spreadsheet\Engine` — is called only by that component's own Novis source. ([`packaging/a-components-engine-class-is-internal`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-components-engine-class-is-internal))
- **The prebuilt libwebp wasm library is committed beside its source hash, and CI rebuilds it and fails on a difference** — libwebp, the one C library inside a built-in component, is compiled with wasi-sdk by a `bun nv` tool into a wasm static library committed under `extensions/image/`, beside the hash of the source it was built from. ([`packaging/a-prebuilt-wasm-library-is-rebuilt-in-ci`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-prebuilt-wasm-library-is-rebuilt-in-ci))
- **A `.nvsx` is a single WebAssembly component whose manifest is an `nvs.manifest` custom section** — A `.nvsx` is **one file**: a WebAssembly component implementing the versioned world `nvs:ext@1.0.0`, with two custom sections inside it. ([`packaging/an-nvsx-is-one-file-carrying-its-manifest`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-nvsx-is-one-file-carrying-its-manifest))
- **An extension package may carry Novis source beside its `.nvsx`, under one namespace, and the component's manifest registers exactly one class** — An extension may carry **two payloads in its one file**: the wasm component, and Novis source that composes calls into it, in the `nvs.source` section (`packaging/an-nvsx-is-one-file-carrying-its-manifest`). ([`packaging/an-extension-package-carries-two-payloads`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-an-extension-package-carries-two-payloads))
- **An extension loads only from an `[[extension]]` entry in the root-owned `nvs.toml`, pinned by its `sha256`** — An extension is loaded from an `[[extension]]` entry in the root-owned `nvs.toml`, and from nowhere else, and every entry carries its pin:… ([`packaging/extension-loading-is-root-controlled`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-extension-loading-is-root-controlled))
- **An extension's classes are registered from its manifest at load, and a call into one is type-checked at compile time and emitted as a direct call** — At load the host reads an extension's manifest — its declared class, its `static` methods and `const` members — and registers the class into a layer of the compiler's signature table that the loaded set writes. ([`packaging/extension-calls-are-statically-typed`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-extension-calls-are-statically-typed))
- **A value crosses into an extension as the WIT type one closed table gives its Novis type, copied whole** — Every parameter and return of an extension's export has a Novis type, and one closed table gives its WIT type. ([`packaging/a-value-crosses-as-its-wit-type`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-value-crosses-as-its-wit-type))
- **A value crosses the guest boundary as a bounds-checked handle, never as a pointer** — Two values cross as handles. ([`packaging/values-cross-as-handles`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-values-cross-as-handles))
- **A guest is instantiated fresh for each request that calls it, so extension state cannot leak between requests** — Each request that calls an extension gets a **pristine instance** of it, created lazily on first use. ([`packaging/a-fresh-instance-per-request`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-fresh-instance-per-request))
- **A guest call runs on its request's core as an async call the request's coroutine polls, and yields at every epoch tick** — A guest call runs on the calling request's own core, as a wasmtime async call that the request's coroutine polls. ([`packaging/a-guest-call-yields-on-its-core`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-call-yields-on-its-core))
- **A guest runs under the request's CPU and memory caps, and a runaway guest traps rather than hanging a core** — Guest execution spends the calling request's own budget. ([`packaging/a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-runs-under-the-requests-budget))
- **A guest's error result throws its mapped class, a trap throws `ExtensionError`, and only a CPU or memory limit is a `FATAL`** — A guest's failure reaches the program in one of three ways, decided by what failed. ([`packaging/a-guest-crash-throws`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-crash-throws))
- **A guest has no ambient authority: WASI is not granted by default, and every host function it receives is capability-checked** — A guest links WASI with an **empty context**: no preopened directory, no network, no environment and no arguments; stdout and stderr go to the request log, the clocks are the request's clock, and random bytes come from… ([`packaging/a-guest-has-no-ambient-authority`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-guest-has-no-ambient-authority))
- **`nvs ext` creates, builds, inspects, tests, verifies and pins an extension, with Rust and C templates** — `nvs ext` is the one tool an extension author needs beyond their language's compiler:… ([`packaging/nvs-ext-is-the-authoring-tool`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-nvs-ext-is-the-authoring-tool))
- **An extension call costs a fixed ten-odd nanoseconds over a built-in call, so an extension's API is coarse-grained** — Measured in a release build: a host-to-guest call costs about 11.5 ns, a guest-to-host accessor call about 9 ns, a 1 KiB bulk copy into guest memory about 12 ns, and a fresh pooled instance plus one call about 8 µs. ([`packaging/the-boundary-is-the-cost`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-boundary-is-the-cost))
- **A C dependency is admitted under ordinary audit only if attacker-controlled data never reaches it; otherwise it needs an exceptional verification record or is confined to wasm** — "Pure Rust by default, deviations argued individually" is a standing test rather than a case-by-case argument, so the answer does not depend on who argues it. ([`packaging/a-c-dependency-answers-two-questions`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-c-dependency-answers-two-questions))
- **Somebody else's specification is implemented by an existing first-class crate, and the compiler and scheduler are written here** — Anything with an external specification — a protocol, a parser, a wire format, a cipher, a codec, a cron expression, a timezone database — is implemented by an existing first-class Rust crate. ([`packaging/somebody-elses-specification-is-a-crate`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-somebody-elses-specification-is-a-crate))
- **Rasterising a PDF page is a decode-only format of `Novis\Image`, and never a member of `Novis\Pdf`** — PDF is on the image component's format roster **decode only**, beside SVG, as `Format`'s `Pdf` case with no entry point of its own: a page opens through the same plan/terminal shape and the same closed set of exports as… ([`packaging/pdf-decoding-ships-in-the-image-package`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-pdf-decoding-ships-in-the-image-package))
- **`nvs service` is a namespace, and everything after a mandatory `--` is stored verbatim as the argv the service runs** — A service is this binary, registered with the platform's service manager, running **one stored argv**. ([`packaging/a-service-is-one-stored-argv`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-service-is-one-stored-argv))
- **The service installer fails closed: a closed `serve`/`run` allowlist, no relative path, no password on a command line, and an argv without `--config` stores the data folder's `nvs.toml`** — The trailing argv is the sharpest sink in the project (`security/sink-predicate`): the command runs elevated, and what it stores is executed by a privileged account at every boot until somebody removes it. ([`packaging/the-installer-is-a-sink`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-installer-is-a-sink))
- **On Windows the argv is encoded into the SCM's one `ImagePath` string, the binary path is always quoted, and nothing else holds it** — The Windows SCM stores **one string**, and the process gets it back through `CommandLineToArgvW`. ([`packaging/the-argv-lives-in-imagepath`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-argv-lives-in-imagepath))
- **A service's default identity is the local system account, and `--account` names any other, the per-service virtual account included** — The default identity is `LocalSystem`, the local system account every hand-registered Windows service gets, so an operator who installs with no `--account` sees the same log-on tab `sc create` gives them. ([`packaging/a-service-runs-as-a-virtual-account`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-service-runs-as-a-virtual-account))
- **A stop drains, no control reloads, and the process's console and its lifecycle records go to the event log** — A hosted server answers its service manager with the operations it already has, rather than a shim reporting what it can see from outside:… ([`packaging/a-service-answers-its-manager`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-service-answers-its-manager))
- **On Linux `nvs service unit` prints the systemd unit and touches nothing; writing it is an explicit `--install`** — `nvs service unit <name> -- serve --config …` writes a systemd unit to stdout and touches nothing. ([`packaging/the-unit-is-printed-and-install-is-the-opt-in`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-unit-is-printed-and-install-is-the-opt-in))
- **The generated unit carries the hardening block, `ReadWritePaths` on exactly the install's write grants, `Type=notify`, `MemoryMax` from `[limits]`, and a socket unit for a privileged port, so the service holds no capability** — The generated unit carries what a hand-written one usually does not:… ([`packaging/the-generated-unit-is-hardened`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-the-generated-unit-is-hardened))
- **A single-file bundle may not install itself as a service** — `nvs service install` refuses when the running binary is a single-file bundle, with a diagnostic (`E0634`) naming the reason. ([`packaging/a-bundle-may-not-install-itself`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-bundle-may-not-install-itself))
- **There is no `Core\Service`: only an operator installs a service, from the command line, and nothing about it is on the request path** — There is no `Core\Service`, no new grammar, no runtime change and nothing on the request path. ([`packaging/a-service-is-operator-surface`](rules/packaging.md#packaging-a-service-is-operator-surface))
